News.title: Meghan ‘wanted to speak out’ about dad Thomas Markle child sex abuse claims but royal bodyguard ‘warned her against it’
News.content:
Next

MEGHAN Markle reportedly wanted to speak out about child sex abuse allegations against her dad but was “warned against it” by a royal bodyguard, it is claimed.

The Duchess of Sussex, 45, previously revealed that the allegations against Thomas Markle Snr, 82, were passed to her in a letter back in 2019.



The revelation has seen the Met Police come under scrutiny for failing to investigate the child sex claims made by Markle Snr’s first wife Roslyn Loveless.

The Sun previously reported in a world exclusive how cops in the Philippines are investigating Meghan’s dad over boxes of sick material containing a child abuse video and child sex images.



Loveless, who died in 2024, specifically alleges that Markle had sex with a child in the US and regularly travelled to the Philippines and Thailand because he claimed that “12-year-olds are legal there”.

Now, it has been claimed that Meghan wanted to speak out about the allegations in the letter, according to The Times.

However, the outlet reports that one of her Royalty and Specialist Protection [RaSP] bodyguards allegedly told her: “Leave it with us, we’ll investigate it.”

The same officer reportedly advised Meghan not to go public at a time she was being criticised for cutting ties with her father – who did not attend the Sussexes’ wedding in 2018 – without any explanation.

The Met, who did not investigate any of the allegations against Markle Snr due to them taking place abroad, are still trying to identify and find the officer in question, The Times reports.

Meghan had also said she was “concerned” no action had been taken by Scotland Yard to alert other authorities after passing her the letter.



Thomas Snr is currently being investigated over a huge stash of child sex images after being reported to police by his own son.

Markle Snr denies all of the allegations, which he’s publicly branded as “sick lies”.

He is said to be in a Florida nursing home and could face questioning by the FBI.



Thomas Junior – Meghan’s half-brother – told The Sun how he stumbled upon a child abuse video on a phone among his father’s abandoned possessions and reported it to cops.

We reported on the full inventory of surrendered computers, DVDs, mobile phones, video tapes, film negatives, memory data cards, books and pictures in a world exclusive.

This included photos allegedly showing Thomas Snr in his 40s or 50s with a young girl in what appears to be a hotel room, and another showing her naked.

The window fitter became his father’s full-time carer after he suffered a stroke in 2022 and moved to Mexico to support him.

The pair relocated to Cebu City in the Philippines in January 2025 before a life-threatening blood clot led to the amputation of award-winning lighting technician Markle Snr’s left leg.



He was forced to return for treatment in the US, leaving behind a large collection of belongings where his son claims to have found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child abuse images.

Meghan’s father lived in the city of Rosarito at the time the hard drives were allegedly loaded with content.

Cops in the Philippines were also granted a warrant earlier this week to search Thomas Snr’s computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes.

Markle Snr’s belongings — itemised in 80 categories on a police inventory list — are being combed through by Cebu’s Regional Anti Cybercrime Unit 7.

A second stash found in a storage unit near Markle Snr’s former home in Rosarito, Mexico, is said to include similarly horrific material.

Meghan, 45, told her dad it would be the last time he ever heard from her — and that she would never allow him to meet his grandchildren – in a letter last year.

He received the letter while in hospital in the Philippines after his leg was amputated in December 2025.

News.title: RAF drones monitor Russian ships in English Channel for first time – after Vlad ‘sends fishing boats to spy on Britain’
News.content:
Next

RAF drones are now actively policing British waters to track Russian naval fleets for the very first time, it emerged last night.

The unprecedented move comes after fears Vladimir Putin and the Kremlin are ramping up sabotage operations in Europe and preparing for a conflict with the UK and other NATO allies.



Now, the Ministry of Defence have confirmed that an unarmed British Protector RG1 drone was recently deployed above the English Channel to shadow a Russian warship.

Operating between late September and mid-October alongside Royal Navy warships and helicopters, the aircraft delivered more than ten hours of “intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance coverage”.



The state-of-the-art surveillance craft is one of 16 unmanned models ordered by the RAF, with 11 currently operational in the fleet.

Wes Streeting, the Defence Secretary, said: “Our Armed Forces work together every day, around the clock, to keep our country safe and safeguard our national interests.

“For the first time, Protector has joined Royal Navy warships and helicopters monitoring activity around our shores, demonstrating how we are constantly innovating to monitor and deter threats and irresponsible provocation.”

It comes amid mounting criticism over Labour’s defence budgets and growing fears that funding gaps could leave the nation vulnerable to Moscow’s aggression.

But officials confirmed that the Royal Navy has ramped up its anti-Russian monitoring operations by 25 per cent in the first seven months of this year, compared to the same timeframe in 2025.

Suspicious Russian vessels have also been detected looming near Britain’s vital underwater cable networks.



In direct response to this threat, the MoD is injecting an additional £330million into seabed surveillance and next-generation anti-submarine warfare capabilities over the coming four years.

Intelligence chiefs fear Britain is high on the Kremlin’s target list as Putin seeks revenge for our unwavering support of Ukraine.

Moscow’s forces have already successfully landed rogue drones inside the borders of Poland, Moldova, Lithuania, Norway and Denmark.



Reflecting on the mission, Wg Cdr Sam Haley, officer commanding XIII Squadron, said: “Protector’s first operational sorties in UK airspace demonstrate the significant value this capability brings to UK defence.

“Working alongside Royal Navy vessels, it provided persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance coverage, highlighting its ability to operate seamlessly across military and civilian airspace in support of maritime security, Nato commitments and wider UK tasking.”

It comes after it was reported that Vladimir Putin is deploying fishing trawlers to spy on the UK’s critical undersea cables.

The bombshell revelation has sparked fears the Russian tyrant is mapping out Britain’s critical infrastructure to prepare for future attacks.

Nato has been tracking civilian vessels loitering in waters around Britain as they carry out espionage for the Kremlin, The Telegraph reported.



The outlet has analysed more than 500 cases of Russian trawlers lurking above vital communication cables linking the UK with Europe and the US.

Others have followed the cable routes – carrying billions of pounds of economic activity – for miles across the ocean.

Ministers have confirmed that Moscow is using “commercial proxies” to threaten the deep sea infrastructure.

Europe has been on high alert for months after increasingly daring Russian underwater sabotage plots.

British forces caught Russian subs training a secret weapon designed to disable critical undersea cables without leaving a trace this Spring.



It comes amid a warning by Defence Secretary Wes Streeting that the country must be ready for war in 1,000 days.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And during his maiden Budget, John Healey announced his intention to increase defence spending to 3 per cent of GDP by 2030.

However, the path to do this will be outlined in the next Spending Review.

News.title: Homes evacuated after ‘explosive’ discovered in car on residential street – as bomb squad deployed & cops launch probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'BOMB' SHOCK Homes evacuated after ‘explosive’ discovered in car on residential street – as bomb squad deployed & cops launch probe







Next

BOMB squad officers were scrambled after a suspected explosive device was found in a car parked on a quiet residential street.

Residents were evacuated from their homes as officers sealed off the area and called in specialist explosives experts.

The device was discovered in a vehicle on Sherwood Avenue, in Poole, Dorset, at around 10.20pm on Friday.

An Explosive Ordnance Disposal team was sent to the scene and worked overnight to make the suspected bomb safe.





Cops put a cordon in place while properties in the immediate vicinity were immediately evacuated.

No arrests have been made and officers are continuing to investigate.

Officers initially attended a property in the road following reports that a parked car nearby contained “offensive weapons and other suspicious items”.

There was also a police presence in Park Homer Drive, in Wimborne, which officers confirmed was connected to the incident in Poole.



One resident told the BBC they had seen armed officers and sniffer dogs in the area.

The force has not yet revealed what the suspected explosive device.

It is not clear whether anyone is being sought in connection with the shocking discovery.

News.title: US Embassy issues urgent alert over ‘threat of mass casualty event’ & warns citizens to avoid Russian museum
News.content:
Next

THE US and Canada have warned of “a credible threat of a mass casualty event” in Moscow.

People have been told to “avoid the area” around the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve – located a few miles from the Kremlin – where an attack was due to take place on Saturday.



It said: “The US Embassy in Moscow is aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1.”

The US government added that it was “coordinating with the appropriate Russian authorities on a response.”



Separately, Russia‘s security services (FSB) said it had received information from ⁠the US through established partner channels about preparations for a terrorist attack in the capital.

Neither the US nor Russia elaborated about who might have made the threat – but so far, no reports of an attack have been made.

Footage circulating on Telegram showed police arriving at the scene of the museum and shutting the entrance.

Officers also blocked the roads leading to the museum.

“We don’t know what’s going to happen; we were just told to close the park for technical reasons,” security personnel at the site told Russian media.

In early March 2024, the US Embassy issued a similar terrorist threat alert for Moscow.



It recommended avoiding mass events on March 7 and for 48 hours after.

No incidents happened, but on March 22, a terrorist attack took place at the Crocus City Hall entertainment centre, killing 151 people and injuring 609.

The warnings come just days before Russia, Ukraine and the US are set to resume trilateral talks over the course of the war.



Negotiating teams are prepared to leave for Abu Dhabi to explore the potential for a peace agreement.

The meeting is scheduled for November 10.

Earlier this week, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri ‌Ushakov said the talks will depend on “the situation on the battlefield“.

“You can see the situation now ​in the Middle East. It just doesn’t allow us to hold it in the near future. That’s my assumption,” he told journalists.

Ushakov also said there had been no discussion of having European negotiators in ​attendance at the next round of talks.



The leaders of Britain, Germany and France said last weekend ‌that ⁠Europe would play a role in US-mediated talks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“There is absolutely no talk about this, nothing being considered,” Ushakov was quoted as saying.

“What there is now is an agreement on resuming ​three-sided consultations with representatives ​of Russia, Ukraine ⁠and the US.”

News.title: Forget slavery apology, the honest conversation Andy Burnham needs is to get serious on the UK’s economy
News.content:
Next

EVERY time Andy Burnham starts one of his “open conversations” the bills start piling up for Britain.

First it was his warm words about realigning with the EU. Now he is open to a formal apology for the slave trade.



Tony Blair has already expressed Britain’s regret for the horrors of slavery and more than $100billion in debts were written off for the countries affected.

So what does our foot-in-mouth PM think he’s achieving by this half-baked virtue-signalling?



Does he naively believe a formal statement will end calls for financial reparations that could run into trillions?

Because the opposite is true. It would only inspire a new chorus of financial demands from cash-hungry Caribbean governments, armies of lawyers and massed ranks of bleeding heart campaigners.



When the Dutch government apologised for slavery, it was forced to set up a 200million euros fund for payments.

Britain would be hit by demands for billions more just as a start.

It is the last thing this country needs after Burnham’s pitiful failure to address our grotesque debts and vast overspending in last week’s Budget.

A shocking 60 per cent of Brits in our poll think he is just tinkering while the economy burns.



Astonishingly, nearly two-thirds of the country believe Britain would not be resilient to a military attack due to the parlous state of our defences.

But what is truly galling is Burnham’s claim that he is being honest with voters.

Is it honest to say you want to bring down the ruinous benefits budget when you don’t have a plan to do so?

We are on course to blow £430BILLION a year on welfare by 2031 but the PM is more interested in delivering his grand vision than tackling it.

Next month he will set out his monumental Ten-Year Plan.



Expect to hear more about constitutional reform, devolution, an extension of public ownership and a social care revolution.

Who will pay for it is quite another matter. But this is politics, not business, so as usual it will be someone else’s money.

Why not admit you are going to tax everyone to death in order to do it, PM?

Now that, at least, would be an honest conversation.

Taking the PG Tips

WHILE the PM shows no sign of curbing spending, leftie councils are also doing their best to waste taxpayer cash.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Lewisham’s spree involves £50,000 in awards for activities such as tea drinking lessons for asylum seekers.

Somebody should tell them there’s not an endless pot.

News.title: Moment mass brawl erupts in Armenian parliament over ‘Ministry of Sex’ row – as MPs hurl chairs & launch punches
News.content:
Next

THIS is the wild moment a mass brawl erupts inside Armenia’s parliament as rival MPs clash over a “Ministry of Sex” row.

Shocking footage shows furious ministers throwing punches and hurling chairs over potty plans to tackle declining sex drives in women.



At one point a politician empties a glass of water over another’s head while his esteemed colleagues kick one another in the groin.

The violent brawl on Thursday – the third in a matter of days – was sparked by a bizarre proposal from the opposition party.



Ministers from the pro-Russia Strong Armenia party suggested creating a Ministry of Sex after claiming that a lack of sexual satisfaction was leading women into political activism.

The ruling party, Civil Contract, immediately shut down the raunchy department plans – which had aimed to leave “no unsatisfied women”.

Tempers boiled over when a ruling party MP demanded an apology – a command which was met by an all-out fisticuffs frenzy.

Rival MPs rushed up to the podium where Civil Contract MP Taron Chakhoyan was speaking and began pummelling one another.

One man can be seen slipping off his blazer and elegantly draping it over a wooden bannister before leaping into the fray.

MP Taron Chakhoyan had blasted the opposition as being “steeped in corruption” before making personal digs at one minister’s alleged nepotism.



Launching into an impassioned tirade, the Civil Contract member said: “Mr Karapetyan, it is not my fault that your entire extended family is involved in politics, including your uncle, your father, and your cousin, who even tried to open a ministry in our country.

“It is not my fault that he wanted to open a ministry that would satisfy all women. You have still not apologised to women for that.”

Strong Armenia MP Narek Karapetyan clapped back and reportedly called Chakhoyan a “mess from head to toe”.



Vahagn Aleksanyan, the parliament’s deputy speaker, threw a red leather chair while Chakhoyan was seen pouring a glass of water over Garnik Davtyan, an opposition MP, according to The Telegraph.

Armenia’s prime minister Nikol Pashinyan later told reporters: “I condemn violence, but I support the measures taken by the Civil Contract faction today.

“Whether with a chair or something else, it is proportionate and right.”

He later joked on Facebook that despite being called “Strong Armenia” the party’s MPs were not “physically strong”.

Opposition MP Karapetyan also defended the parliamentary brawl, calling it a “normal Armenian-style man-to-man fight”.



He added: “People who had been getting on our nerves for months got it right in the mouth – and got it good.”

The parliamentary speaker did not initially stop the fight so that “everyone could see all of this”.

But when the violence spiralled out of control he quickly called for recess – a command which appeared to have been ignored.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fighting allegedly continued along the corridors – with politicians emerging from the chambers with torn clothes and injuries.

The prosecutor’s office told local media there was “no information available” about any criminal proceedings following the fight.

News.title: Man in his 20s suffers life-changing injuries after being stabbed in Tesco car park – as cops hunt three ‘attackers’
News.content:
STABBING HORROR Man in his 20s suffers life-changing injuries after being stabbed in Tesco car park – as cops hunt three ‘attackers’







Next

A MAN in his 20s has been rushed to hospital with potentially life-changing injuries after a horror stabbing near a Tesco car park.

The victim was attacked shortly before 2pm yesterday near the car park of Tesco Extra in Trowbridge, Wiltshire.

Cops say the three suspects fled the scene following the savage incident, and a manhunt to locate them is continuing.

The man was rushed to hospital, where he is being treated for potentially life-changing injuries.





Officers are appealing for witnesses and anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage to come forward.

The force says an increased police presence is in the area as cops continue their enquiries.

Detective Sergeant Jonathan Dean, from Central CID, said: “We appreciate the concern this incident may cause, however please be reassured that we do not believe there to be a wider risk to the public.

“While we are carrying out enquiries, I’d ask anyone who may be able to help to get in touch.

“If you witnessed the incident, or believe you may have seen the suspects before or after the incident, or have any CCTV or dashcam footage then please come forward.”

He added: “If you have any concerns then please don’t hesitate to speak to one of our officers.”

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting log number 154 of October 31.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or through its website.

News.title: Criminal who killed mum in horror crash fails to dodge deportation despite claiming he’d be persecuted as a witch
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

STAY BID FAILS Criminal who killed mum in horror crash fails to dodge deportation despite claiming he’d be persecuted as a witch

Credit: Stephen Armstrong







Next

A CRIMINAL who killed a mum in a car crash failed to dodge deportation despite claiming he’d be persecuted as a witch.

The 33-year-old, known only as TM for legal reasons, arrived here from Zimbabwe in 2003.

He was convicted of GBH, burglary and drugs — then of causing death by dangerous driving.

TM was jailed for eight years in 2019 and ordered to be deported in 2023.





He appealed saying he would be persecuted as a witch in Zimbabwe due to learning disabilities and poor mental health.

But the Immigration Court in Bradford heard he had held down jobs, had no problems with literacy or numeracy, and had no mental health problems.

The judge dismissed his appeal.

Earlier in the month, The Sun revealed how Britain’s courts were being swamped by suspicious asylum appeals from migrants who claimed to be gay or atheist.



The creaking legal system — which is already facing huge backlogs — has seen a sharp increase in preposterous applications by chancers.

A growing number of asylum seekers are using their native country’s intolerance of homosexuality as a legal weapon.

Recent crazy cases include a former Namibian professional footballer who claimed to be bisexual.

In another farce, a Pakistani student announced on the morning of his tribunal that he was gay.

News.title: Government introduces 'tough new rules' on November 1 for thousands of dog owners
News.content:
Government introduces 'tough new rules' on November 1 for thousands of dog owners

Breaching the new rules could lead to up to six months in prison and unlimited fines

View 3 Images The new rule kicks in on November 1

Dog owners not following a 'tough' law change from today (November 1) will face 'legal consequences', the Government has announced. It is thought that the change in the law will affect thousands of dog owners across the UK.

‌



‌



It relates to how dangerous dogs are kept at home - in particular, XL Bullies. Currently, the XL Bully is one of five breeds banned in the UK, with the others being the Pit Bull Terrier, the Japanese Tosa, the Dogo Argentino, and the Fila Brasileiro.

‌



You are only allowed to keep a banned dog if you have a valid Certificate of Exemption and the dog is not acting dangerously. In January 2024, it became illegal to sell, give away, or abandon an XL Bully, and it became illegal to own one without a valid certificate two months later. It is thought around 61,000 were issued.

‌



The Government website says that your dog must be neutered, microchipped, kept on a lead and muzzle in public, and kept in a secure environment so it can't escape.

Vet urges dog owners to use 1 item of clothing to calm pets on Bonfire Night READ MORE :

XL Bully 'exemption' change update as Defra issues statement READ MORE :

The owner must also:

be aged over 16

show the Certificate of Exemption when asked by a police officer or council dog warden, either at the time or within 5 days

let the Index of Exempted Dogs know if you change address, or your dog dies

‌



Being a banned breed, it is illegal to:

sell a banned dog

abandon a banned dog

give away a banned dog

breed from a banned dog

‌



View 3 Images XL Bullies were banned in 2024

Law change

From today (Sunday, November 1) the law has changed. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) says: From 1 November 2026, you must not leave a child under 12 in close contact with a banned dog in a private place (for example a home or garden), without adult supervision."

‌



A Defra statement said: "Children will be better protected from dangerous dogs in the home under a new government measure coming into force today (November 1) to strengthen safeguards around banned breeds, including XL Bully types.

"From today, owners must not leave a child under the age of 12 in close proximity to a banned breed dog in a domestic setting or other private settings without adult supervision.

‌



"The new safeguard will reduce the risk of serious injury to children in domestic environments, while allowing exempted dogs to remain with families where appropriate supervision is in place.

"Owners of banned breeds who do not comply with this new measure could have their dogs seized, face up to six months in prison, and an unlimited fine. This new condition will be applied to Certificates of Exemption, which allow owners to legally keep a banned breed such as XL Bullies.

‌



"Any attack on a child by any dog is unacceptable. Under existing legislation, owners can face enforcement action, including up to 14 years in prison."

View 3 Images Protest against the UK Government's ban were held (Image: Getty)

‌



Legal consequences

Dame Angela Eagle, Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, said: "No child should ever have to suffer the trauma of a dog attack, and these tough new rules will help protect them from these horrific incidents.

“While many owners are acting responsibly, those that don’t will face the legal consequences of leaving a child alone with a banned breed – including up to six months in prison and unlimited fines.

Article continues below

“This measure will help protect children from serious harm while ensuring responsible owners can continue to keep their dogs, provided the necessary safety measures are in place.”

News.title: King Charles under pressure after PM says he's 'open' to formal apology for slave trade
News.content:
The King is under increasing pressure after the Prime Minister said he is “open” to calls for Britain formally apologise for its role in the slave trade.

The monarch’s current tour of the Caribbean has been dominated by calls for him to apologise for the monarch’s association with slavery and pleas for reparations totalling billions to affected nations. Buckingham Palace has consistently outlined that the King would not offer an apology, and would reiterate his previous statements expressing his deep sadness and sorrow on the issue.

Andy Burnham, who is due to attend the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm) in the Caribbean next week, alongside the King, on Friday expressed his personal “sorrow and regret” for the suffering caused by the transatlantic slave trade and said he wanted to offer a “structured dialogue” with those affected.

View 5 Images Charles is visiting the Caribbean region (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Kate releases sweet new photo of Prince Louis as a toddler crouching over a pumpkin for Halloween READ MORE :

But he went further than any of his predecessors, or the sovereign, has ever done before, saying: “Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them.”

On the first day of his nine-day tour of The Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, the King said “it is only right that we should acknowledge the great suffering of the past in these islands and beyond”. Yet, campaigners across the region were angered that he again failed to go further and issue an apology for the monarchy’s historic role in the brutal slave trade.

A spokesman for the King said: “As we have indicated, The King will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this Visit. You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond.”

View 5 Images Charles tour of the Caribbean has been described as the "most perilous" so far (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Buckingham Palace said the monarch would attend Chogm in his capacity as Head of the Commonwealth, adding: “It would not be appropriate for him to address matters of particular policy relating to the UK Government's position.”

The row comes after Prime Minister of The Bahamas, Philip Davis, said following the King’s visit earlier this week, that he “would be open” to losing Charles as the island’s head of state.

He also said that the call for reparations for slavery “is not absolutely money” and points to “acknowledgment, education, training, things of that nature”, pointing to the work the King's Foundation is engaged with, providing education grants across the Commonwealth as a potential vehicle.

However, leading historian Sir Anthony Seldonhas described Charles's Caribbean tour as "the most perilous" of his reign so far. He added: “His freedom is so constrained. He can be empathetic, he is very empathetic, he can say good words, but it's not open to him, it's not his right to be able to say that there will be an apology, it is (that of) the head of Government - the Prime Minister."

‌



Tory leader Kemi Badenoch on Saturday also criticised Andy Burnham's consideration of a formal apology, labelling it as a “navel-gazing distraction”. She added that slavery was “an evil in which people from every continent and region participated” and argued the Commonwealth should be “looking forwards, not backwards” at a summit in Antigua and Barbuda next week.

View 5 Images Charles is touring the Caribbean (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

She pointed to the intervention by Sir Tony Blair, who in 2006 expressed “deep sorrow and regret” over the UK's involvement in the slave trade but stopped short of a full apology, in arguing that Britain has already confronted its history.

In a lengthy post on social media, Mrs Badenoch said: "If Caribbean countries are asking Britain for a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade, will they also be asking the same of the descendants of African kingdoms, rulers and merchants who captured, sold and profited from the trade?"

‌



Royal sources indicated that the Prime Minister’s unprecedented statement was not delivered in conjunction with Buckingham Palace, stating that the royal household had been “informed in a timely manner” about his intentions. Before embarking on the tour, Buckingham Palace said the visit would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past”.

A spokesman for the King added that Charles would reflect on and renew his commitment to acknowledging “the wrongs of the past” and finding creative ways to “right inequalities that endure.” Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Mottley, who has sought reparations, welcomed Mr Burnham's statement, saying she would engage in good faith while still seeking reparatory justice.

View 5 Images Charles toured different locations in Guyana (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

Denis O'Brien, founder of The Repair Campaign, said Burnham's statement was disappointing and did not go far enough, adding: “”The British Government must stop obfuscating and give a full and formal apology now. This would be a significant and symbolic first step towards reparatory justice.”

‌



The Palace says apology and reparations are primarily matters for governments, leading the King walking a “diplomatic tightrope”. A spokesman added: “He is up for challenging visits with complex issues and relationships in play.

He sees it as his role to ‘bat for Britain’, the Realms and wider Commonwealth, promoting, protecting, and enhancing relationships at the highest level. “One of the many benefits of a Constitutional Monarchy is the ability to transcend politics.”

However, the Prime Minister ruled out considering financial reparations, saying he did "not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part."

News.title: Double-decker bus hits building in Derbyshire as several injured and cordon in place
News.content:
Double-decker bus hits building in Derbyshire as several injured and cordon in place

Several people have been injured after a double-decker bus collided with a building in New Mills, Derbyshire

View Image Emergency services rushed to a street in New Mills after a double decker Bee Network bus collided with a building (Image: ASP)

Several people have been injured after a double-decker bus collided with a building in Derbyshire.

‌



‌



The incident happened near the junction of Union Road, Market Street and St Mary's Road in New Mills at about 5.20pm today (Saturday). All three roads have since been closed. A cordon is in place around the scene due to concerns over a "potential gas leak", Derbyshire Police said.

‌



Police, fire and ambulance crews are attending the incident. Those injured are being treated at the scene and are not thought to have sustained life-threatening injuries, the force said.

Article continues below

The Manchester Evening News is reporting that it's understood that residents in the home above the building have been evacuated whilst emergency services await a structural engineer.

News.title: Celebrity Traitors LIVE: Maya Jama praised for incredibly generous move after the final
News.content:
The Celebrity Traitors have crowned their winners and even though Traitor Maya Jama was eliminated during the last round table, she has made a donation to her chosen charity

Maya Jama has been praised by fans after announcing she has donated to her chosen charity even if she didn't win The Celebrity Traitors.

Fans widely praised the broadcaster online, with one describing the donation as a "fabulous gesture" and someone else saying that despite being eliminated, Maya proved to be "the star of the show". One more said: "Well done Maya! You were a brilliant traitor."

The Faithfuls came away with the win, as actor Sebastian Croft and comedian Romesh Ranganathan triumphed after seeing off James Blunt, King Kenny and Leigh Anne Pinnock in the nerve-shredding End Game.

The duo took home £41,500 each for their chosen charities - Choose Love for Croft and the Refugee Council for Ranganathan.
