News.title: French police fire tear gas as more than 300,000 march across France in latest anti-government protests
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Police in Paris have fired tear gas during the latest anti-government protests in France as scuffles broke out on Halloween night.

More than 300,000 people across the country took to the streets to march in what authorities said were largely peaceful demonstrations on Saturday. But they said police had faced "a great deal of violence"and that officers were bracing for scattered unrest across the evening.

It is the third consecutive weekend of nationwide demonstrations, with authorities bracing for violence after nightfall. Demonstrations are also taking place in a number of cities in Germany, with marches turning violent and molotov cocktails being thrown at police in Frankfurt.

Around 70,000 police officers and gendarmes have been deployed across France, with Saturday’s marches pushed away from central boulevards to the outer fringes of major cities.

French interior minister Laurent Nuñez has warned of a “very high risk” of coordinated disorder, cautioning that Halloween will not be accepted as an excuse to wear masks or trigger street violence.

open image in gallery Protesters run amid tear gas, during a demonstration organised by labour unions in Paris ( Reuters )

The mobilisations follow two weekends of unrest that have seen widespread rioting, looting, arson, and mass arrests across the country.

At Porte de Bagnolet, on the eastern edge of Paris, several thousand people have gathered on Saturday afternoon behind a line of high school students leading the march hand in hand.

Stewards from the CGT union kept watch at the front of the procession, while riot police lined adjacent side streets.

Among those on the march was 21-year-old university student Corentin Cabreux, who said squalid conditions in student housing forced him to turn out.

open image in gallery A pyrotechnic explodes next to police officers in riot gear in the French capital ( Reuters )

“I live in a state-run student residence where there are damp stains all along the bottom of my walls, whole sections peeling off, cockroaches everywhere, rats,” he said.

Mr Cabreux added that he hoped the turnout would remain peaceful to counter government depictions of the movement as mere cover for rioting.

In recent weeks, police crowd-control tactics have drawn fierce criticism from trade unions and legal monitors following the repeated use of tear gas, water cannon and dispersion grenades.

open image in gallery Huge crowds turned out across France for the third weekend of demonstrations, including here in Marseille ( Reuters )

Anger mounted earlier this month after a 15-year-old student had their hand blown off after picking up an explosive stun grenade.

While France previously suspended the use of stun grenades for student rallies, Mr Nuñez confirmed that all intermediate crowd-control weapons remain authorised if officers face targeted assaults.

Mass protests in the country began last month when secondary school pupils walked out over staff shortages, deteriorating school buildings and a university admissions system seen as unfair to disadvantaged students. The movement has since widened into a broader challenge to Emmanuel Macron’s government, drawing in trade unions and left-wing groups opposing economic reforms.

In an effort to prevent a repeat of previous evening unrest, the president ordered marches kept out of central commercial districts.

In Paris, police have barred access to Place de la République and Les Halles between 23:00 and 06:00, while unaccompanied minors face a 21:00 curfew around the Champs-Élysées.

The unrest in France is part of a widening pattern of youth discontent across Europe.

open image in gallery A protester holds a smoke bomb with flames in the foreground during an anti-government demonstration in central Tirana, Albania ( AFP/Getty )

In Albania, violent clashes between young demonstrators and riot police have now entered their second week in the capital, Tirana, over soaring food prices, low wages and university fees.

On Friday, officers fired tear gas after government and education ministries were pelted with stones and pyrotechnics, leaving dozens detained and scores of protesters and police injured. There were further clashes in the country on Saturday.

In Italy, riot units remain on high alert across Milan, Turin and Bologna following recent clashes between student groups and law enforcement, with calls for fresh demonstrations circulating widely on TikTok over precarious job contracts and rising university costs.

In Germany, the youth campaign “Gen Z regelt” (“Gen Z’s got this”) has called for demonstrations across roughly 30 cities, demanding funding for education, healthcare and climate protection, while opposing any return to military conscription.

open image in gallery German protesters facing riot police during a demonstration organised by "GenZ regelt! ( AFP/Getty )

Berlin police are expecting around 10,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate, while luxury retailers along the Kurfürstendamm boulevard have boarded up display windows ahead of the evening.

In Spain, regional police in Catalonia have activated their highest emergency alert in Barcelona after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged fresh gatherings.

The alert follows rioting last Saturday that resulted in roughly 130 arrests, mostly of minors, prompting officers to seal off access routes to major commercial districts.

News.title: Rachel Reeves calls for UK to rejoin EU: ‘Brexit has made us poorer, weaker and less secure’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rachel Reeves has said she believes Britain should rejoin the European Union as she warned Brexit has made the country “poorer, weaker and less secure”.

The former chancellor voiced her support for Andy Burnham’s move to open the door to negotiations with Brussels as she said she “welcomed” his decision.

Writing in the Sunday Times, Ms Reeves said she accepted there was a “debate to be had” about the UK’s future in the EU, but that she believes the country’s future ultimately lies within the bloc.

open image in gallery Rachel Reeves has thrown her support behind moves to rejoin the EU ( Getty )

“I am proud of the progress we have already made in strengthening our relationship with the European Union,” she wrote. “Brexit has made us poorer, weaker and less secure. There is a debate to be had about our future relationship with Europe, and I welcome Andy Burnham’s leadership in facing up to this. No one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were.

“I do believe Britain’s future lies in the European Union. However, it is incumbent on supporters of our re-entry to make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right — especially ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month, where at a minimum we should be looking for confirmation of the ambitious youth mobility scheme negotiated earlier this year, and — I hope — progress towards entry into the SAFE defence partnership.”

The comments make Ms Reeves one of the most prominent Labour figures to speak out explicitly in support rejoining the EU, despite being part of a government that made a manifesto pledge not to reverse Brexit.

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham has said it is time for an ‘honest’ conversation about Brexit ( PA Wire )

Last week, Mr Burnham wrote in the Sunday Times he believes it is time for an “honest” conversation about the impact of Brexit on the country. He said he would reveal more about any potential proposals for closer EU ties around the time of the EU-UK summit on November 20, when a youth free-movement deal will be struck.

It comes after a major new poll shared exclusively with The Independent showed support for reversing Brexit has risen and opposition has fallen since Andy Burnham opened the door to Britain rejoining the EU.

The Ipsos survey found that 56 per cent of respondents now say they would vote in favour of becoming part of the EU again, up four percentage points on a similar poll in May.

At the same time, the number who back staying out has fallen three points to 30 per cent.

When the findings were filtered by those likely to vote in a future referendum, the result was 63-34, with 3 per cent saying they did not know.

The poll also revealed that 73 per cent of those aged under 35 want to rejoin the bloc, alongside 77 per cent of those who voted Labour at the last general election, 31 per cent of Tories and even 16 per cent of Reform voters.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton: First Ferrari pole reminds me of Michael Schumacher’s success
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lewis Hamilton says claiming a first pole for Ferrari evoked memories of watching Michael Schumacher dominating for the Scuderia.

The 41-year-old earned his first pole position in over three years, since the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023 – 1,197 days ago – in Mexico City.

Hamilton began this weekend by doubling down on his vow to be racing into the 2030s, declaring that Formula One has “never had anyone like me”.

Hamilton believes he is still matching the youngest drivers on the grid and showed all of his enduring quality to pip former Mercedes team-mate George Russell to pole by just 0.009 seconds.

open image in gallery Hamilton celebrates pole (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

“My first Ferrari pole, I mean jeez it takes me back to watching Michael (Schumacher) get all those poles for Ferrari and all those wins,” Hamilton, who has previously claimed sprint pole for the team, said.

“It is very, very special.”

The seven-time world champion became the oldest F1 pole-sitter since 42-year-old Mario Andretti in 1982.

His desire to race in Africa, with a race announced in Rwanda in the “early 2030s” has seen him vow to still be competing at the top level for years to come.

Hamilton remains mathematically in the title picture, 124 points adrift of leader Kimi Antonelli – who will secure his place as F1’s youngest world champion by finishing ninth or better on Sunday.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli is likely to be celebrating the championship on Sunday (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Antonelli is 21 years Hamilton’s junior. Asked how he is still delivering at 41, Hamilton said: “When there’s a will there’s a way!

“It’s all in the mind for all of us. You might feel aches and pains, luckily I don’t.

“That love is not gone. I wake up every day thinking about it, I dream about it.”

The British driver claimed his first win for Ferrari in Barcelona in June and is delighted to now have a pole to his name to repay the faith from the team.

“We just held on to that belief that one day we will get back on to the front row and P1,” Hamilton added.

“It was a really clean lap – I needed it because Charles was three tenths up the road. But I knew areas I could improve on.

“It’s just my belief in this team, the opportunity they have given me and the faith they have shown in me.”

Antonelli will start from fourth as he bids to celebrate the title with a fiesta on Sunday. The Italian was fifth fastest but gained a place due to a penalty for Max Verstappen.

open image in gallery Russell claimed second for Mercedes (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez features the longest run down to turn one on the F1 calendar and Hamilton will have Russell and team-mate Charles Leclerc – who starts third – filling his mirrors.

“It is a long way down to turn one – I don’t think I have ever been on pole here,” Hamilton said.

“I think the others have a new tyre for the start but to have pole here, it feels special to be here in Mexico and (pole position) 105, I like that number.”

News.title: FBI blames North Korea for stolen billions from Binance in biggest hack in history
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The theft of billions of dollars from Binance within a matter of minutes, the biggest crypto heist in history, was orchestrated by North Korean hackers, the FBI said Saturday.

The bureau said in a statement that this week's attack was tied to “malicious cyber activity” by an entity known as TraderTraitor, the same actors behind a $1.5 billion Bybit hack last year.

The FBI asked crypto exchanges, blockchain analytics companies and others to block transactions linked to various addresses to make sure the money is not laundered to cover up its origins.

It also said its probe found that TraderTraitor was converting stolen assets primarily into a cryptocurrency called ethereum. The FBI expects that TraderTraitor will now attempt to convert the assets using DeFi and “instant swap services.”

On Thursday, $6.3 billion in bitcoin and other digital currency was stolen from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, in what several crypto experts said bore the hallmarks of a North Korean hack.

The company said Saturday that it had enough set aside in the same digital currency that was stolen to cover 90% of the missing assets and promised that customers would be fully reimbursed.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton claims shock first Ferrari pole – and first in three years: ‘Lost for words’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari – and first in over three years – at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Saturday.

The 41-year-old, whose last pole came in Hungary in July 2023 with Mercedes, claimed top-spot by just 0.009 seconds to former teammate George Russell in second.

Kimi Antonelli, who is set to win the title on Sunday, will start in fourth alongside Charles Leclerc in third. Max Verstappen will start fifth, as a result of his one-place grid drop for a clash with Liam Lawson on Friday.

Yet Hamilton, who becomes the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti 44 years ago, was in a state of shock after a pole position which he admitted on team radio was “a long time coming.”

“Wow! That felt great, feels good!” Hamilton said. “So happy. I'm lost for words.

“It's been a challenging weekend, had an engine issue yesterday. We were on the back foot, but we did a good job with the set-up but it was so close between us all.

“To have pole here, don't know if I've had one here before! I think my first pole with Ferrari.”

Hamilton did record a pole position for the sprint race in China last year but had failed to claim P1 in qualifying since.

open image in gallery Hamilton finished just ahead of George Russell and Charles Leclerc ( PA )

He added: “Where there's a will, there's a way. It's all in the mind for all of us. I don’t have the pains other people have – I ice bath a lot – all those things you can do to keep yourself young and fit.

“But I love what I do, I dream about it.

“The support I have around the world, these guys keep me going. Hope I can do it for them tomorrow.”

Antonelli, meanwhile, needs to just finish ninth or higher to claim the world championship and become the youngest champion in the history of the sport.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes looks visibly emotional as he applauds fans after Man Utd’s defeat at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Next

BRUNO FERNANDES could barely fight back the tears after applauding the travelling Man United fans following their loss to Chelsea.

The Red Devils suffered a 2-0 defeat in west London to leave them winless in nine games and with boss Michael Carrick‘s job hanging on by a thread.



The United fans cheered Carrick as he departed Old Trafford following their loss to Bournemouth last week, but they intensely booed the players who followed him.

This time around, the fans were much warmer with the defeated players and Fernandes was visibly emotional during the exchange.



Of course, the Portuguese superstar has been at the centre of much of United’s hardships as of late.

Although he broke the Premier League assist record last season and was voted the PFA Men’s Player of the Year last season, he has not had the same influence this term.



He has three goals and one assist so far this campaign, but none of that has translated into results for Man United.

He was openly critical of Carrick and his tactics following their Champions League loss to Como, leading to the manager benching him for the next game.

He was back in the starting line-up for the clash at Stamford Bridge, but that failed to have the desired impact as well.

Fernandes has long been linked with a move away from the club with the playmaker going as far as to suggest the club wanted to cash-in on him with Saudi Arabia interested in the summer of 2025.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, he remains one of United’s superstar players, but is he a part of a locker room that doesn’t believe in Carrick’s skills?

Lisandro Martinez had an outburst himself after another Champions League loss for United, but he took aim at the board above Carrick rather than the management team.

The Argentine later retracted and apologised for his comments. He was also subsequently sent off against Chelsea.

But if this video proves anything, it’s that the club does mean something to Fernandes and the results are hurting him just as much as they are the fans.

Sports.title: Declan Rice to sign incredible £18million-a-year Arsenal deal… but will still be earning LESS than Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA has confirmed Declan Rice will become the latest Arsenal star to sign a new long-term deal.

Rice, 27, who faces Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, is out of contract at the end of next season.



But the midfielder has been in talks over a fresh deal which would see him on par with Bukayo Saka’s £350,000-a-week wages.

Boss Arteta said: “My feeling is that Declan is very happy here. Every conversation I have with him, he wants to continue here for the long term — and it will be a matter of time until we resolve that.”



England star Rice has become a key player for the Gunners since joining from West Ham for £105million in the summer of 2023.

And his new deal at the Emirates will see him land a big pay rise from his current £240,000-a-week salary.



In February, Gunners winger Saka signed a long-term contract to remain with the North Londoners until 2030.

And French centre-back William Saliba penned a new five-year agreement last September.

Only last month, it was announced that manager Arteta had also put pen to paper on a new deal until 2030, doubling his pay to a whopping £20m a year.

Arteta, 44, insisted he is happy with the performances of Rice — even though he has not always been at his best since returning from World Cup duty with the Three Lions.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Spaniard said: “He has been very consistent again. What we demand from him every year is very difficult to do, difficult to maintain.

“He is doing it and big credit to him. You have big players for the big matches.

“We know the kind of performance we want from Dec and the rest of the boys against Liverpool, to get away from there with three points.”



Arsenal, who sit second in the Premier League ahead of the Liverpool clash, have had some injury issues.

But Rice, left-back Riccardo Calafiori as well as wingers Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke — who did not feature in the shock Carabao Cup fourth-round loss to League Two outfit Fleetwood in midweek — have all trained ahead of the trip to Anfield.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 1 Fulham 1: Zion Suzuki makes huge blunder and John McGinn misses penalty as Emery train halted by Arbeola
Sports.content:
Next

ZION SUZUKI went from hero to zero — after a bizarre own goal from the Aston Villa keeper denied Unai Emery’s side victory.

Suzuki had pulled off a string of saves to cement his reputation as one of the signings of the summer.



However, it all went wrong for the Japan stopper after Nicolas Jackson had set up a potential third successive Premier League win for Villa with his eighth goal of the season.

Fulham always looked a threat, with Suzuki the man repeatedly standing in their way.



Villa supporters were already singing “The World’s No1” about the man who replaced Emi Martinez, now at Chelsea.

Then came the moment of madness that allowed Fulham to take a point — and even they could not have expected to be gifted such an equaliser.



Alex Iwobi swung in a 64th-minute corner which was aimed right on top of Suzuki.

In trying to keep it out, the keeper only managed to fumble the ball over the line.

And goalline technology confirmed the goal after Suzuki tried to scramble the ball clear.

Villa took the lead in the 39th minute with a superb Jackson goal following Johan Manzambi’s pinpoint pass.



Jackson powered his way past two defenders before fancy footwork gave him the space to score.

Villa now face Barcelona on Tuesday in their toughest test of the Champions League season so far.

But they will need to play better than this to get a result at the Nou Camp.

Skipper John McGinn’s missed penalty after 14 minutes also proved costly for the hosts.

Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header strike Sander Berge’s raised hand.



No one appealed at the time, but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor to review the incident and awarded the spot-kick.

McGinn’s effort crashed against the crossbar and bounced out.

It was a strange choice for the Scot to step up with Jackson available — having previously scored just one penalty in his entire career.

But Suzuki’s clanger summed up a bizarre 24 hours for Villa.

It saw chairman Nassef Sawiris go into battle with Carragher over remarks made on the Stick to Football podcast.



The ex-Liverpool defender suggested Emery must surely be looking to get to the next level of the game because Aston Villa could never be as big as Manchester United.

That was followed by Carragher telling Villa fans to ‘Shut the f*** up’.

Billionaire Villa co-owner Sawiris said legal proceedings were being instigated, and less than 24 hours later Carragher apologised for his language.



Villa supporters wasted little time in making their views known with a first-minute chant of “Jamie Carragher, what a w****r”.

The backing for the manager is clear, however, with fans singing “Unai Emery’s Claret and Blue Army” on repeat.

Yet this result will still sting the Spaniard on a day when he needed Villa’s revival to continue.

Fulham proved a match for Villa, who lived dangerously before the crazy equaliser.

Cottagers midfielder Shea Charles said: “The way the goal came wasn’t how we deserved it.

“We played how we can in the second half.”

Team-mate Calvin Bassey added: “I’m proud of the boys. I think we should have got more.”

Sports.title: Man Utd fans aim X-rated chant at Sir Jim Ratcliffe during Chelsea defeat as Jason Wilcox ‘called every name under sun’
Sports.content:
Next

HATRED, mischief and the hairdryer were thrown at the board.

Manchester United’s travelling army went to Stamford Bridge expecting another defeat and primed to conduct a public execution of those at the top.



Six days after the Stretford End turned up the heat at Old Trafford following the defeat to Bournemouth, the raucous away end in West London brought even bigger fireworks.

Michael Carrick will likely have two more games to lap up his chant as United boss before the inevitable comes during the international break.



Maybe a few directors will suffer twice more — against Roma and Aston Villa — with their jobs on the line if a third manager is sacked 2½ years into their reign of terror.

Whether you are home or away, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe is no different from the Glazers.



A shiny new stadium means nothing if the club is relegated.

The first salvo came before most people had settled into their seats.

“Jim Ratcliffe’s a c***, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c***, just like the Glazers, Ratcliffe’s a . . . ”

And all in Ratcliffe’s favourite part of the UK — Chelsea, home of his beloved Grenadier pub in Belgravia and the club he failed to buy in 2022.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Director of football Jason Wilcox was called every name under the sun and chief executive Omar Berrada was high on the hit-list as United missed several chances before half-time.

The pair were even spotted making an awkward appearance on the team bus before a glum Carrick showed up afterwards.

Not exactly the VIP treatment they might have imagined when they signed up for the United soap opera.

In the press box, there was an amusing observation from several London-based reporters — how many other directors of football in the Premier League could be recognised by name?

Not many. Wall-to-wall coverage of the country’s biggest crisis club means Wilcox has become almost as familiar to supporters as the manager.



The former Leeds and Blackburn winger’s name has not escaped the spotlight since Lisandro Martinez attacked the club chiefs after the Atletico Madrid defeat in the Champions League, insisting that “the technical director” needed to do more.

There is an irony in Martinez demanding better recruitment, when his own performances have hardly removed the need for defensive reinforcements.

Making only his second start since that bombshell interview in Madrid, the Argentine managed to turn another afternoon into a personal nightmare. Booked for a foul on Morgan Rogers, 83 SECONDS later he raised an arm into Wesley Fofana’s face inside the United box.



VAR intervened and a Cole Palmer penalty was awarded and converted.

A player calling for the club to do more had just left his team-mates with even more to do.

Carrick, meanwhile, barely lifted his eyes from his notepad as Martinez trudged down the tunnel. The away end needed no prompts.

Out came the classic 1974 Pilot hit: “It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes, it’s Carrick, you know.”

There was another twist in the Martinez saga, too.

Peter Schmeichel finally decided to have his say on the defender, having previously given him an easy ride on CBS in Madrid.



The legendary goalkeeper does not want to see the World Cup winner in a United shirt again.

The travelling support will continue to be more than forgiving of Carrick, who has not won in the Premier League since August 30 against Ipswich or a game of football in 52 DAYS.

Bruno Fernandes too was treated to his Portuguese magnifico tune, despite failing to be their saviour this season as he has been in the past.



The Player of the Year looked emotional, teary-eyed even, presumably unable to save a fourth manager from being axed since he joined in 2020.

Carrick said: “The supporters have been absolutely amazing, and the way they’re not just turning up, it’s the effort, the money they spend for that.

“But they’ve been really tested at the moment.

“They’ve gone through some really big highs over the years, and it’s easy to go the other way.

“But the way they’ve stuck by all of us and supported the team, and went through the second half in difficult circumstances, and stayed behind, that sums up exactly what they’re all about.



“We have got to give them something to really get their teeth into, a good direction.

“I’m not clinging to the first half as a huge positive but they have the type of feelings and performances that we’ve got to give to them.

“But I massively appreciate them for being what they are, and they’re showing everything they are at the moment.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Indeed United supporters are the only positive that this club has right now.

Chiefs are running out of places to hide and a boardroom change feels unavoidable.

Sports.title: Harry Kane shows off Ballon d’Or trophy to adoring Bayern fans before England captain skies penalty in derby draw
Sports.content:

HARRY KANE missed a penalty in his first game after winning the Ballon d’Or.

Then the England icon thought he had made amends by setting up Dayot Upamecano for a Bayern Munich winner.



But Borussia Dortmund came away with a deserved 2-2 draw thanks to Fabio Silva’s late leveller.

It was an emotional Allianz Arena return for the man who was crowned best player on the planet on Monday.



Kane, 33, made a triumphant entrance from the tunnel clutching his golden trophy.

Waiting on the pitch with the players were his family, including wife Kate and children Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry.

He grabbed a microphone to tell the fans: “I’m extremely proud to be a Bayern player.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment Swindon goalie Connor Ripley pinches Ian Holloway’s FLATCAP to block out sun as cheeky move pays off

SWINDON goalkeeper Connor Ripley led his team to a League Two victory over Rotherham thanks to manager Ian Holloway’s FLAT CAP.

The keeper struggled in goal after being blinded by the glaring sun.

And there was no baseball cap in sight – like the ones Bayern Munich‘s legendary goalie Oliver Kahn used to don.

Swindon supporters loved the retro sight as they flooded social media.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland’s dad breaks silence on Man City guilty verdict and speaks out over son’s future amid relegation threat
Sports.content:
Next

ALFIE HAALAND has broken his silence on Manchester City’s financial breaches.

The Norwegian, 53, is the father of City star Erling Haaland, who has been playing under the cloud of the charges since the club’s guilty verdict was handed down in September.



And now he has finally given an update on how he and his son are handling the decision, and the prospect of severe penalties that could even include a relegation to the Championship.

When asked about his reaction to the verdict, Haaland told Viaplay: “Well, it has been circulating for quite a while, hasn’t it?



“So finally something came that was concrete, which it is possible to fight against for City as a club.

“Obviously, these are serious allegations, but now there is an appeal case pending to be heard, so I think we have to stay calm, keep our cool, and wait to see how it turns out.”



When prompted about what his son thinks about the club’s situation, he played down the impact of the crisis.

Haaland continued: “Erling thinks about playing as much football as he can and concentrates on that. I think it’s more those of us outside the pitch who think a bit more about it.”

Haaland’s scoring form would suggest he has not been too rattled by the developments, bagging nine goals in as many games so far in the league alone.

But there is no secret information helping him keep his cool, with the father-son duo apparently as in the dark on City’s appeal as the rest of the footballing world.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

When asked is he had been told any further details, Haaland explained: “Nothing more than what’s in the media. And there is an awful lot written there, and very one-sided, I would say, right?

“Because it’s hard for Manchester City to come out right now – with an ongoing appeal – and defend themselves.

“So we hope they get a fair hearing, and then we’ll see if they manage to prove that they are innocent, eventually.”

Haaland, who made 38 league appearances for City himself between 2000 and 2003, praised the focus and conduct of City’s stars as they contest a title race and the appeal at the same time.

He added: “Now we just have to wait and see. I think they’ve done more than well to stand tall through this, because of course they have faced plenty of accusations. So I feel the player group has handled it very well.



“We also have to remember that these are things that allegedly happened quite a few years ago. The players today had nothing to do with it. So they’ve played well. They lost their last match, so it’s time to get back to winning ways.

When asked if he felt punishing the current crop of stars – including his son – was unfair, he admitted: “Yes, in a way, one might feel that having to potentially take punishment for something done many years ago… yes, I would say so.

Haaland was even confronted by the prospect of City’s relegation, and what Erling might do should such a drastic measure come to pass.

But he did not seem convinced that such a heavy sentence would be handed down, and waved away comparisons to Juventus being dropped to Serie B as a result of the Calciopoli scandal in 2006.



He laughed when asked if he feared a similar fate for his boy’s side, saying: “Well, Juventus was match-fixing and a few other things.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I think we should await the appeal process. It could happen quickly, even though there are rival supporters, clubs, and not least journalists who are out for blood against City right now.

“So we’ll just have to wait and see what the appeal outcome says. City believe they have strong evidence to stand up and prove their innocence, so I think we wait until that decision is reached.”

Sports.title: Prem star Jack Grealish spent two nights boozing in pub and karaoke bar days before being axed from Everton squad
Sports.content:
Next

JACK Grealish spent two nights on the trot boozing in London and Cheshire — days before a telling-off from Premier League club Everton.

The England winger, 31, first hit a London karaoke bar until late on a Monday night.



He then returned home to the North West and joined pals for a late-night session at a pub called The Mucky Pup the following night.

The £300,000-week star, on loan from Manchester City, visited other venues with a group of pals.



They included a ten-pin bowling alley in Cheshire’s trendy Altrincham area, close to the £6million home he shares with Sasha Attwood.

The two days of partying happened on October 19 and 20 — a week before Everton announced Grealish had been left out of the team over a “discipline issue”.



Prior to that it was said he could not face Arsenal last Saturday because he was ill.

Grealish’s boozy week started when he attended the Pride of Britain Awards at London’s Grosvenor House hotel.



After the ceremony, he arrived at BAM Karaoke Box in London’s Victoria and stayed until the early hours.

An insider said: “Jack was in great spirits after the awards and went out into London with a couple of mates.

“He got to BAM very late and stayed there until the early hours. They had several drinks, sang some songs and headed off very late.



“He looked like he was having a brilliant time.”

Grealish then headed home early Tuesday morning.

According to sources he attended training with Everton later that day.



But by Tuesday evening he was seen drinking in the Mucky Pup Irish bar in Wilmslow, where he met several pals including Everton team-mates Jordan Pickford and Tyler Dibling plus former England and City pal Kyle Walker.

One onlooker said: “They were watching the PSG v Barcelona game in a private back room of the pub.

“They were in good spirits and there were a lot of drinks being knocked back by all of them, including Jack.”

Sources said Jack and his Everton team-mates were given the day off from training on Wednesday, the day after he was in the Mucky Pup.

After he was left out of the Toffees’ Carabao Cup win over Newcastle, manager David Moyes said: “The club made the decision and I support it.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Grealish has made six appearances for Everton this campaign but has yet to score.

Everton have not yet confirmed whether he will return to the squad for tomorrow’s Prem match at Newcastle.

Sports.title: USA's Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at Mexico Open
Sports.content:
Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.

About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle.

That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie.

Novak ended the day on a 23-under 190, primed for his first individual title on the PGA Tour. His only other victory was teaming with Ben Griffin in the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year.

He had the low round of the day while playing in the last group, and goes into the final round coming off scores of 61-62.

"Very much the same, maybe a little sloppy at the end," Novak said of the two rounds. "But the putter saved it."

He holed a six-foot par on the 16th and made a 10-foot par putt on the 17th after coming up short.

Matthieu Pavon of France birdied his last two holes for a 65 to get within six shots. Doug Ghim had a 64 and was another shot behind.

"It makes it easier for me to be in my own bubble because I know that something significant would probably need to happen for me to have a chance tomorrow," Ghim said. "I'll do my best to put any pressure on him and see what happens."

Pavon needs something special, too, though he already is having a good week if he can hold his position. His two-year exemption from winning at Torrey Pines in 2024 runs out this year. Pavon came to the Mexico Open at No 140 in the FedEx Cup. A runner-up finish would move him just inside the top 100.

Image: The USA's Andrew Novak enjoyed another stellar day at the Mexico Open on Saturday

Kihei Akina, a 20-year-old, settled down after a bogey-bogey start and posted a 68. He was nine shots behind in a tie for seventh. Another finish in the top 10 would give him another point in the PGA Tour University accelerated program.

Everyone is chasing Novak, who has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.

"You want to back up a really low round with something low, but you don't usually expect that," Novak said.

"You expect usually there's going to be some give, and you've just got to be patient with it the next day. I still kind of came out firing today, was throwing some darts, making putts and trying to stay out of my own way."

Sports.title: Hamilton: A 'dream' to emulate Schumacher with first Ferrari pole
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton said he had achieved his "dream" of emulating Michael Schumacher after claiming his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The 41-year-old unexpectedly snatched pole from Mercedes' George Russell in a thrilling end to qualifying to take his first pole in over three years and extend his record career pole tally to 105.

Hamilton and Schumacher share the sport's record for the most Drivers' Championships with seven each, but while the Brit won one title with McLaren and the other six with Mercedes, the bulk of Schumacher's success came at Ferrari as he won five in a row from 2000 to 2004.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "To get the pole, finally get a pole for Ferrari, just takes me back to when I was a kid and sitting on the sofa and watching Michael get those poles, thinking 'how cool would it be to do that?'"

"It was a dream my family have shared with me and I know so many people in the world grew up watching Michael.

"To be at this point of my career and still have this special feeling - 105 [poles], the number doesn't mean much in a sense, it feels like the first.

"I spoke a couple years ago about getting to have a first. It feels like when you get to 40 they are all gone, but I'm having those firsts this year and I'm in a really good place."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix

2009 F1 world champion and Hamilton's former team-mate Jenson Button said he noticed how confident the Ferrari driver looked in Q3.

Hamilton had been four tenths off the pace of his team-mate Charles Leclerc after the first runs in Q3, but then produced his best lap of the weekend when it mattered most.

"Watching that lap back, he was so smooth," Button said.

"There was one moment were he got a bit of oversteer but apart from that he is driving within the limits. I think that's the big positive."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton edged out George Russell to become the oldest driver to claim pole position since 1982

Can Hamilton win the Mexico City GP?

Hamilton, who is the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti in 1982, starts on the front row alongside Russell - the only two drivers who can prevent Kimi Antonelli from becoming world champion on Sunday.

Antonelli only needs to finish in the top nine to become champion but, should he come 10th or fail to score any points, victory for Hamilton or Russell would delay the inevitable for another round.

The long run down to Turn 1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez always creates jeopardy and the pole-sitter has the disadvantage of towing trailing cars down the long straight.

Mexico City GP: Top 10 Starting Grid 1) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



2) George Russell, Mercedes



3) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



4) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



5) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



6) Lando Norris, McLaren



7) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



8) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



9) Pierre Gasly, Alpine



10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi

Hamilton, whose only Grand Prix win for Ferrari came in Barcelona earlier this year, says it will be a "big challenge" to keep Russell and Leclerc behind, but that he will make his car "as wide as possible".

"It's a long run down to Turn 1 - very tough," he said.

"It's not a bad place to be in first but people can tow you. Lando did a really good job last year so I have to try and do what he did.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton complained about a power issue before having an early end to his Friday in FP2 at the Mexico City GP

"Getting away off the line, I'm going in a little bit blind because in FP2 the engine stopped, so I didn't get to do a long run. I really don't know what the balance is like when you put all that fuel in.

"I kind of have to engineer my way through it and somehow drive my way through it. If we can get to Turn 1 first, then it comes down to how you manage your tyres. Hopefully we can have one of those special days where you can maybe whisper them a long way."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite qualifying second, Mercedes driver George Russell admits he's 'still a bit frustrated' with his lack of consistency this season

Russell thinks Turn 1 will be "crucial" as overtaking is likely to be difficult due to the high altitude, with the tight margins between the top teams potentially too small for passes to be possible later in the race.

"I think the race pace, there's probably going to be a tenth between the top seven or eight drivers," Russell said.

"Overtaking is going to be tough, overheating, etc. It's always the case here in Mexico. But get a good night's sleep and see what the race brings."

Leclerc added: "I'll keep my head down as much as possible and see what's possible. But, yes, it's always an exciting Turn 1 there, and we'll see how it goes."

Sports.title: Antonelli feeling 'tense' amid effort to seal F1 title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has admitted to feeling "more tense than usual" ahead of attempting to seal the Formula 1 world championship at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old only needs to finish ninth in the race to become the sport's youngest world champion.

Antonelli qualified fifth on Saturday but will start from fourth on the grid due to a penalty for Max Verstappen.

Speaking after the session, the Italian revealed that he is not feeling his best as he continues to recover from an illness that caused him to miss his media duties on Thursday.

He told Sky Sports F1: "It has not been the easiest weekend to be fair.

"Definitely still not feeling 100 per cent. There is talk of what could happen [with the championship] and definitely I'm a bit more tense than usual.

"Definitely I don't feel as relaxed but I try to have a good sleep tonight and focus on tomorrow."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Kimi Antonelli on the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest ever world champion, Ted Kravitz looks at the history of those who have broken that record previously

Despite his condition, Antonelli was still able to produce a decent final lap in qualifying as he finished within two tenths of pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton.

However, the fact that his team-mate George Russell was only marginally behind Hamilton in second perhaps reflected the Italian not being able to summon his best level.

Antonelli added: "I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn't have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie.

"It was a poor lap, many mistakes here and there. Overall, still P4 and a lot to play for tomorrow."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admits he felt 'a bit tense' after qualifying only fifth for the Mexico City Grand Prix

'It's insane!' - Norris happy to pass No 1 onto Antonelli

Lando Norris says he is "more than happy" to pass the number one he has had on his McLaren this year to Antonelli when the Mercedes driver replaces him as world champion.

Antonelli has massively exceeded expectations during just his second season in F1 to comprehensively outperform Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite.

"He's done an incredible job and done it in a pretty incredible way," Norris said ahead of the race weekend in Mexico.

"People are saying he hasn't had any tough competition this year. That proves the point that he's done such an incredible job.

"He's got a very, very talented team-mate that he's beaten through the whole season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player As Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli nears clinching the 2026 F1 championship, the rest of the grid give their verdict on the Italian's season

"I have nothing but respect for Kimi. He's a very nice guy. We get along very well and I'm more than happy to pass the No 1 over to him.

"He deserves it. He's done an incredible job, especially in his second year in Formula 1. Youngest world champion, it's pretty insane.

"I enjoy other people having that kind of success. It's nice to see."

Sports.title: Canelo returns to beat Mbilli and reclaim world title in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez marshalled Christian Mbilli as he reclaimed the WBC super-middleweight world championship he used to hold.

The Mexican superstar won the title beating Mbilli by unanimous decision in Riyadh.

Canelo was returning to boxing a year after his stunning loss to Terence Crawford and went straight in with a strong, previously undefeated world champion.

Mbilli did press Alvarez in the first half of the fight. He threw in busy bursts and moved Canelo into the ropes.

But Canelo began to exert increasing control of the action from the sixth round onwards.

With brilliant skill he used a right uppercut to open a path for a hard right cross. He grew more comfortable on the ropes, working with counter-punches, and his vicious uppercut made Mbilli wary.

In the eighth round Canelo finished a four-punch combination with a right to the head. Mbilli drove forward and all of a sudden the referee took a point off the champion for hitting round the back of the head.

Image: Christian Mbilli ultimately could not get to grips with Canelo. (AP Photo/David Becker)

Mbilli urgently needed to shift momentum. Instead Canelo turned the screw. Alvarez came off the ropes to work from the centre of the ring, drilling Mbilli with his right hook.

In the final round Mbilli struck in a good shot but backed off. Canelo even waved him in again, but Mbilli wouldn't respond.

Canelo pressed forward, and Mbilli smacked him with a hard right. Canelo wanted to finish fighting and blasted home an excellent right.

He made sure of a unanimous decision, taking the win 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 on the cards.

Alvarez is a vastly experienced veteran, who's won it all many times over in his 68-bout professional career. Yet he was delighted, almost relieved to be a world champion again.

"It's so difficult to explain. It's something unbelievable," Canelo said. "Now after 21 years as a professional, 16 years ago I won my first title, now I won the title again… I want to thank everybody back home.

"I knew he was a strong fighter. He didn't throw a lot of punches because it's difficult to throw punches with me... I did perfectly," he added.

"I'm going to keep learning, I'm going to keep working hard. I'm going to take a couple of weeks off and then come back."

Image: Canelo Alvarez was coming back after a stunning loss to Terence Crawford.

Jaime Munguia had to weather an almighty scare to carve out a unanimous decision win over Nikita Zon and defend his WBA super-middleweight title.

Zon, genuinely an awkward southpaw, found a home for heavy backhand lefts in the opening rounds. He drove Munguia to the ropes and into corners.

He was on the verge of knocking out Munguia in the sixth round. He led with a long left uppercut, badly hurting the Mexican. Munguia retreated but Zon swarmed all over him. He hammered Munguia but the champion refused to fall.

When Zon tired, Munguia hit back and he took clear control in the late rounds to win 16-112 and 117-111 twice on the scorecards.

Towering featherweight Rafael Espinoza easily dismissed replacement opponent Ricardo Blandon to retain the WBO world title.

He banged a flush cross into the top of the Nicaraguan's head which opened up a nasty cut along Blandon's eyelid. The ringside doctor pulled him out in the third round immediately after inspecting it.

Sports.title: Suzuki makes string of saves before conceding own goal in draw with Fulham
Sports.content:
Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham.

Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner.

With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player John McGinn hits the bar after Villa were awarded a penalty when a Sander Berge handball in the box was caught by VAR.

The home side nearly paid a heavy price for McGinn's miss straightaway after a Fulham counter-attack, but Oscar Bobb was brilliantly denied the opener by a one-handed save from Suzuki who tipped the ball over.

Villa went in front after Timothy Castagne's error allowed Johan Manzambi to play a ball through to Jackson, who cut inside and beat David Affengruber, before wriggling clear of the recovering Castagne to slide the ball past Bernd Leno.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nicolas Jackson puts Villa in front in their Premier League match against Fulham.

There were chances at both ends in the second half, with Victor Lindelof almost extending Villa's when he directed Ian Maatsen's effort towards goal only to be denied by a reflex save from Leno.

Suzuki was forced to divert a Matty Cash away from the on-rushing Gonzalo Garcia before saving an Alex Iwobi header from eight yards out.

But Villa's goalkeeper made an unforced error when he allowed an Iwobi corner to slip through his fingers and bounce over the goal-line before he could retrieve it as Fulham drew level.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Fulham.

Suzuki got down at his near post to make a late save to deny Antonee Robinson, before Pau Torres headed wide from 12 yards out at the other end as both sides had to settle for a point apiece.

What the managers said...

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery:

Emery: 'Disappointing result but a fair result'

"It was a disappointing result, but a fair result. I think they deserved it as well, this draw.

"It was tough for us in the second half, more than the first half.

"Second half, we knew we should try to play in the same way as in the first half, but they dominated more in the second half, they created chances and they scored a goal.

"We created some chances and we could have even won the match, but I think it was a fair result.

On Suzuki's error: "This is part of football.

"I think he played fantastic and he did a lot of saves and action defensively, so he can make one mistake like this. It's part of football.

Arbeloa: We are a difficult team to beat

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa:

"I am so happy with our performance in the second half. This is what I want to see from my team, that character, that ambition.

"We needed to be aggressive against a team like Villa.

"It was a Champions League team in front of us.

"Technically, I thought we were very good but this is the Premier League and you have to be aggressive, and physically, you have to be at your best level.

"I think maybe we deserved a little bit more, but the performance was really great.

"I think we are a very difficult team to beat and I think we can beat anyone."

Fulham are heading in the right direction

Analysis by Lewis Jones:

There was something rather telling about the reaction of the Fulham players to their travelling supporters at full-time. This was not a team celebrating a point like they had got away with something. It was a team that knew they had given their fans plenty to shout about.

Fulham were excellent for large parts of their 1-1 draw at Aston Villa. They took the game to Unai Emery's side, dictated the tempo for long spells and created enough opportunities to leave Villa Park feeling they should have taken more.

The underlying numbers reinforce the eye test. Fulham generated 2.2 expected goals, the fifth-highest total recorded by any visiting team at Villa Park since the start of the 2023/24 season. They also registered 40 touches inside the Villa penalty area. That is serious territorial dominance against a side who rarely allow opponents to dictate terms on home soil.

This feels like a Fulham team beginning to find its feet. There is more purpose to their attacking play, more conviction in possession and a growing belief that they can compete with the division's better sides.

The key moments from Villa Park

5: CHANCE! Iwobi strikes from 15 yards but blazes it over the crossbar. Terrible execution.

7: CHANCE! Goretzka rises highest at a corner but plants his header over the crossbar

14: PENALTY! The referee takes to the mic and awards Aston Villa a penalty after Berge is penalised for handball

16: MCGINN HITS BAR! The crossbar is absolutely rattled by the Villa man. It was a fierce strike, but the ball comes back off the woodwork.

Image: John McGinn misses the chance to open the scoring from the penalty spot during Aston Villa's game against Fulham

32: SAVE! Fulham counter and Bobb only has the goalkeeper to beat from 10 yards but Suzuki reacts with one-hand to tip it over.

39: GOAL! Jackson backs Castagne and Affengruber towards their own goal and turns them one way and the other. It's awful defending but Jackson takes full advantage, finding the bottom corner.

48: CHANCE! Cash's ball is flung into the middle which Suzuki gets a hand to, stopping Garcia from getting a tap-in as the ball hits the striker and deflects wide.

61: SHOT! Great trickery from Bobb, his effort is blocked and Charles comes in on the rebound. It's a precise effort but it's the wrong side of the post.

65: GOAL! Iwobi swings a juicy corner right into the six-yard box and Suzuki allows it to slip through his fingers and over the goal-line.

80: SAVE! Garcia flicks one to Robinson in acres of space. Cash can't touch the Fulham man who hits one from the angle. Suzuki gets down to stop it.

90+1: CHANCE! Torres heads wide from from eight yards out and sinks to his knees.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists he will still be in charge of Manchester United against Roma
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insisted he would still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. United’s problems mounted as their winless run reached nine games. Carrick is clinging on to his job after overseeing the club’s first such run since 1988 and tried to focus on the next game as he analysed his side’s defending when Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Chelsea.

“It’s never a good goal to concede,” he said. “Morgan went through the middle of us and at that point the game was right in the balance. To concede like that was a big moment. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”

United played well during the first half, but missed a series of clear opportunities. They folded after going behind and their fate was sealed when Lisandro Martínez was sent off for a foul that led to Cole Palmer making it 2-0 from the spot. Carrick, though, steered clear of criticising one of his most experienced players for leaving United in the lurch.

“It was a major part of the game,” he said. “The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it.”

United were just above the bottom three before the afternoon games, but Carrick said there would be no stigma attached to one of the biggest clubs in the country falling into the relegation zone should results elsewhere have that effect. “There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes it any different,” he said. “It’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez isn’t looking at his man when he barges into Wesley Fofana, giving away a penalty, and earning a red card in the process. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Carrick was asked if his players were ready for a relegation battle. “You can look at it like that, and you can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches,” he said. “That’s the way it’s got to be approached.”

Chelsea moved into fourth place overnight, responding well to losing to Tottenham in the league and Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup. “The first half was intense,” Xabi Alonso said. “United had their chances, we were close as well, so at half-time we have spoken and the reaction from the second half was better.
