“We started quite well, we got the lead, we looked in better control and after 2-0 and the red card the context of the game changed. But it has not been easy.”

Alonso praised Estêvão Willian after the Brazil winger sparkled on his first start in the league this season. “We spoke after Tottenham and he knew that he was going to be playing today,” the Chelsea manager said. “He has had the best response to show he deserves more, that he was prepared and that’s what you want, so I’m very happy for him.”

Sports.title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham a point
Sports.content:
Fulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence.

Villa’s goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropped Alex Iwobi’s corner over his own goalline to deny Unai Emery’s team a fifth win in six games after Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the top third of the Premier League. Not even John McGinn’s missed penalty had looked set to deny them as they took control in the first period.

But while Villa were made to look below par by a Fulham side making it seven points from the last nine, the home supporters sang long and loud to make their manager know how much he is appreciated.

The Holte End had not waited long to voice their verdict on the spat between the former England international and the Villa chair.

Carragher had admitted that his words were “clumsy and wrong” after telling Villa fans “to shut the fuck up” as they reacted angrily to his claims that Emery should want to manage Manchester United if Michael Carrick were to be sacked after their long winless run. It seemed like a storm in a teacup to many until Nassef Sawiris issued a statement promising to initiate legal action. “As custodians of this great club, we cannot stand still while the F word is directed at Villa fans,” Sawiris said.

Notwithstanding this disappointing draw, it is beyond question that Emery has done an admirable job at Villa. Even after losing another tranche of top talent, with Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Emi Martínez heading up the exits last summer after winning the Europa League, the former Arsenal and PSG manager has resurrected the club’s fortunes yet again. They start seasons slowly – winning only two of their last 12 league games in August and September – but once he has cast his spell and integrated the new signings, Villa tend to get going; they had won eight of their previous 10 league games in October and November.

View image in fullscreen Zion Suzuki fumbles the ball into the net to gift Fulham their goal. Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/Shutterstock

It must be galling to qualify for the Champions League twice in three years and yet still have your best talents lured away. So the idea that United could, in Carragher’s eyes, come and click their fingers and expect Emery to be unable to resist their faded grandeur evidently stuck in the throats of Villa fans and chair alike.

Fulham’s second-half showing, in particular, merited a draw that followed their recent league wins over Hull and Coventry and kept them two points above the relegation zone in Álvaro Arbeloa’s first autumn in charge. Emery would never countenance it but perhaps Villa’s ultimate glamour trip, to Barcelona, on Tuesday before next Sunday’s visit to Old Trafford, of all places, overshadowed this game.

McGinn spurned his first penalty for the club (excluding shootouts), awarded after Sander Berge was belatedly adjudged to have handled Leon Goretzka’s header, when he thundered his spot-kick against the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson opens the scoring for Aston Villa in the first half. Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

But while Fulham had plenty of the ball, Villa appeared content to threaten on the counterattack. Indeed, they took the lead in the 39th minute after Jackson was sent running down the inside-left channel by a perfect through ball from Johan Manzambi. The £65m striker weaved into the penalty area past Timothy Castagne and David Affengruber before slotting in his fifth goal in five Premier League games.

Fulham were much more dominant in the second half. “They were more aggressive than us in the first half,” Arbeloa admitted. “I told my players I know we are a team that wants to control the game through the ball. But this is the Premier League. If you want to win a game, you need to fight for every ball.” When Castagne headed on Alex Iwobi’s corner, both Gonzalo García and Shea Charles got a touch on the ball before it spooned up on to the roof of the net. Villa were riding their luck.

Fulham’s dominance paid off, however, in the most unexpected fashion midway through the second half. Suzuki, who has been lauded for his early-season form, had just saved a header from Iwobi when, from the Nigerian’s ensuing corner, under no pressure, he inexplicably dropped the ball just over the line. “It’s part of football,” Emery said. “I make mistakes as coach. The players are making every match mistakes … when it’s the keeper, those mistakes are more in focus. I prefer to speak about the saves he did today.”

Sports.title: Spurs see off Crystal Palace after Mateta’s early red to pile pressure on Sage
Sports.content:
Fortune is not favouring Pierre Sage. Just when the Crystal Palace manager needed a positive result, Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card condemned his side to a third straight defeat in the league, leaving their manager’s position hanging by a thread.

Goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensured that Tottenham recorded a third successive victory for the first time in 616 days as they moved into the top half of the table. To put that into context, Spurs have had three full-time managers since then, so it was no wonder that Roberto De Zerbi looked so pleased at full time.

By contrast, Sage’s future is in doubt, given that there was an expectation he could be sacked if they lost this game. While Mateta’s reckless red card did him no favours and Palace managed to stay in the game until Van Hecke’s innovative finish 17 minutes from full time, they now find themselves in the bottom three. Only the chair, Steve Parish, will decide his fate with Liverpool up next at home before the international break. Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank are waiting in the wings.

“I told the players I want to be the first on pitch on Monday. I will do the best session I can. Now I have the rage to train more, because the game I saw this evening is not in line with my conviction,” said a defiant Sage. “It’s not me to decide this thing, but if I have one hour, I will give my best during one hour, and if I have 10 years, I will give my best during 10 years. I am responsible for the situation, and I am the guy who will find the solution for the situation.”

View image in fullscreen Jan Paul van Hecke uses his head to double Spurs’ lead. Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA

Having won only twice at home in the league all year, Tottenham’s supporters had reason to be optimistic after successive victories over Coventry and Chelsea. But while De Zerbi used his programme notes to urge his players not to get complacent, there is no mistaking the signs of momentum, and the Italian singled out the performance of his compatriot – £100m summer signing Sandro Tonali – in midfield. “We played with two players more,” said De Zerbi. “We can’t forget where we were before the last international break. But now we are playing as a team.”

Tottenham’s cause was certainly aided when Mateta was sent off after only 13 minutes. The France striker was never going to get to the ball before Micky van de Ven as he passed it back to Antonin Kinsky, and Mateta’s studs caught the Tottenham defender on the back of his heel. The referee, Michael Oliver, initially showed a yellow card but the outcome was inevitable when the VAR directed him upstairs. Some of the home supporters gasped when they saw a slow-motion replay on the giant screens, although that made it look much worse.

View image in fullscreen Jean-Philippe Mateta’s reckless challenge on Micky van de Ven (left) resulted in a red card for the Crystal Palace player. Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA

Sage shook his head as Mateta trudged down the tunnel. Not for the first time this season, after Axel Disasi’s red card against Ipswich last month, Palace found themselves down to 10 men with most of the game still to play. They kept Tottenham at bay for a while but played a part in their own downfall again. No one was picking up Gray – who scored his first Spurs goal against Palace in a rare win under Thomas Frank last year – at the back post from a deep Mohammed Kudus corner, and he headed in unopposed. The television cameras cut to Parish in the stand looking less than impressed.

View image in fullscreen Archie Gray (right) heads home to open the scoring for Tottenham against Crystal Palace. Photograph: Jed Leicester/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

De Zerbi replaced Gray, on a yellow card, at the break with Pedro Porro. Palace retreated even further and Van Hecke should have done better from close range after another corner but ballooned into the crowd. In an attempt to relieve some of the pressure, Sage threw on former Arsenal striker Eddie Nketiah to jeers from the Spurs fans. Dwight McNeil had a rare sight of goal that was blocked but Palace almost paid the price as Tottenham broke downfield.

Any hopes Palace had of snatching something ended when Fernandes picked out Van Hecke and the Dutchman, on the ground, cleverly nodded the ball over the line after Henderson had pushed his initial header on to the bar. Had Kudus scored after being set up by 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett,it would have rounded off the perfect afternoon for De Zerbi, who is the latest example of how quickly things can change in football.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca rues ‘silly’ errors after Manchester City defeat against Brighton
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victory here. Ayari’s strike was made possible after Nunes, City’s right-back, missed Diego Gómez’s cross from the right, so the ball could come back across goal via Maxim De Cuyper.

The 2-1 loss at Aston Villa came from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowing Nicolas Jackson’s long-range winner to squeeze under his body.

“Sometimes it happens,” said Maresca. “Unfortunately, it is happening for our players, but it is part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse, understand what we can do better and try to move on.

“We are the second team in terms of scoring in the Premier League, but we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid and hopefully we can avoid in the next game.

“It is a very similar feeling we had after the Aston Villa game – unfortunately we created enough to get some points but we didn’t score. At the moment it is like this. We did enough to deserve something. We need to move on and try to win games. For sure we are not happy.”

While Maresca said he had not seen the free-kick awarded against Elliot Anderson to decide if this was fair, Brighton’s victory takes them to 19 points, two behind City, who are the leaders before Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

Fabian Hürzeler was delighted his players had changed the feeling of Wednesday’s Carabao Cup penalty shootout loss to City. “Every morning you can wake up and decide if you’re disappointed by something you cannot change or set the tone,” he said. “Stand up and have the belief that you’ll have a different feeling. It was brutal [the cup defeat]. We promised ourselves that we won’t have the same feeling.

“We want to be satisfied. We created energy, positivity, the next day. You need this. We saw Saturday as an opportunity to come back stronger. This was the approach and how the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.”

Hürzeler was asked what is possible for Brighton this season. “The only thing we’re focused on is that we are in a big process, a process of analysing the game. Then try to prepare for Getafe [on Thursday], a big challenge.”

Sports.title: European football: Kane misses penalty as Dortmund share spoils in Der Klassiker
Sports.content:
The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for ⁠Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw ⁠in Der Klassiker on ⁠Saturday ​that kept the teams level on points at the top.

Kane, who collected his prize in a ceremony ⁠in London on Monday, was an unused substitute in the 6-1 German Cup second-round demolition of Magdeburg on Wednesday ⁠but returned to the starting lineup on Saturday, missing from the spot with Bayern 1-0 up. He also hit ​the post, one of four ‌times Bayern struck ‌the woodwork. Silva snatched the equaliser in the 89th minute to leave both ‌teams on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference.

In a rollercoaster first half Bayern hit the post through Michael Olise and Ismael Saibari missed a golden chance before the visitors had a goal ruled out by VAR.

View image in fullscreen Fabio Silva’s late equaliser keeps Dortmund level on points with Bayern at the top. Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty Images

Bayern, ‌also hit by injuries to Serge Gnabry and Olise, struck in the 38th minute thanks to Konrad Laimer’s goal on ​the rebound, after his first effort was blocked by Dortmund’s Gregor Kobel.

With the Bayern head coach, Vincent Kompany, recovering after his collapse last week, Bayern’s full-back Laimer was more threatening than Kane, who sent his 56th ⁠minute spot-kick against the crossbar. Dortmund scored through Serhou Guirassy on ​the hour but parity lasted only ​six minutes as Dayot Upamecano tapped in from a Kane ​assist from close ‌range.

Kane’s low shot ​bounced off ​the post before Silva scored the equaliser. Bayern’s Lennart Karl still had time to see his shot in stoppage time bounce off the crossbar and cap a frustrating day for the champions.

Elsewhere in the Bundesliga, last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg beat Augsburg 2-1 thanks to Cyriaque Irié’s 85th-minute goal to stay third. RB Leipzig are close behind in fourth after beating Schalke 2-0. The league top scorer, Niclas Füllkrug, added his ninth goal as Werder Bremen beat Hoffenheim 2-0 to move up to fifth. Bayer Leverkusen’s strong early form hit another setback in a 4-2 loss at home to Stuttgart for back-to-back defeats. Borussia Mönchengladbach and Paderborn drew 0-0.

View image in fullscreen Atlético Madrid’s Alex Grimaldo (right) celebrates after opening the scoring against Levante. Photograph: Kai Forsterling/EPA

In Spain, Barcelona enjoyed an emphatic 6-1 home win over Alaves, with Raphinha, Fermín López, Lamine ⁠Yamal and Anthony Gordon all on the scoresheet, as the hosts responded after losses to Real Madrid and Paris St Germain. Barcelona ⁠top La Liga on 30 ⁠points, two ​ahead of Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0 earlier on Saturday, with Real Madrid six points off the pace before ⁠visiting Racing Santander on Sunday.

The opening exchanges at Camp Nou were punctuated by frustrated shouts from the home manager, Hansi Flick, in response to ⁠Barcelona’s defending, but Alaves soon found it impossible to live with their fluid attacking play.

“It was a hard week for us, there was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans [to bounce back],” López said. “They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha, with them we will achieve big things.”

There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo.

In Italy, Milan’s Diego Moreira claimed one goal and two assists as his side took three precious points with a 3-1 victory over Inter in their Serie A derby on Saturday, while Roma enjoyed a 5-2 victory at ⁠Udinese.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In a week when ⁠the clubs ​shared more details of San Siro’s replacement, Milan’s fast start earned the win that lifts them into fourth ⁠place, four points behind leaders Lazio and Inter who have 25. The result means Lazio can move three points clear of Inter when they host Cagliari on Sunday. Roma ⁠are third on 24 points.

Milan made the perfect start as Christian Pulisic headed their opener after four minutes ​before Adrien Rabiot added a second six minutes ‌later. Inter pulled a goal ‌back through Alessandro Bastoni in the 22nd and the momentum was with them.

View image in fullscreen Milan players congratulate Diego Moreira after his goal against Inter. Photograph: Claudio Villa/AC Milan/Getty Images

The next goal was always ‌going to be crucial and it went to Milan as Moreira scored with a superb free-kick just before half-time to help his side to a fourth straight win over Inter.

Roma were 4-0 up in 37 minutes at Udinese as they overwhelmed the hosts, who are second-bottom on five points. Bryan Cristante headed the first goal after 10 minutes, before Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen struck the woodwork. Rodrigo Mora ‌netted the second in the 31st minute after being set up by Cristante, and two minutes later Malen scored his eighth Serie A goal of the season.

Evan Ndicka ​headed the fourth from a corner before half-time after which Udinese mounted something of a comeback. Nicolò Zaniolo and Matteo Palma scored for the hosts but Daniele Ghilardi added a fifth, his first Serie A goal, for Roma.

Bologna climbed to ninth with ​a third successive league win thanks ​to a 2-1 victory over Monza, their first home success since April. Tommaso Pobega and ​Federico Bernardeschi netted for ‌Bologna, after the ​visitors scored an early ​penalty through Gustavo Varela, the top Serie A scorer with nine goals in as many games. He had been substituted by the time Monza were awarded a second penalty in the final 10 minutes and this time Patrick Cutrone missed from the spot as they were denied a point.

Sports.title: Naderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup final
Sports.content:
Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.

The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well.

“So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Rangers – who will face the winners of Sunday’s semi-final between Hearts and Hibernian in the final – went into the game unbeaten in 10 and firm favourites.

With five Aberdeen defenders missing through suspension or injury – Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester, Dan Happe, Kristers Tobers and Chris Cadden – there was a makeshift element about their lineup, with a first start of the season for Nicky Devlin.

McInnes, the Rangers manager who won the trophy with Aberdeen in 2014, raised eyebrows by dropping midfielder Dan Neil, with left-back Tuur Rommens starting and Penrice moving into midfield, and Badredine Bouanani starting in place of Djeidi Gassama.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Naderi diverts James Prentice’s shot past Marius Müller. Photograph: Kirk O’Rourke/Rangers FC/Shutterstock

There was more readjustment for Aberdeen when Emmanuel Gyamfi injured himself trying to tackle Kim Min-su and was replaced by Stuart Armstrong.

In the 23rd minute, the Rangers defence parted and Nesta Guinness-Walker drove through the gap, forcing goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to save. Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet glanced a header wide of the goal before Naderi hooked an effort over the crossbar.

Quick Guide Scottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed Steward Show Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh. Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away. “We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.” Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth. Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association Photograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Just before the break Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller parried a low drive from Bouanani to safety, then Naderi headed a cross from stand-in captain Nico Raskin just over before Kim slashed a drive wide.

As the game became stretched, Pandur saved a deflected Kevin Nesbit drive then Müller blocked a shot from Kim before Rangers striker Kevin Kelsy somehow managed to head a pinpoint delivery from Bouanani past a post from six yards.

Müller’s foot blocked another effort from Bouanani and beat away a Raskin volley as the Aberdeen box came under siege. On a rare break, Nesbit’s shot was deflected wide and from the corner the Aberdeen striker hooked over the bar.

Aberdeen finally succumbed when Bouanani knocked the ball back to Penrice and he fired towards goal, with Naderi stepping in to beat Müller from close range.

Sports.title: Julio Enciso strikes again to earn Ipswich a point against Hull
Sports.content:
Hull maintained their unbeaten home record, but their winless run stretched to eight games after Julio Enciso earned Ipswich a draw at the MKM Stadium.

Ipswich had the lion’s share of possession in the first half, cutting through Hull’s defence repeatedly and Nobel Mendy and Konstantinos Tzolakis were unable to prevent Florentino Luis’s 22nd-minute opener as he sliced through on the right unhindered.

After 37 minutes, the visitors appeared to have doubled their lead as Enciso headed in from a corner, but the effort was disallowed for a foul on Oli McBurnie.

Hull upped their game after the break and after 58 minutes Tim Iroegbunam raced down the right and fired home the equaliser.

The pattern of the game changed entirely and 10 minutes later McBurnie slammed the ball beyond Christian Walton from a free-kick to giveHull the lead.

But it lasted only six minutes as Enciso worked his way through Hull’s backline to produce a stylish leveller from just outside the area. It followed his equaliser last week that earned his side a 1-1 draw against Nottingham Forest.

“We were excellent, the better side for almost all of it,” said the Ipswich manager, Gary O’Neil. “There’s disappointment that it doesn’t get us three [points], but a point on the road in the Premier League is still something.

“There was a lot of promise that we were much better than them in their own stadium. That takes some doing, they’re a good side and they’ve been doing well. You have to give them credit, they’ve done this against everybody.

“They don’t dominate the game, they don’t batter your goal, but if you make a mistake they will capitalise on it and that was the case today.”

After dominating possession early on Ipswich were rewarded with Florentino slipping past Mendy to leave Tzolakis with no chance as the ball flew past him and into the right corner.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie celebrates after putting Hull 2-1 ahead against Ipswich. Photograph: Dave Lofthouse/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Just over 10 minutes later the visitors threatened again, this time turning a corner, but it was chalked off as the referee, Thomas Kirk, adjudged McBurnie had been fouled by Abdul Fatawu.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

After the break, Ipswich continued to cause Hull problems, with Emersonn hitting the side-netting, having worked his way neatly through Hull’s back four. At the other end Walton was tested by a Lewie Coyle cross.

The hosts were pressing and the equaliser arrived when Iroegbunam was played through in space by a fine McBurnie pass and fired home.

The home side continued to look increasingly threatening, with Coyle going close with a shot that went wide before McBurnie stuck a 68th-minute free-kick through the wall.

Hull could not keep hold of the lead, however, and Enciso picked his way through the defence to fire home impressively and make it 2-2.

“We should have controlled the last 20 minutes better because Enciso scored an excellent goal, but still we could have defended it,” said the Hull manager, Sergej Jakirovic. “But if you cannot win, at least don’t lose. I know we are waiting now for almost two months for a win, but I am still positive.”

Sports.title: ‘We need to be better’: Manchester United’s Olid demands progress after Everton draw
Sports.content:
A group of well-choreographed, fancy-dress-wearing school-age dancers fully embraced the Halloween spirit on Saturday as they boogied to one of Michael Jackson’s greatest hits at half-time here. Alas, the match itself was no thriller.

For Manchester United, the only scary thing about this game was how little they tested Courtney Brosnan in Everton’s goal in the first 75 minutes as they demonstrated their lack of creativity.

Brosnan did well to save from Elisabeth Terland’s strike, as United grew into the game late on and began to apply some pressure, but this was a fixture worthy of finishing goalless or – as Sky Sports put it – ghoul-less.

Terland has scored five Women’s Super League goals against Everton, but Brosnan was equal to her close-range shot after Jess Park’s through ball.

“It was not a good performance, but we aren’t always going to perform amazing or good,” said the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid. “But it’s [about] always finding a way to win and today we didn’t.

“We need to be better. Out of possession, we were late, jumping late, to the individual duels, and in-possession we missed that creativity or connections we were having in the last matches.”

Everton, who are winless in all 15 WSL meetings with United, will be the happier with the point, and their encouraging performance, but they missed the opportunity to climb above their opponents into fourth and might wish they could have converted some of their good midfield play.

Their former Manchester United full-back Hannah Blundell hooked a dangerous effort, left-footed, towards the top corner in the first half, but her shot was saved by Phallon Tullis-Joyce, who also held on to shots – directed straight at her – from Ornella Vignola either side of the break.

Rosa van Gool and Yuka Momiki were combining well for Everton in midfield to frustrate United. United had won away at Everton in the past four seasons, but they were second best in the first half and unable to break the deadlock in the closing stages, despite making improvements after Simi Awujo came on.

United have been on a positive run, winning three and drawing one of their previous four WSL matches, the derby against Manchester City through a morale-boosting late equaliser, as well as enjoying a 100% record in the Players Cup, but they were stifled by an Everton side whose midfield kept the ball well.

Olid, who took over from Marc Skinner in August, said: “After such a positive performance on Sunday [against City] there is always that question – [are we] going to keep that standard or are we going to go a little down, like a hangover after that good match? I expected we would be better than we were. If this has to happen for us to learn and improve, we are going to do that.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A Park effort sailed high over the bar, after an Andrea Medina shot was blocked inside the Everton area, but otherwise there was relatively little to note of United’s first hour, from an attacking perspective.

This was Everton’s first draw of the league campaign, after three wins and four defeats, and they climbed above Arsenal – who play on Sunday – into sixth. They remain two points behind United, as Scott Phelan continues to oversee a steady – if unspectacular – spell in charge.

The Everton head coach said: “In the first half, I thought we were competitive, we showed some good bits with the ball. We just probably lacked a little bit of end product and belief in our game to finish the good passages of play we had. Second half, not so much, but it did highlight the togetherness of the team and the defensive organisation.”

His team certainly did look defensively well-organised. All they were really lacking was a top-quality focal point in attack, in a wretched game that did little to generate suspense.

Sports.title: Premier League boss challenges board to sack him amid deeper problems at club
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner has insisted that a new manager at Nottingham Forest will not guarantee improvement.

Forest were beaten 2-0 by Brentford on Saturday and have fallen into the Premier League relegation zone with nine games played.



3 Glasner believes he is safe at Forest and says that a change of manager would not bring improvement to the club Credit: Getty

They also have just one win from ten in all competitions since Glasner joined as head coach in July.

The former Crystal Palace boss is the fifth name to take the job in less than three years after Steve Cooper was sacked in December 2023.

Nuno Espirito Santo, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira preceded Glasner, who was very transparent on the club's struggles.



Speaking to the media after the loss at Brentford, he was asked if he has the freedom to make the changes he wants at Forest.

Glasner insists Forest sack won't bring change

"There is no other way," he declared. "And if I don't have the freedom, they have to sack me. That's it."



And when speaking to talkSPORT's Jack Cunningham, Glasner explained how Forest's problems run deeper than whoever is in charge.

"The reality is we lost four of our last five games, and that means for me it's time also to speak very honestly about it. It's time to change things because otherwise things will happen again



"We have to change things, I have to change a few things and I will definitely change a few things."

Glasner added: "I feel now maybe I was a little bit too patient and made a little bit too many compromises on a few things. And this is what I will definitely change.

"Then it's up to the players if they buy in, I think then we can get the turnaround and if not, the sixth manager will follow."

3 Brentford scored a goal in each half against Forest to inflict a fifth league defeat on their opponents Credit: Getty



On whether he is feeling the pressure from Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis, Glasner stated: "No, I don't have pressure, I think nobody needs to have pity with the manager.

"You get sacked, you go home with your family and, if you want, you can start a job within two weeks. But the players, the staff, they have to work and continue in the same situation like last year.

"If there have been four managers and things didn't really change and now it's the fifth one and things don't really change, I think it's deeper than changing the manager.

"But again, I have no concerns at all about my position.

"I came to Nottingham Forest to help the club establish in the top half of the Premier League, helping the owner to get his vision to reality, and for this we have to change things 100 percent, otherwise it's impossible."



Having his final say on the result to talkSPORT, Glasner remarked: "We want to be successful, but again, we need to change a few things.

3 Glasner has lost six of his ten matches across all competitions at Forest, and won just one of those Credit: Getty

"And let's say maybe the most obvious one is we are outrun by the opposition in every single game, this is number one. We're losing duels, I think today it was 61 per cent for Brentford in ground duels.

"That's the foundation, the basics of everything. Then we can talk about tactics, how we're playing looks nice. But in the important areas, you need to win the duels."



Forest are 19th and joined by Palace and Sunderland in the relegation zone, although Manchester United are only a point above them after their 2-0 loss to Chelsea.

They host leaders Manchester City at the City Ground next Saturday before the November international break.

Sports.title: Manchester United make immediate decision on Michael Carrick’s future after Chelsea defeat
Sports.content:
Manchester United make immediate decision on Michael Carrick’s future after Chelsea defeat

Michael Carrick is expected to be in the Manchester United dugout on Tuesday night against Roma, talkSPORT understands.

United were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea on Saturday afternoon and went down to ten man when Lisandro Martinez was sent off.



2 Carrick is set to be given more time as United head coach despite their winless run of nine matches Credit: Getty

The Red Devils are highly unlikely to make a head coach change until the upcoming international break at the earliest, even though the hierarchy held summit talks.

Senior boardroom figures are still hoping Carrick can turn around the club's worst start to a season since the 1986/87 campaign.

Carrick is preparing to be in charge for the Champions League clash at home to Roma.



United will then welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford on November 8.

Dismal United run continues

Carrick was on course for a first United victory since September 10 as they led after half an hour through Matheus Cunha.

However, the forward was found to be in an offside position and the goal was ruled out.



Morgan Rogers waltzed through their defence and chipped over Senne Lammens at the start of the second half to put Chelsea ahead.

Martinez was then shown two yellow cards in quick succession, the second of which saw him hit Wesley Fofana in the face with his arm.



Cole Palmer scored the penalty despite the best efforts of Lammens, and Estevao Willian had a second goal disallowed for the hosts.

United missed a string of chances, particularly during the first half, and fell to their fourth league defeat as a result.

2 Carrick has at least two more matches in charge at United, with a tough test against Roma next up Credit: Getty

Manchester City, Brighton, Atletico Madrid, Como, Bournemouth and Chelsea have all beaten United since they beat Sabah FK last month.



United have also drawn with Fulham, Tottenham and Leeds United in their winless run of nine matches.

They only remain outside the bottom three on goal difference, with Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland all below them.

Defeat to Roma during the week could see them slip down into the elimination zone of the Champions League.

Meanwhile, a similar result against Villa next weekend may see them enter the international break as a relegation-threatend side.

Sports.title: Harry Kane in unwanted 14-year first as Borussia Dortmund stun Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Harry Kane in unwanted 14-year first as Borussia Dortmund stun Bayern Munich

Harry Kane missed a penalty as Bayern Munich dropped points in the 2-2 Der Klassiker draw with Borussia Dortmund.

The newly-crowned Ballon d'Or winner smashed the woodwork with his effort from 12 yards early in the second half at the Allianz Arena with Bayern leading 1-0.



3 Kane became the first player since Robben in 2012 to miss a penalty during Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund Credit: Getty

Kane has only failed to convert a spot-kick 16 times during his career, whilst netting 113 of the total 129 he has taken.

However, the striker's penalty miss on Saturday evening was the first in the Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund since 2012.

Bayern legend Arjen Robben was the last player to squander such an opportunity during a 1-0 Bundesliga defeat in April 2012.



Bayern held to draw by Dortmund

Konrad Laimer put the hosts in front in the 33rd minute shortly after Dortmund had a Jobe Bellingham goal disallowed for a foul.

Serhou Guirassy levelled on the hour mark, only for Kane to make up for his penalty miss by assisting Dayot Upamecano.



He headed the ball across the face of goal for the defender to pick up an eighth assist of the campaign.

Dortmund were close to their first defeat of the season, but saved by Fabio Silva with a minute to go thanks to his well-taken shot.



The historic rivals are level on 18 points with five wins and three draws, although Bayern are top of the Bundesliga on goal difference.

Bayern have lost only one of their last 18 competitive meetings with Dortmund, winning 13 and drawing four.

They are also unbeaten in their last 22 Bundesliga matches as leaders against the second-placed side, the league's longest-ever run.

3 Kane had a helping hand in one of Bayern's goals, but they could not hold onto their lead and had to settle for a draw in the derby Credit: Getty



Before kick-off, Kane was given a hero's welcome by Bayern fans as they celebrated his Ballon d'Or win.

The England captain walked out onto the pitch and showcased the iconic golden ball to the crowd.

"I'm extremely proud to be a Bayern player," he said. "I hope we win many more titles together."

It was revealed on Friday that Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or ahead of Kylian Mbappe by just 28 points.



This is the fourth-closest voting gap in the prestigious award's 70-year history.

Kane is now the fifth Englishman to win the award after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer reveals he rejected EFL job before agreeing to become Match of the Day pundit
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer reveals he rejected EFL job before agreeing to become Match of the Day pundit

Alan Shearer has revealed he once turned down the chance to manage Cardiff City.

Shearer was interviewed by the Championship club after being relegated from the top-flight in 2009 as interim boss of Newcastle - his hometown club where he spent most of his playing career.

3 Shearer took interim charge of Newcastle for eight games 17 years ago, but was unable to save his beloved Magpies from relegation Credit: Getty

But the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer decided that he was done with management at that early stage, instead turning has hand to punditry with the BBC – most notably as a regular on Match of the Day.

Why did Shearer say no to Cardiff?

Explaining his decision to snub Cardiff, Shearer told the BBC: "Newcastle were in desperate trouble and I could never say no [to taking that job] – we were bottom of the league, fighting for our lives.

"I should have known that when I signed the contract on April Fool’s Day that it wasn’t going to work out!"

Following his brief spell in the St. James' Park dugout, Shearer was initially open to staying in management – but he ultimately changed his mind.

"I always felt that I was going to go into it again and I wanted to," he continued.

"I had a couple of interviews and got offered the job at Cardiff. And then things changed... and I thought, ‘What am I doing here?'"

Shearer stays loyal to Match of the Day

Shearer has now been part of the Match of the Day team for the best part of two decades, also working for the BBC on live coverage of the World Cup, FA Cup and more.

The 56-year-old also co-hosts The Rest Is Football alongside Match of the Day colleagues Gary Lineker and Micah Richards.

Lineker fronted Match of the Day when Shearer came onboard, but left the BBC last year.

Since Lineker's departure, the iconic Premier League highlights show has employed a rotating presenting line-up of Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan.

3 Among Shearer's fellow Match of the Day pundits is another legendary former Premier League striker, Wayne Rooney Credit: BBC

Shearer, who scored a record 260 Premier League goals for Blackburn and Newcastle, remains part of a refreshed punditry pool.

Former Tottenham boss Thomas Frank and ex-Manchester United full-back Ashley Young are among the new names involved for 2026/27.

However, the BBC have been warned to learn from the demise of Football Focus in order to ensure Match of the Day survives.

"I think, like every show in the world, if you don't have good talent on there, then you are not going to have a good product," said talkSPORT's Simon Jordan in August.

"Shearer's good. I think Wayne [Rooney] is getting much better. The digital landscape is, of course, undermining linear broadcasting.

"It is decimating linear broadcasting. And the figures that you get now of that once upon a time you'd turn on EastEnders and 20 million people would watch it, those days have gone.

3 Shearer remains the Premier League's all-time top scorer with 260 Premier League goals Credit: Getty

"But digital is still underpinned to some extent by the credibility of mainstream media.

"And so the good pundits that land in mainstream media and do digital as well will still want mainstream media to seed some of their credibility, viability, and validity so that they can do the digital stuff."

Sports.title: West Ham fans turn on Nuno Espirito Santo amid more Championship misery
Sports.content:
West Ham fans were heard chanting 'Sacked in the morning' to boss Nuno Espirito Santo during their 3-1 defeat to West Brom.

The Hammers have dropped to eighth in the Championship following a second consecutive defeat in England's second-tier.



3 West Ham fans turned on boss Espirito Santo as they fell to defeat at home against West Brom Credit: Getty

West Brom went ahead via Felix Horn Myhre with 20 minutes played, before Jarrod Bowen equalised with his seventh goal of the season.

But Jimmy-Jay Morgan and Callum Styles wrapped up the points for the visitors at the London Stadium to go fourth in the table.

Towards the end of the match, West Brom fans sang 'Sacked in the morning' to Espirito Santo, who used to manage their rivals Wolves.



They were joined by the home faithful, with West Ham supporters turning on their head coach for a second time this season.

Espirito Santo faced the same chant during a 1-1 draw with Watford in their third match of the season.



West Ham have now lost three of their seven home matches in the Championship this term.

What has been said about West Ham?

Speaking on talkSPORT commentary, Perry Groves stressed he doesn't believe the Hammers will achieve automatic promotion back to the top-flight.



He said: "This West Ham, I wouldn't say team now, a bunch of players.

"At the beginning of the season, you'd have said that they should be nailed on to being in the top two.

"You're looking at this, and yet the evidence we've seen in front of our eyes, is you would say that they have got no chance of being in the top two if they carry on like this, because it's just too disjointed."

3 West Brom leapfrogged West Ham into fourth with their away victory Credit: Getty

Groves later added: "The only reason I say that he's not under pressure is maybe the West Ham hierarchy and how much it will cost to get rid of him, obviously, with the compensation payment.



"So maybe because of his record in the Championship with Wolverhampton Wanderers, it might give him a bit of a say.

"But if they don't turn this around before the international break, that's when decisions could be made.

"And West Ham are just a team of individuals, you know you have the problem at Manchester United where the Manchester United players... the culture stinks.

"This is going towards that end because there was no urgency at all."

West Ham are now four points outside the top two in their bid to win instant promotion back to the Premier League.



3 Espirito Santo has called upon the West Ham fans to stick together amid their poor run of form Credit: Getty

They have two wins from their last six in the league and, speaking to talkSPORT after, Espirito Santo sent a message to the fans as he said: "We need to stick together.

"That's the only solution to go back to results, sticking together, helping each other, improving our game. If we do this, the fans are going to be with us."

Sports.title: Man United player ratings: 1/10 Lisandro Martinez must make public apology after unforgivable act of self-sabotage
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez was the first Manchester United player to break ranks on the club's shambolic hierarchy.

But at Stamford Bridge the hot-headed defender basically turned the gun on himself as United’s horror season took another negative turn, leaving Michael Carrick’s position hanging even more in the balance.

4 Lisandro Martinez was dismissed after receiving two bookings in 82 seconds Credit: Getty

Martinez's embarrassing afternoon

Martinez’s brainless decision to lead with his arm when trying to defend a cross and catching Wesley Fofana in the face was an unforgivable act of self-sabotage.

It is no secret Martinez wants out of United, and he should be made an example of now, not that their squad is exactly packed full of players to take his place after the board negligently opted against reinforcing that area of the squad in the summer.

Martinez had already been left embarrassed after allowing Morgan Rogers to waltz past him and dink the opening goal deftly over Senne Lammens as the United defence parted like the Red Sea.

Having been shown a second yellow card for his moment of madness the man affectionately known as ‘The Butcher’ by United fans completely lost his head and had to be escorted off the pitch by his teammates.

It was exactly the type of scene Carrick did not need at the start of a week that will surely break his career in the Old Trafford dugout.

Cole Palmer was never going to miss the penalty and at 2-0 down with ten men, United were never going to mount any kind of comeback.

The irony for Carrick is that his side were the more confident and cohesive team in the first half, producing arguably their best 45 minutes of a campaign that is unravelling at an alarming rate.

Carrick and Fernandes make amends

As expected, Carrick restored captain Bruno Fernandes to his starting 11 after they kissed and made up.

Fernandes was serenaded with chants of ‘Bruno, Bruno’ by the travelling fans during the pre-match warm-ups.

The Portuguese went about his task like he had a point to prove and bridges to build, leading the press that he had publicly complained was non-existent in the wake of the 4-1 drubbing at Como.

4 Bruno Fernandes was one of United's few bright sparks on another miserable afternoon Credit: Getty

He was also noticeably less theatrical than usual, getting straight back to his feet after being brought down by what he thought was a foul and encouraging rather than lambasting Amad Diallo when he opted to shoot rather than square the ball back to his skipper, who was in a better position.

Fernandes did balloon one glorious opportunity into the Matthew Harding stand after a rapid Red Devils counter-attack.

He then whipped a delicious ball across the six-yard box which narrowly evaded Bryan Mbuemo at the far post before playing in Amad with a sumptuous ball around the corner.

The only issue for Carrick, who interestingly did not appear on the edge of his technical area for the first 15 minutes of the contest, is that Amad has not scored since December and could not keep his shot down.

United fans make their feelings clear once again

Nonetheless the travelling hordes were clearly buoyed by a much-improved performance from their team and did not pass up the opportunity to make it clear who they blamed for the mess their beloved club are in.

‘You can stick your new stadium up your arse’ and ‘sell United f*ck off home’ were just two of the songs they serenaded Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers with.

4 Carrick is surely on borrowed time at United Credit: AFP

Sporting director Jason Wilcox also did not escape their ire, while Carrick himself was once again serenaded positively.

Carrick sent his players out early for the second half, presumably on the back of words of encouragement over what he had witnessed.

However, there was always a suspicion they would pay for those spurned opportunities and so it proved as Chelsea scored twice in 14 minutes to win the game.

By the end of the game that extended United’s winless run to nine games, the home fans were taunting Carrick with cries of ‘we want you to stay.’

4

The end for Carrick?

The United boss surely needs positive results at home to Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and when Aston Villa visit in the league next Sunday or you fear his position becomes untenable.

But it is Martinez who should be making another grovelling public apology for letting his manager, teammates and the fans down.

Sports.title: Man United set horror 38-year record as pressure piles on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Manchester United made it nine matches without a win for the first time since 1988 as they suffered a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

Undone by a flash of genius and moment of stupidity, the loss leaves United boss Michael Carrick clinging to his job despite overseeing an encouraging opening half by his team.



4 A moment of magic from Morgan Rogers set Chelsea on their way to a crucial three points Credit: Getty

United, who saw a first-half goal from Matheus Cunha chalked off for offside, wasted a hatful of chances with Amad Diallo guilty of two gilt-edged misses.

At the other end, Estevao, handed his first Premier League start of the season, also saw his effort ruled out.

Pedro Neto dragged his close-range effort wide as the half drew to a close.



The game sprang to life in a frantic 13-minutes period early in the second half.

4 This is Man United's longest winless run in 38 years



A moment of brilliance

A wonderful solo run and finish from Morgan Rogers fired Xabi Alonso’s side in front.

The England international continued his excellent start to the season with his sixth goal in 12 games for the Blues.



If Carrick’s side didn’t already have a mountain to climb then their cause was made even harder when Lisandro Martinez was given his marching orders shortly after the hour.

Initially booked in the 59th minute, the Argentine was brandished a second yellow card for an inexplicable elbow on Chelsea’s Wesley Fofana just 82 seconds later.

Carrick, staring at yet another defeat, opted not to feast his eyes on Martinez as he trudged down the Stamford Bridge tunnel.

talkSPORT's Stuart Pearce who was at Stamford Bridge on commentary duties was less than impressed by the World Cup winner's actions.



4 Lisandro Martinez was dismissed after receiving two bookings in 82 seconds Credit: Getty

Pearce said: "He's lost his head. He's just making rash decisions. Since the (Rogers) goal, Martinez's performance has been absolutely shocking.

"I'm not sure I've seen a worse 20 minutes from a player."

United’s second-half implosion was then capped off when Cole Palmer converted the resulting penalty to see off the Red Devils.

Carrick’s side were given a reprieve when Estevao saw yet another expertly-taken finish ruled out for offside.



Despite yet another game without a win and further doom and gloom clouding the Old Trafford club, fans remained in full voice until the final whistle.

Unwanted record

The defeat sees United reach an unwanted 38-year record sparked by their startling winless run.

4 Carrick cut a forlorn figure in the Man United dugout Credit: Getty

The club’s nine matches without victory equals a similar run under Sir Alex Ferguson in 1988.



And it is a run that could be further extended over the next week with the vist of in-form Serie A side Roma in the Champions League in midweek.

Then, Aston Villa head to Old Trafford next Sunday in a pivotal Premier League clash.

United provisionally sit 16th in the table but could end the weekend in the bottom three if results go against them.

For Carrick, his race may well be run in the Old Trafford dugout but not in the hearts of the travelling support who let the under pressure manager know just where their loyalties lie.



And Carrick took the time to acknowledge the United faithful.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he said: "The supporters have been absolutely amazing. I know they have been, but it really does get tested when you're not winning enough football matches. For them to support us like they did today and stay strong just shows what they're all about. They're desperate; they want to be there; they want to keep driving us on.



"As a group, we've got to give them more to go on. I think the first half, there was a lot there for them to enjoy and to support and get behind. Again, we all feel disappointed with the end result, but they're there. They're always there and I fully appreciate everything they gave us."

On another disappointing afternoon for his side, Carrick reflected: "It was a total game of two halves. I think the first half was as good as we've been for quite some time. It looked dangerous, looked fluid. We had chances, had massive chances, could have had other chances with some of the play that we had with the final ball.



"Normally they go in; we expect them to go in at the moment. Obviously, it didn't go in. Then the second half, it just changed. Them scoring so quickly after half-time, it changes the dynamics. It's something you've got to deal with...You've got to manage the moments. The game got away from us in the end, in the second half.

It's two extreme halves of football, really."

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez gets cold shoulder from Michael Carrick after generational head-loss at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez gets cold shoulder from Michael Carrick after generational head-loss at Chelsea

Lisandro Martinez was ignored by Manchester United boss Michael Carrick after getting two yellow cards in 82 seconds against Chelsea.

The defender received his marching orders in a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge after a brainless shove on Wesley Fofana which resulted in a Chelsea penalty.

2 Carrick refused to acknowledge Martinez on his way down the tunnel Credit: AFP

Cole Palmer dispatched the spot-kick to put the Blues 2-0 up, with Morgan Rogers having broken the deadlock early in the second half.

Rogers breezed past Martinez for the goal – and forced the Argentina defender into a clumsy challenge for his first yellow card.

It left Man United heading for yet another defeat amid already intense pressure on Carrick, who appeared to blank Martinez as he headed off down the tunnel.

Carrick was backed by the board ahead of the trip to London, but time is ticking on his time in the dugout.

Martinez in hot water again

The costly red card comes weeks after Martinez called out the United hierarchy in a bombshell interview.

Martinez's dismissal came moments after talkSPORT's Stuart Pearce had slammed his second-half display.

"Martinez has lost his head, he's making some incredible rash decisions," the legendary former England defender said.

Speaking after the red card, Pearce added: "I'm not sure I've seen a worse 20 minutes from a player."

Is Martinez's United career over?

Ex-Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole, commentating on the game for TNT Sports, went as far to suggest Martinez's United days are numbered.

"Martinez, it's run its course," he said. "In a Manchester United shirt, he's at the scene of the crime too often, so I think that's probably his time done."

2 Martinez inexplicably shoved Fofana off the ball

It's the second time the 28-year-old Argentina international has been sent off since joining United from Ajax four years ago.

Martinez was also dismissed in a 2-1 home loss to Leeds back in April.

His latest indiscretion was emblematic of United's current plight.

The 13-time Premier League champions have won just one of their opening nine league games this season, losing four.

As such, they find themselves hovering just a point above the relegation zone.

United are also winless in nine matches in all competitions, losing four of their last five, including a humbling 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como – after which captain Bruno Fernandes publicly criticised Carrick's tactics, resulting in his being dropped for last weekend's home loss to Bournemouth.

And while fans continue to protest against the club's owners, the person who will likely ultimately pay the price is Carrick himself.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes holds back TEARS after Man United beaten by Chelsea: Captain appears emotional as return to squad after public criticism of Michael Carrick ends in defeat
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to be on the verge of tears as he embraced the travelling faithful following his side's latest defeat. Fernandes returned to the United side after being dropped for their loss against Bournemouth last week, when he was an unused substitute. The decision from Michael Carrick came after his skipper had criticised Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, leading to uncertainty around the duo's relationship. In the week, however, they held crisis talks to fix their relationship, and Fernandes was back in the team – and playing 90 minutes – against Chelsea on Saturday. Yet he was unable to turn around his side's fortunes, with United falling to a 2-0 defeat, and the club have now gone nine games in all competitions without a win. And he appeared to be in a battle to hold back the tears as United's players headed over to the away end at full-time, showing how much the team's poor form is affecting him. A visibly emotional Bruno Fernandes after another disappointing result for Man Utd 💔 pic.twitter.com/E4MhUoD8VW — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 31, 2026 Bruno Fernandes appeared to be fighting back the tears following Manchester United's defeat by Chelsea Carrick has made a habit of applauding the fans first after the game, and was cheered off following the Bournemouth defeat before those in attendance turned on the players. On this occasion, Carrick again walked down the tunnel without his players, but the team were in fact cheered. Fernandes was stood alone, and repeatedly wiped his face as he took in the situation. 'He's a big player, Bruno,' Carrick said after the game. 'He offers us so much, you know, with his experience. 'He's been through a lot here and achieved a lot and shown what he can bring to the team. 'So he's an important part of the team for us and I think we've got a good balance today. We've got a good team and the boys are looking forward to it.'
