World.title: El mensaje del Papa emociona a los asistentes al funeral por las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de Urda
World.content:
El arzobispo de Toledo preside la misa por los fallecidos, mientras decenas de vecinos siguen la ceremonia desde fuera de la iglesia

Los vecinos de Urda se han emocionado este sábado al escuchar, al final de la misa funeral por los fallecidos en el accidente ferroviario, la carta que el papa León XIV había enviado a las víctimas. La iglesia parroquial de San Juan Bautista se ha quedado pequeña y quienes no han podido entrar han seguido la ceremonia desde fuera. El arzobispo de Toledo, Francisco Cerro Chaves, ha destacado el consuelo que han encontrado en las palabras del pontífice: “Nos ha llenado el corazón de esperanza”. La misa funeral de este sábado ha sido organizada por la Archidiócesis de Toledo, con la participación de las parroquias de Urda y Los Yébenes, y presidida por el arzobispo Francisco Cerro Chaves. Más adelante se celebrará un funeral oficial en la catedral de Toledo.

Cerro ha empezado a leer la carta: “El Papa León XIV, vivamente apenado al conocer la dolorosa noticia del trágico accidente ferroviario ocurrido en la localidad de Urda, Toledo, ofrece sufragios por el eterno descanso de los difuntos. Asimismo, el Santo Padre ha hecho llegar su sentido pésame a los familiares de los fallecidos, “junto con sus expresiones de consuelo, viva solicitud y deseos de pronto restablecimiento de los heridos”. Su Santidad, a la vez que ha animado a los miembros de los equipos de rescate a perseverar en los trabajos de socorro y asistencia, les imparte a todos de corazón la confortadora bendición apostólica, como signo de esperanza en el Señor resucitado”, ha leído el obispo auxiliar de Toledo, Francisco César García Magán. El mensaje está dirigido al arzobispo y firmado por el cardenal Pietro Parolin, secretario de Estado.

Cerro Chaves ha explicado, además, que han recibido condolencias de distintos lugares del mundo, pero ha destacado especialmente el mensaje del papa, que le ha sorprendido “muchísimo”. “Se ve que tiene una sensibilidad tan grande con el mundo del dolor y del sufrimiento”, ha señalado.

El presidente de Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, en la misa por las víctimas del accidente ferroviario en Urda (Toledo). Victor Sainz

Este sábado por la mañana, los vecinos se han acercado a la parroquia con sus mejores galas. Había mayores, jóvenes y niños. Bajo el sol, los asistentes se agrupaban junto a la fachada de piedra, ocupaban los escalones y se sentaban en el murete de la entrada. Entre los asistentes estaba Antonio García Condado, farmacéutico de Urda, que el día del accidente dejó el desayuno tras recibir la llamada de su hija y condujo hasta la zona cero. Después regresó a la farmacia para recoger medicamentos y material con el que volvió a ayudar. De aquellas horas quiere conservar el recuerdo de un herido al que acompañó mientras se despedía de su familia: al día siguiente, su mujer Maite lo llamó para contarle que seguía vivo. “A mí me reportó un entusiasmo que no te puedes imaginar”, recuerda. Este sábado ha asistido a la misa con tristeza por los fallecidos y con el deseo de que sirva de consuelo a sus familias.

Durante la homilía, Cerro Chaves se ha dirigido a las familias de las víctimas: “No tenemos palabras que puedan llenar el vacío de una ausencia tan dolorosa”. También ha pedido a quienes tienen responsabilidades en la seguridad de los transportes que trabajen con diligencia, buscando la verdad, la justicia y la protección de la vida humana para evitar que se repitan tragedias como esta.

A la entrada de la misa, el alcalde de Urda, Manuel Galán, ha dicho que es un día “de dolor” y de reconocimiento a quienes están sufriendo y a las familias de los fallecidos". También ha pedido una oración por los hospitalizados: “Para que se curen, para que se sanen, para que de la forma más rápida y de lo mejor posible puedan estar con sus familias”.

Galán ha dicho que este viernes pudo hablar con los vecinos para conocer cómo se encontraban. “El pueblo está muy dolorido, está muy dañado psicológicamente, necesita apoyo”, ha señalado. El regidor ha agradecido a los medios que les ayuden a expresar lo vivido: “Todo ese dolor lo sacan y les ayuda a ir pasando los días y a pasar ese dolor que ellos tienen interiorizado”.

El arzobispo de Toledo, Francisco Cerro, durante la misa por las víctimas del accidente ferroviario, este sábado en Urda. Victor Sainz

Antes de entrar en la iglesia, el presidente de Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, ha informado de que continúan las altas hospitalarias. En la comunidad permanecen ingresadas 34 personas, 15 de ellas en la UCI. “Evolucionan razonablemente bien”, ha señalado.

García-Page ha confirmado que el balance de fallecidos se mantiene en 69, incluidos quienes se encuentran en depósito y la persona que murió en un hospital. Ha explicado que las notificaciones se realizan bajo la coordinación de la autoridad judicial forense y de la Guardia Civil, con un protocolo “enormemente estricto” y “dobles pruebas de verificación”.

“Sé que es tremendo porque todos quisiéramos que pudieran descansar también las familias cuanto antes, pero es la autoridad judicial y es la ley”, ha añadido. También ha contado que los hospitales de Castilla-La Mancha han atendido a personas de nueve nacionalidades y que en los dos trenes viajaban pasajeros de hasta 27 nacionalidades distintas.

El presidente autonómico ha explicado, además, que están en contacto con la autoridad judicial para habilitar, si fuera necesario, iluminación durante la tarde y la noche que permita continuar los trabajos de búsqueda y la recogida de datos periciales. “Estamos bajo su coordinación”, ha señalado.

La vicesecretaria de Sanidad y Política Social del PP, Carmen Fúnez, ha trasladado, también a la entrada del funeral, su apoyo a las familias de los fallecidos, a los hospitalizados y a quienes todavía no han encontrado a sus seres queridos. “Son ellos el foco, el objetivo y el porqué hoy estamos aquí”, ha declarado.

“Hoy venimos a esta misa a rezar, a recordar y a transmitirles todo nuestro apoyo, todo nuestro cariño y toda la solidaridad posible a esas familias que han perdido a una persona, que han perdido a un ser querido”, ha afirmado. También ha expresado sus deseos de recuperación para quienes siguen ingresados.

Vecinos de Urda (Toledo) tras asistir a la misa en recuerdo a las víctimas del accidente ferroviario. Victor Sainz

Al concluir el funeral, Cerro Chaves ha dejado junto al Cristo el báculo que le regaló el pueblo de Urda con motivo de la concesión del título de basílica al templo de la imagen. “Muy sencillo, de madera y plateado”, ha explicado.

Los asistentes han formado una fila entre los bancos para acercarse al Cristo de Urda que ha sido trasladado desde su basílica hasta la parroquia para presidir el funeral. A sus pies había rosas amarillas y rosadas, una por cada fallecido. Uno tras otro, los vecinos pasaban junto a la proa y extendían la mano para tocar la cabeza del ángel.

“Eso es un poco la devoción que hay en este pueblo al Cristo, por eso están pasando todos”, ha explicado el arzobispo. En las fiestas del Cristo de Urda, ha contado, los fieles forman largas colas para besar la barca o acercarse al cordón de la imagen. Es una forma de decirle: “Oye, acuérdate de que lo estamos pasando muy mal”.

World.title: La carta de Sheila a su madre, víctima del accidente de tren: “No sé ser tú, mamá. No sé cómo se sostiene todo sin ti”
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

La joven, de 31 años, despide a Toñi Barba, una de las 69 víctimas mortales del siniestro, en una carta en la que también habla del dolor de su padre, que viajaba junto a ella

Han pasado apenas 24 horas desde que una llamada partió en dos la vida de Sheila Chao Barba. Su madre, Toñi Barba, es una de las 69 víctimas mortales del accidente ferroviario ocurrido en Toledo. Viajaba en el vagón 7 del AVE rumbo a Sevilla junto a su marido, Antonio Chao. Sus hijas les habían regalado una escapada de un par de días a la capital andaluza. Una de ellas los había despedido esa misma mañana en la estación de Atocha. Poco después, empezó a recibir en el grupo familiar de WhatsApp las fotografías que sus padres enviaban desde el tren. Al llegar a casa, la noticia del accidente lo cambió todo.

Toñi y Antonio viajaban juntos cuando sintieron un golpe seco. El vagón se deslizó por el terraplén y, al recuperar la consciencia, se encontraron rodeados de hierros, desconcierto y caos. Antonio sintió que el techo iba a ceder e intentó proteger a su mujer cubriéndola con los brazos. Quiso abrazarla, hacer de escudo con su propio cuerpo, pero las extremidades no le respondían. Después, el destino de ambos se separó. A Antonio lo trasladaron en ambulancia al Hospital Universitario de Toledo. De Toñi, en cambio, no hubo noticias durante un día entero. Fueron 24 horas de espera, de llamadas y de incertidumbre para una familia que todavía no sabía que tendría que aprender a despedirse.

Esta es la carta que Sheila, de 31 años, escribe a su madre horas después de aquel viaje que nunca debió terminar en despedida:

Sheila Chao junto a su madre Toñi Barba, en un selfie tomado por ella misma. Foto cedida por la familia.

“No sé qué hacer con todos los días que nos quedaban juntas. Ni cómo se vuelve a casa cuando el mundo se ha terminado y fuera la gente sigue viviendo como si nada.

Pero papá…

Joder, mamá. Papá.

Porque nosotros hemos perdido a nuestra madre, pero él ha perdido su vida entera. Su casa, su compañera, su niña. Y hasta en aquel tren, mamá, hasta cuando todo se venía abajo, él solo pensaba en ti. Hizo todo lo que pudo por protegerte. Pidió que te sacaran antes que a él. Porque incluso estando herido, incluso sin saber qué iba a pasar, seguías siendo tú lo primero y en lo único que pensaba. Qué manera tan brutal de querer a alguien. Y qué injusticia que un amor así no haya podido salvarte.

No sé cómo se le explica a un hombre que tiene que seguir viviendo cuando se le ha ido la persona que le daba el motivo para vivir.

¿Cómo se supera eso, mamá? ¿Cómo se le pide que sea fuerte si lo que le daba fuerzas eras tú?

Papá va a recuperarse, te lo prometo mamá. Voy a estar a su lado. Y voy a cuidar de Cris, voy a abrazarla cuando te necesite, aunque yo también esté buscándote.

No sé ser tú, mamá. No sé cómo se sostiene todo esto sin ti. Y tengo un miedo terrible.

Vamos a volver a reír, mamá.

No sé cuándo.

Ni sé cómo.

Pero vamos a hacerlo por ti.

Ojalá todo el mundo pudiera ver que mis padres se quisieron de una manera que algunos no llegarían a conocer ni viviendo cien años. Que ni siquiera en el peor momento papá dejó de elegirte. Y que ahora nos toca a nosotras enseñarle a vivir sin ti, cuando ni siquiera nosotras sabemos si podremos hacerlo.

No sé qué voy a hacer con tu ausencia. Pero sí sé qué voy a hacer con tu amor. Voy a gastarlo en cuidar de los nuestros. Y cuando nadie me vea, voy a seguir siendo tu niña, la que todavía necesita que su madre le diga que todo va a salir bien.

Más te quiero yo, mamá.

Y me lo estoy callando".

World.title: La operación policial contra Blocus acumula dos encarcelados y un menor detenido en Valencia
World.content:
La operación policial contra Blocus acumula dos encarcelados y un menor arrestado en Valencia, además de otro joven detenido en Barcelona. Un juzgado de Catarroja ha decretado este sábado el ingreso en prisión provisional, comunicada y sin fianza para un detenido en Alfafar (Valencia) por su supuesta integración o relación con este movimiento. El detenido queda investigado por un delito de pertenencia a grupo criminal orientado a la movilización o inducción a terceros para la comisión de delitos de desórdenes públicos y robos.

Además, un juzgado de Torrent (Valencia) ha decretado también el ingreso en prisión provisional y sin fianza para el considerado como “fundador e impulsor” de Blocus España, un joven de 20 años detenido este viernes en la localidad valenciana de Picanya. Él mismo se autoproclamaba el fundador de este movimiento surgido en Francia, que emplea las redes sociales para convocar a sus seguidores, jóvenes algunos de ellos menores de edad, para citas y quedadas que derivan en saqueos de comercios y actos vandálicos en la ciudad.

Esa segunda prisión preventiva tiene el carácter de comunicada, excepto en lo que concierne al acceso a los ordenadores o cualquier otro tipo de dispositivo en el centro penitenciario que le permita acceder a redes sociales de cualquier clase, según ha informado el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de la Comunitat Valenciana (TSJCV). El detenido está investigado en una causa abierta por delitos de organización criminal destinada a la incitación para cometer desórdenes públicos, robos con fuerza en comercios y daños, sin perjuicio de ulterior calificación.

La captación del supuesto líder comenzaba con vídeos en TikTok y carteles, elaborados con carteles de inteligencia artificial y códigos QR, desde donde los interesados eran derivados a grupos de WhatsApp y Telegram y, posteriormente, a canales privados. Según las pesquisas de la Guardia Civil, los organizadores pedían difundir los enlaces en grupos de clase y otros espacios del entorno escolar, lo que facilitaba la llegada de las convocatorias a menores de edad. Los mensajes indicaban acudir con mochilas, material escolar y pancartas para aparentar una reivindicación estudiantil, pero también vestir ropa negra y máscaras para dificultar la identificación.

Además, la Policía Nacional y la Guardia Civil han detenido en los últimos días a más personas relacionadas con las convocatorias para provocar disturbios, saqueos y pillaje este sábado, entre ellos este joven, considerado como “fundador e impulsor” de Blocus España, y un menor de Valencia encausado por la distribución de mensajes para entrar en chats del movimiento utilizados para coordinar disturbios. En total, hay 10 detenidos en España desde el miércoles vinculados con Blocus.

En Cataluña, los Mossos d’Esquadra han detenido este sábado al mediodía en Cabrera d’Anoia (Barcelona), un hombre de 21 años por su presunta relación con el canal Blocus y con la coordinación de los actos vandálicos registrados en Barcelona el pasado 24 de octubre. Según la investigación, la persona detenida era administradora de uno de los grupos de comunicación que se creó para facilitar la organización de los disturbios y la coordinación de los participantes.

Los Mossos detallan que el acceso a este grupo se habría promocionado mediante la difusión de un cartel en la red social TikTok que incorporaba un código QR con acceso directo en un canal de WhatsApp.

Este sábado, la detención se ha producido en Cabrera d’Anoia, en el marco de la investigación abierta para determinar las responsabilidades de las personas que habrían participado en la planificación, coordinación y difusión de las convocatorias vinculadas a los saqueos y disturbios.

Las indagaciones también han permitido determinar que el detenido habría tenido una participación activa en la dinamización del grupo y que se encontraba en Barcelona durante el desarrollo de los saqueos.

Además, la sección de menores de Barcelona ha acordado este sábado el internamiento en régimen cerrado para el menor detenido en Sant Sadurní d’Anoia (Barcelona) por su presunta vinculación con los disturbios del sábado pasado en el centro de la capital catalana, impulsados por el grupo ‘Blocus’. La decisión se ha tomado tras practicar distintas diligencias, ha informado el TSJC en una publicación en ‘X’ recogida por Europa Press. El arresto de este menor de 17 años tuvo lugar el jueves, el mismo día en en que los agentes detuvieron en Bellmunt d’Urgell (Lleida) a otro joven de 16 años, señalado por los investigadores como el presunto creador y administrador de uno de los principales canales de mensajería utilizados para coordinar las movilizaciones.

World.title: El despliegue policial por Blocus acumula un millar de identificados en Barcelona
World.content:
Los Mossos d’Esquadra han desplegado este sábado por la tarde un dispositivo de máximos para evitar una nueva oleada de altercados en el centro de Barcelona. En coordinación con la Guardia Urbana, los agentes han saturado con uniformados y policías de paisano zonas como el Passeig de Gràcia, con el objetivo de identificar a jóvenes y, en algunos casos, registrar mochilas y chaquetas en busca de objetos que puedan utilizarse en saqueos. En total, un millar de identificaciones en una jornada sin incidentes destacables pero que era la respuesta preventiva ante las convocatorias Blocus previstas para este sábado. Además, han detectado a 12 menores en riesgo, porque llevaban elementos como pasamontañas, y los han trasladado a comisaría como medida de “protección”, a la espera de ser recogidos por sus padres. La principal preocupación de los Mossos se centraba Barcelona, donde han coexistido tres convocatorias, en la plaza de Cataluña, en la Pedrera y en Arc de Triomf. A última hora también han aparecido en las redes menciones a Les Glòries o la plaza de Urquinaona. A pesar de eso, los Mossos han detectado escasa actividad en los grupos, de los que muchas personas han salido, o que directamente Telegram ha clausurado.

Este sábado, a las cuatro de la tarde, el Passeig de Gràcia, uno de los principales ejes comerciales de la ciudad, era un hervidero de gente arriba y abajo. Una postal habitual un fin de semana en Barcelona, con la particularidad de que la mayoría de las tiendas están blindadas. Sus escaparates acristalados están tapados con conglomerados de madera y planchas de cartón prensado. Algunas incluso con protecciones metálicas, como el supermercado Aldi, en la Gran Vía, que ha decidido cerrar a las dos de la tarde, ante la posibilidad de que se puedan repetir los disturbios de la semana pasada.

Agentes de los Mossos piden la identificacion a varios jóvenes en Barcelona. Carles Ribas

Pero la mayoría de los comercios han continuado abiertos, por lo menos hasta media tarde. Los Mossos d’Esquadra han desplegado un dispositivo policial masivo ante la posibilidad de que, de nuevo, se repita la reunión de jóvenes en el centro de la ciudad con el único objetivo de cometer robos y saqueos. El sábado pasado, 24 de octubre, la policía catalana se vio sorprendida por la violencia de unos chavales, muchos menores de edad, que, sin mediar protesta previa, se lanzaron a romper escaparates y robar tiendas. La jornada se saldó con 133 detenidos, 89 de los cuales eran menores de edad. La Fiscalía ha soliciado 70 medidas de alejamiento para esos menores y el internamiento de ocho de ellos.

Pero Barcelona no ha sido la única ciudad bajo la mirada policial. En redes, se ha difundido un centenar de carteles que llamaban a repetir los saqueos de Barcelona en una decena de puntos más: Lleida, Badalona, Igualada, Mataró, Girona, Terrassa, Gavà, Figueres o Castell-Platja d’Aro. Los Mossos se han desplegado también en esos municipios, aunque la evaluación del riesgo que ha llevado a cabo la policía ha otorgado un nivel de menor conflictividad a esas posibles concentraciones. A primera hora de la noche, no se habían registrado incidentes en ningún punto.

El centro de coordinación central de los Mossos (CECOR) ha reunido a los altos mandos del cuerpo en su sede central, en Sabadell, a partir de las cuatro de la tarde. Además, se han activado también centros de coordinación regionales para cada una de las regiones que estaban bajo el radar ante posibles convocatorias Blocus.

La judicatura también ha estado en alerta ante la evolución de la jornada y contaba con la posibilidad de incrementar sus efectivos. Asimismo, el colegio de abogados ha activado 15 letrados más del turno de oficio por si, como ocurrió la semana pasada, existía un gran número de detenidos. A las nueve de la noche, constaban cuatro arrestos de los Mossos en Barcelona, no vinculados con Blocus. Los Mossos han activado su nivel 4 para las convocatorias en la capital catalana, un tecnicismo policial que evalúa el posible riesgo de una protesta en una escala del 1 al 4. Eso supone, en su lenguaje, que se prevé una “manifestación combativa”. La última vez que se decretó ese nivel fue en 2021, durante las protestas por el encarcelamiento del rapero Pablo Hasél.

World.title: From pickles to magic: 11 great things to do in November
World.content:
It’s November, the quiet before the Christmas cheer storm. But there’s still much non-festive fun to be had, as the list will show.

Make a night of it

It’s Museumnacht in Amsterdam this month. Some 65 museums are keeping their doors open and there is a raft of night-time activities, including Ask an Imam where visitors can discuss matters of faith, a trip on a boat used by refugees, and many more. November 7. Website

Spot the differences

The Frans Hals Museum in Haarlem is planning its own blockbuster exhibition with the succinctly named Hals-Rembrandt, which focuses on the differences and similarities in the styles of the two Dutch 17th-century masters. The museum will open earlier and use time slots to give visitors the opportunity for a proper gaze at the juxtaposed works. From November 6. Website

See ancient Egypt come to life

The Olympisch Stadion in Amsterdam is hosting Tutankhamun – the immersive exhibition, where VR wizardry takes you to the heart of ancient Egypt without getting sand between your toes. It’s a pretty amazing spectacle and children will love it too. From November 6. Website

Spare five minutes

The Orange Theatre Company presents a series of five-minute English language monologues around the theme ‘In the Flesh’ as part of its Tiny Theatre programme. It’s all about desire, so it might get a bit steamy in the Oedipus Brewery in Amsterdam. November 11. Website

Get into a pickle

It’s American Pickle Day on November 14 and Amsterdam, like New York, a traditional pickle city, is getting in on the act. A Big Dill celebrates that history with an exhibition of pickle paintings by New York painter Harvey Herman, himself a member of the Tannenbaum pickle family and a former seller of “pickles for a nickel”, pickle history from both cities and, of course, pickle tastings. It’s on at the st-Art Centre in Amsterdam-West. November 14. Website

Praat Nederlands

People from the Leiden region are invited to join fellow expats/immigrants/internationals struggling to learn the language and speak Dutch all day long. Practise Dutch in “a safe space” to boost your confidence and meet like-minded folk to have a good moan about the pitfalls of this wonderful and useful language. There are activities as well. November 26. Website

Catch Shrek in Amsterdam

Grab your chance to take the nippers to Shrek The Musical, the jolly story of the ogre, the princess and the talking donkey. It’s on at the Amsterdams Theaterhuis and we are including the December dates in case you want to avoid the December festive reservation surge. It’s in English, by the way. November 27-29, December 3-6. Website

Say hi to the Sint at Soestdijk

Sinterklaas is always met with a warm welcome in the Netherlands and that includes a well-deserved stay at the sumptuous, former royal palace Paleis Soestdijk. The Sint will not just be luxuriating in a royal bathtub, of course. The Blue Corridor (the former royal residence) has been turned into a Pieten Palace where Pieten are busy sorting out the presents and poems for December 5. Sinterklaas will make time for children wanting to see him, and they can even take a peek at his bedroom and do lots of activities. Children can bring a drawing to butter the Sint up. November 27, 28, 29. Website

See the seedy side of the Herengracht

The opulence of the houses on Amsterdam’s Herengracht finds its origin in the slave trade. Number 605, now the Willet-Holthuysen museum, named after its last owners who left the double canal house and its contents to the city, is a good example. Previous owners financier Willem Deutz (1697-1757) and merchant Fredrik Berewout (1692-1777) grew massively rich on the profits made from the slave trade, as the current exhibition Plantation along the Canal makes clear. Among the exhibits is a complete inventory of the Jagtlust plantation in Suriname, owned by Berewout, including the names and value of 125 slaves. Until April 4. Website

Find out how it’s done

Abracadabra, at the Jewish Museum in Amsterdam, is a fascinating look at the world of Jewish illusionists around 1900. The “Golden Age of Magic” included such famous names as escape artist Harry Houdini, and Horace Goldin and Okito (the stage name of Dutch magician Theo Bamberg) among others. World-renowned Dutch illusionist and collector Hans Klok became the chosen recipient of Bamberg’s tricks of the trade and decided to share them with the world, along with other magicians’ lore. Klok himself puts in an appearance on video to explain some of the tricks and visitors are invited to have a go as well. Until March 29, 2027. Website

Mind your ankles

Yay! Get your platform shoes on and dance to the music of the 70s at the Wereldmuseum in Amsterdam. There is much more to disco than glitter and glam. Its history is tied up with the emancipation of gays, queers, Latinos and other marginalised groups who created their own fabulous world of music and art. You can bop your way through hundreds of disco tracks, videos, artworks, fashion pieces and design objects, including works by Andy Warhol, Keith Haring, Kwame Brathwaite, Michael Abramson, Meryl Meisler and many others. Until August 22, 2027. Website

World.title: Fears spread over Gen Z riot plans across NL
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

There are fears that a “Gen Z” protest, inspired by the ongoing unrest that has swept through France and other countries, could hit the Netherlands over the weekend.

A report in AD found that groups on Telegram, Snapchat and other social media platforms are preparing to riot in cities including The Hague, Maastricht and Eindhoven.

While no applications for protest permits have been submitted, police have said they generally monitor online forums for signs of trouble but would not comment on this matter specifically.

The messages, which include calls to loot shopping centres, were enough to prompt school heads to issue warnings to parents in Maastricht. Limburg police backed the warnings, according to local broadcaster L1 News.

Shopkeepers in The Hague have also started boarding up their windows as a precaution, as some messaging groups are calling for gatherings on the Malieveld and attacks on commercial centres nearby, according to Omroep West.

The protests in France, which have spread to Italy and Spain began over education and living standards among young people. Many of the demonstrations quickly descended into serious rioting, often with heavy police response.

There are similar concerns in Germany, where youth groups are preparing to protest over similar issues on Halloween.

World.title: “No movement” in cabinet talks amid left-right stalemate
World.content:
The cabinet’s attempt to win over left- and right-wing opposition parties in its ongoing tax plan talks failed again on Friday.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and other senior ministers met opposition leaders a day after three right-wing parties, the far-right JA21, orthodox Protestant SGP and farmer-citizen movement BBB, banded together to push their demands as a single bloc. The demands range from harsher asylum measures and changes to abortion rules to scrapping a tax rise to pay for defence.

The move was the latest attempt by the opposition to force the cabinet to pick a side. Opposition parties have said for weeks that the cabinet will never get a broad agreement, because the two sides of the aisle have incompatible demands.

The offer presented on Friday covered how to pay for changes to box 3, the tax on savings and investments, without raising taxes on wealth, sources told the Telegraaf.

The cabinet would use money left over from a fund to refund people who were overtaxed under box 3 in past years, and cut taxes for business owners who pay themselves profits from their own companies. It would also keep a tax deduction for healthcare costs that was due to be scrapped in 2028.

Regardless of the offer, the stalemate appears to continue. Centre-left PRO leader Jesse Klaver said he saw “no movement at all” on his party’s demand for higher taxes on the wealthy and lower taxes on workers.

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans called it “a tough, complicated conversation”, but said the new right-wing alliance remained intact.

The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA does not have a majority, so it needs support from opposition parties to get its tax plan through parliament.

World.title: Government seeks to ban smoking where children congregate
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet wants to prohibit smoking at locations dominated by children, including petting zoos and after-school and other managed playgrounds.

Sources told broadcaster NOS the proposed ban will be discussed at Friday’s Council of Ministers.

While most such places are already smoke-free, the government wants to ensure that the remaining few ban smoking. The House of Representatives also supports the ban and wanted to extend it to other kid-friendly locations like zoos and amusement parks.

That may come in the future, along with bans at unattended playgrounds and outdoor swimming pools, but for now, the government will focus on managed playgrounds and day care centres where there is wide support for the plan.

The ban is part of the government’s efforts to have a smoke-free generation by 2040. Measures already in place include a display ban, unattractive packaging and fewer locations to purchase cigarettes.

World.title: Herman Brood painting added to national art collection
World.content:
A painting by rock legend and artist Herman Brood has been added to the National Collection, placing Brood in the company of Dutch icons such as Rembrandt, Ferdinand Bol, Piet Mondriaan and Karel Appel.

“We believe that Herman Brood should be given more prestige as an icon of the twentieth century as an artist,” said the cultural heritage anency (RCE).

The untitled acrylic work, made with an ever-present injection syringe and paint rollers, features two men with a pistol. It has been hanging on the wall of the tax office in The Hague but was moved earlier this week to the RCE’s depot in Amersfoort, where it’s been given the name “rock-‘n-roll on canvas”.

The inclusion of the work in the 120,000-strong national collection is official recognition that Brood has contributed substantially to Dutch culture and history. The work will be preserved permenantly and can be lent to museums.

“Junkie who painted”

Rob Dupré, a friend of “The Never Be Clever” and “Saturday Night” singer who died in 2001, told broadcaster NOS that Brood would rise from the dead if he heard the news.

“In life, he was seen as a rock ‘n’ roll singer who worked as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if everyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympics,” said Dupré, who works to detect counterfeits attributed to the artist.

It’s thought the painting ended up in the tax office to pay off a debt. “He didn’t do receipts and that kind of civil matter,” Dupré said. “He painted five paintings and then spent them on alcohol, drugs and women. He wasn’t really businesslike.”

As to the painting now part of the Rijks collection, Dupré says: “Have you ever had an envelope from the Tax and Customs Administration?… He deliberately painted those two people’s sweaters in exactly the same colour.”

As for the gun? “Everyone would want to have that in their hand when you get a tax assessment, right?” Dupré told AD.

Great honour

“He would have thought this was a great honour,” Brood’s wife Xandra Brood told the AD, adding that she had to point out colours to him because the artist was colour-blind. “He worked very fast and made several paintings one after the other.”

She hopes the painting will eventually hang on the walls of Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum, his greatest wish.

This painting’s estimated value is 13,000 to 15,000 euros, but Dupré says that’s maybe gone up 50% since the painting became part of the national collection Thursday.

That inclusion, says Dupré, is official recognition of the artist’s craftsmanship. “He was much more than a side-working rock star. And that is now being recognised.”

World.title: French customs seize thousands of THC sweets bound for NL
World.content:
French customs officers have intercepted 3,560 packs of cannabis-laced sweets that were being shipped from the US to the Netherlands, the European anti-fraud office OLAF said on Thursday.

The sweets contained THC, the main psychoactive substance in cannabis. Of the packs, 3,213 copied the look of a “very well-known European gummy brand”, using altered lettering to resemble its name. OLAF did not name the brand. All the packs have been destroyed.

OLAF did not say who the sweets were meant to be delivered to in the Netherlands.

In a statement, the agency said the familiar packaging gives the false impression of an ordinary, safe product, but that a single product could contain a high amount of THC, and children could be at risk.

Cannabis sweets have caused several scares in the Netherlands. This summer, Utrecht police warned parents after two children became ill from sweets found in a school playground, broadcaster NOS reported.

World.title: Seven Rotterdam police officers to face trial over arrest death
World.content:
Seven police officers will go on trial in January next year over the death of a 32-year-old man who was held in a “prone position” on the ground for a long time after being tasered during an arrest in Rotterdam in 2023, the public prosecution department (OM) said on Thursday.

Two officers chased the man on June 9 that year, first in a police van and then on foot, after reports that he had crashed his bicycle into a car and then cycled on.

When he ignored their instructions, one officer used a taser, but it did not incapacitate him or stop him from further resisting. More officers arrived and several of them pinned him down. Soon after he became unwell and was given CPR but died in hospital.

In February 2024 the OM said it would prosecute eight officers after an investigation by the Rijksrecherche, which investigates the police. A pathologist concluded the man’s death could have been caused by the way he was restrained.

The officers are accused of breaching the rules on the use of force with fatal consequences, which has been a criminal offence in its own right since July 2022.

The OM said on Thursday it had dropped a case against an eighth officer, as he was still in training and was following instructions.

The case will be heard on January 19 and from February 15 to 18 by the Blauwe Kamer, a special court in Utrecht that handles cases against police officers. The court will rule on all seven cases at the same time.

In September another Rotterdam man, Alfredo Goeloe (51), died during an arrest after collapsing while officers held him on the ground. That incident led to protests in the city. The Rijksrecherche is investigating his death as well.

World.title: Polish president in physical confrontation with judges amid power struggle at constitutional court

We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK). Afterwards, the president announced that he would hold a series of meetings with political leaders on Saturday afternoon to discuss the crisis. However, it remains unclear to what extent the government, which is in conflict with the opposition-aligned Nawrocki and is backing the judges seeking to control the court, will engage in that process. Meanwhile, the court itself remains surrounded by riot police and anti-government protesters. On Friday, Nawrocki had been flying to Senegal for a state visit when the crisis at the court broke out. He ordered his plane to turn around in midair and return to Warsaw. At around 1 a.m. on Saturday morning, Maciej Berek, a close associate of Prime Minister Donald Tusk who was recently chosen as a new TK judge, shared videos showing Nawrocki entering the TK building amid a confrontation at its doors. The president was heard asking judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who is leading the attempt to take control of the court, to move out of his way and could be seen pushing his way past her. Afterwards, presidential aide Marcin Przydacz claimed that Korwin-Piotrowska and another judge, Krystian Markiewicz, had “breached the inviolability of the head of state”. Berek denied this and said that it was the president who “barged into judge Korwin-Piotrowska with great force”. Subsequently, a further film showed Nawrocki, after he had entered the building, in a verbal confrontation with Korwin-Piotrowska and others, in which he can be heard telling them, “you are not Constitutional Tribunal judges”. ⚠️Mamy kolejne nagranie z TK. Tym razem prezydent krzyczy do sędziów, że „nie są sędziami” i w otoczeniu funkcjonariuszy SOP wchodzi po schodach na górę. pic.twitter.com/rkhoQLIv94 — Kamil Dziubka 🟡🇵🇱🇺🇦 (@KamilDziubka) October 31, 2026 The conflict stems from a years-long crisis around the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. It also regards the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Świeczkowski, as illegitimate. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, including Korwin-Piotrowska, Markiewicz and Berek. Those five judges arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies in parliament and submitted their oaths to the president’s office. However, Święczkowski, who before being appointed as a TK judge had served in the former PiS government, refused to accept those five judges on the court. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 On Friday evening, the judges appointed by parliament this year entered the TK and Korwin-Piotrowska announced that she had suspended Święczkowski for failing to properly exercise his duties. She said that, as the judge with the longest experience, she had assumed the position of acting head of the tribunal. Outside the court, riot police held back protesters, including opposition politicians, who called the events a “coup d’état”. Święczkowski himself was prevented by police from entering the grounds after some of his supporters had used a power tool to cut through the fence. At around 5 a.m., Nawrocki was seen leaving the TK. “There has been a violation of the constitutional order of Poland and a forceful takeover of a constitutional body,” said the president in a statement read by the head of his cabinet, Paweł Szefernaker. The president announced that he would hold urgent consultations with parliamentary groups in an attempt to “restore the legal order”. Those meetings are scheduled to take place on Saturday afternoon. There is chaos at Poland's constitutional court tonight as a group of government-backed judges moved to take control from the opposition-aligned chief justice. Riot police have surrounded the court and were seen preventing the chief justice from entering https://t.co/xpkp3sjPFn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 30, 2026 Leading figures from the right-wing and far-right opposition, with which Nawrocki is aligned, have indicated their willingness to engage in talks, as have two of Tusk’s junior coalition partners. Szymon Hołownia, the founder of the centrist Poland 2050 (Polska 2050), confirmed on Saturday morning that his group would attend the talks. He also urged Tusk to sit down at the table with Nawrocki. Hołownia said that his party had “watched last night’s events with concern” and that they “bring shame on Poland”. While he criticised Święczkowski and other PiS-nominated judges, he said that trying to fix the TK “by force” would only “exacerbate its downfall”. On Saturday afternoon, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, leader of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL) and a deputy prime minister, also revealed that he would personally attend the consultations with Nawrocki. @PL_2050 na wydarzenia dzisiejszej nocy patrzy z zaniepokojeniem. Przynoszą one Polsce wstyd. Nie przybliżają nas do naprawy tego, co zostało zepsute. Jest dla nas jasne, że Bogdan Święczkowski, wraz z nominatami PiS-u, zrobił z TK karykaturę sądu konstytucyjnego. Sytuacja w… — Szymon Hołownia (@szymon_holownia) October 31, 2026 Tusk’s only comment so far has been a social media post saying that restoring the rule of law “requires decisive action”. His justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, announced on Friday evening that he was seeking to have Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution lifted. On Saturday, speaking to broadcaster TVN, Żurek expressed support for the actions taken by Korwin-Piotrowska. He called Nawrocki’s behaviour at the TK “shameful” and said he “hoped prosecutors will take action, because it is unacceptable for someone protected by presidential immunity to behave in such a way”. Meanwhile, Tusk’s other main coalition partner, The Left (Lewica), announced on Saturday afternoon that it would not attend the talks with Nawrocki. “One cannot accept an invitation from someone who is himself responsible for the current situation regarding the Constitutional Tribunal,” wrote Anna-Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus. “The TK is in the hands of independent judges. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. Those five judges arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies in parliament and submitted their oaths to the president’s office. However, Święczkowski, who before being appointed as a TK judge had served in the former PiS government, refused to accept those five judges on the court. In doing so, he ignored an order by the European Court of Human Rights that the judges be allowed to take up their positions. Święczkowski argued that the ECHR had no authority to issue such a ruling. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Rumours have long swirled that the government would introduce those judges onto the court by force. PiS supporters have been camped outside the TK grounds for weeks with the aim of preventing that from happening. On Friday evening, large numbers of riot police were deployed around the TK. On the court’s website, a brief statement appeared, saying that a “break in the activities” of Święczkowski and his deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been ordered. The statement did not say who had ordered that break, but it cited article 130 of the law on common courts, under which the president of a court or the justice minister can order an immediate break in a judge’s official duties if they are caught in the act of committing an offence. However, Marcin Matczak, a prominent scholar of constitutional law who was also a critic of PiS’s judicial reforms, wrote on social media, that, while the justice minister exercises oversight over common courts, he cannot do so over the TK. “I consider Bogdan Święczkowski to be the worst person to serve as the president of the TK,” wrote Matczak. “I never thought I’d end up defending him, but this legal basis [for suspending Święczkowski] is nonexistent for a million reasons.” Ze szczątkowych informacji, na jakiej podstawie zawieszono B. Święczkowskiego, wynika, że ma to być art. 19 ustawy o statusie sędziów TK, który mówi, że do spraw nieuregulowanych w tej ustawie stosuje się „przepisy dotyczące praw i obowiązków sędziów SN” i art. 130 ustawy o SN,… — Marcin Matczak (@wsamraz) October 30, 2026 Meanwhile, Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, issued a statement announcing that he had submitted motions to the TK to waive the immunity from prosecution of Świeczkowski and Sochański. He said that the documents had been “delivered to the longest-serving judge of the Constitutional Tribunal”. That was a reference to Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the TK judges whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. She told state broadcaster TVP that it was she who had issued the order to suspend Święczkowski from his duties. She justified her action by accusing Święczkowski of blocking judges from taking up their positions and of overseeing irregularities in the assignment of judges to cases, reports Polskie Radio. Korwin-Piotrowska’s claim to have the longest tenure among TK judges relates not to her service on tribunal itself, but to the fact that she first began her judicial career in 1995. 🗣️ “Bogdan Święczkowski narusza zasady funkcjonowania TK. (…) Nie było innego wyjścia” – sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska w TVP Info. pic.twitter.com/22FYJJbQAC — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 30, 2026 While the TK website appears to now be under the control of Korwin-Piotrowska, the court’s account on social media service X issued a statement saying that “an unlawful takeover of the TK’s website has occurred”, that “Bogdan Święczkowski remains chief justice”, and that “Korwin-Piotrowska is not a TK judge”. “All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d’état,” it added. Nastąpiło bezprawne przejęcie strony internetowej Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Prezesem @TK_GOV_PL jest nadal Bogdan Święczkowski, a Wiceprezesem Bartłomiej Sochański. Pani Anna Korwin-Piotrowska nie jest sędzią Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Wszystkie osoby uczestniczące w… — Trybunał Konstytucyjny (@TK_GOV_PL) October 30, 2026 The court’s spokeswoman, Weronika Ścibor, told broadcaster Kanał Zero that “seven people elected as [TK] judges this year” had been escorted into the building by officers from the State Protection Service (SOP), a body responsible for protecting state officials. SOP is subordinate to the interior minister. She said they had entered the grounds of the court through a gate that leads from the prime minister’s chancellery, rather than the main entrance from the street where protesters are gathered. Korwin-Piotrowska also confirmed to TVP that she was one of seven judges who were inside the TK on Friday evening. Rzeczniczka Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Weronika Ścibor komentuje sytuację w TK. Według jej relacji siedem osób wybranych na sędziów weszło do budynku w asyście funkcjonariuszy SOP, natomiast wiceprezes Bartłomiej Sochański nie został wpuszczony na teren Trybunału. pic.twitter.com/VwxU4UrYuz — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) October 30, 2026 The developments at the court prompted outrage from the opposition. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński declared outside the court that “as of today, Poland has become a police state, and from there it’s a straight path to authoritarianism, and then to totalitarianism”. Kaczyński called on Nawrocki to return to Poland from his state visit to Senegal and defend the court. The president himself quickly confirmed that he had done so, with flight trackers showing his plane turning around in midair and heading back to Poland. Meanwhile, Zbigniew Kapiński, the chief justice of the Supreme Court – a separate entity from the Constitutional Tribunal – told Kanał Zero that he was “appalled” by what was happening, which was “undoubtedly a coup d’état”. Our most tracked flight right now: A Polish government aircraft en route to Senegal is now returning to Warsaw. https://t.co/YdLhQmV8pl pic.twitter.com/Dz9KPgI3eI — Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) October 30, 2026 Tusk, however, issued a statement on social media defending what was taking place at the TK. “Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” he wrote. “After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland approves first fast-track renewable energy zones
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced its first fast-track zones for renewable energy projects as the coal-dependent country seeks to speed up its transition to cleaner sources of electricity. The regional assembly in Wielkopolska province, western Poland, this week approved plans covering 105.4 hectares across four municipalities, where investors will be able to develop solar farms under simplified planning and environmental procedures. The environment ministry estimates that the changes, introduced under an EU directive, could reduce project preparation times from three to four years down to just one or two years. Pierwsze #OPRO już są! Sejmik województwa wielkopolskiego przyjął dziś pierwsze w Polsce plany OPRO. Obejmą one ok. 105,4 ha w gminach Lwówek, Rawicz, Słupca i Złotów.🔆 ❓Czym jest OPRO? ✅To Obszary Przyspieszonego Rozwoju #OZE, czyli tereny, na których – już podczas ich… — Marek Pogorzelski (@rzeczni_MKiS) October 26, 2026 Under the scheme, planning and much of the environmental assessment will be completed before investors apply for permits, allowing projects to move forward more quickly. Environmental authorities will also have a maximum of 45 days to review projects with a capacity of at least 150 kW. Industry representatives told energy Świat OZE, a renewable energy news service, that obtaining an environmental decision can currently take up to 150 days. The newly designated areas, known as Accelerated Renewable Energy Development Zones (OPRO), will be located in the municipalities of Złotów, Lwówek, Rawicz and Słupca. Together, they have an estimated technical potential of 66-80 megawatts of solar capacity, depending on the arrangement of the panels. Maria Niewitała-Rej, a climate and energy policy analyst at the Reform Institute, a Warsaw-based think tank, told the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna newspaper that while “the scale of the Wielkopolska plan is modest, the adoption of the first resolutions is a step in the right direction”. The creation of accelerated renewable energy development zones stems from the EU’s revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), which requires member states to designate areas where renewable energy projects can be developed more quickly. Under the directive, permitting procedures in these zones should take no longer than 12 months for onshore projects and 24 months for offshore projects. EU rules required the first zones to be designated by 21 February 2026, making Poland’s adoption several months late. Polish state mining firm JSW, which is the EU's largest producer of coking coal and one of Poland's biggest employers, has announced that it will cut over 4,000 jobs, 21% of its workforce, by the end of this year as it seeks to stem large financial losses https://t.co/EWP3rAVMaH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Poland has long had one of Europe’s most polluting energy sectors. The country still produces around half of its electricity from coal, by far the higher proportion in the EU. However, the share of renewables has grown significantly in recent years. It nearly doubled from 14.7% of the energy mix in 2021 to 29.4% in 2025. Onshore wind was the largest contributor last year, accounting for 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. Poland’s national energy and climate plan, approved in June, envisages coal accounting for just 0-5% of the energy mix by 2040. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%). Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish Left seeks to end state funding of clergy’s social contributions as government reform stalls
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Left, a junior partner in Poland’s ruling coalition, has proposed a bill to abolish the Church Fund, which provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy. It says it is frustrated by delays in fulfilling a pledge made by most parties in the wide ruling coalition to reform the fund. However, another coalition partner, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), says that it will oppose the bill, calling instead for a system allowing taxpayers to allocate part of their taxes to religious institutions of their choice. Senior church figures also say they have not been consulted. 📣 Lewica składa ustawę likwidującą Fundusz Kościelny. Czas na realizację umowy koalicyjnej w zakresie świeckiego państwa‼️ Co zakłada nasz projekt? ⬇️ ✅ Składki na duchownych przestają być w 80 procentach finansowane z budżetu państwa jak dotychczas. 50% składek pokrywać… pic.twitter.com/syqUMdCugr — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 29, 2026 The Church Fund, originally established in 1950 to compensate religious communities for property seized by the communist authorities, provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy, for religious organisations’ charitable activities, and for the renovation of religious buildings. It now supports all legally recognised religious denominations in Poland, including those that did not lose property at the time. Last year, the state spent 275.7 million zloty on the Church Fund. This year it has budgeted 272.6 million zloty. Most of this money is then used to cover 80% of clergy members’ social security contributions. Under the bill proposed by The Left, churches would pay half of the contributions, with clergy covering the other half. For regular workers, such contributions are funded jointly by employees and their employers, Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus, pointed out, as quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We are introducing the same arrangement for priests and members of the clergy.” At least 17.5bn zloty in state funds went to religious bodies from 2021-23, with over 95% going to Catholic organisations, the state auditor has found. In response, the speaker of parliament has proposed measures to reduce and better oversee such spending https://t.co/IN3dpY4La2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 16, 2025 An exception is made in the bill for members of enclosed religious orders and missionaries, who would have their contributions paid in full by their churches. The cost of maintaining historic churches would be covered by the National Fund for the Protection of Monuments, Żukowska explained. Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is the leader of The Left as well as the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful chamber in the Polish parliament, said the party did not oppose religion but wanted clergy to be treated equally under the law. “I would like to remind my coalition partners: our coalition agreement includes a commitment to work toward establishing the principles of a secular state in Poland,” he said, speaking alongside Żukowska. “Our patience is running out”. Ahead of the 2023 election, both the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and The Left pledged to abolish the Church Fund, while the centre-right Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) proposed replacing state funding with voluntary taxpayer contributions. PSL had no equivalent formal party-wide pledge. In 2024, after the coalition came to power, Tusk announced plans to reform the fund and appointed a government working group led by the PSL leader and deputy prime minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. The group’s work has since stalled. Kosiniak-Kamysz yesterday dismissed The Left’s proposal, saying it has “not the slightest chance of support in parliament”. His party, the second largest in the coalition with 32 of 239 MPs, sees the existing fund as an inexpensive form of compensation and will oppose abolishing it, he vowed. Instead, taxpayers should be able to allocate part of their taxes to a religious institution of their choice, a system used in several European countries, to “let the Polish people themselves decide whether or not they want to contribute,” he said, quoted by broadcaster Polsat News. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński, a member of Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO), said that he supported reform, but criticised The Left for submitting the bill without consulting its coalition partners. A long-term decline in trust in the Catholic church in Poland has accelerated over the last year, with only 35% of Poles now saying they trust the church. Meanwhile, the armed forces now enjoy record-high trust of 94% https://t.co/ErCBE4HwWR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 17, 2025 Religious communities also criticised the proposal for not having been discussed with them in advance. In a press statement sent to PAP, the Polish Episcopal Conference (KEP), the main organ of the Catholic church in Poland, said any solution should comply with the country’s agreement with the Vatican, as well as the constitutional principle that relations between the state and religious communities be regulated by mutual agreement. Bishop Jerzy Samiec, head of the Evangelical-Augsburg Church in Poland, the country’s biggest Protestant body, pointed to the significant costs churches face in maintaining their properties, including care homes and other facilities. The Catholic Church, Poland’s dominant religious institution, has seen a long-term decline in public trust, with only 35% of Poles saying they trusted it in 2025. That has coincided with a series of crises in recent years, in particular over revelations of child sexual abuse by members of the clergy and negligence in dealing with them by the church hierarchy. A variety of surveys, including from the church itself, show that religious attendance and identification have been declining in Poland in recent years. A growing number of Poles are turning away from the Catholic church, but not from religious belief itself. This creates challenges for the church, but also for Polish identity, which has historically been linked to Catholicism, writes Katarzyna Skiba https://t.co/udWGzd0X7F — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 18, 2023 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU. However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a “consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state” with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a “parody”. But soon, said Kaczyński, “a window of opportunity” for reform may appear because “completely different governments could emerge” in Poland, France and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year. PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day. He warned that the incoming opposition government will "strive to implement this plan" and called on Poles to "fight" against it https://t.co/QDbxmiaazJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2023 Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties. However, the PiS leader then warned that, “if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force”. Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties “include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU. This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations”. “It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,” he added. The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before. “Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,” wrote Tusk himself on X. “This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.” “So they do want Polexit after all,” wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania…An end to subsidies for farmers and investments…And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.” In a video published later on Thursday, Tusk declared that next year’s parliamentary elections would help decide “whether Poland remains in the European Union or leaves it”. Jarosław Kaczyński ogłosił właśnie, że Polska powinna zacząć rokowania o warunkach wyjścia z Unii Europejskiej. O taką między innymi stawkę toczy się dziś w Polsce walka. Twarda walka. Nie zamierzam jej przegrać, nawet jeśli nie wszyscy zagrają ze mną. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 29, 2026 Kaczyński responded by saying that “Tusk is lying as usual”. He emphasised that he believes “the EU is needed but it requires thorough reform” so that it “benefits not the elites, but ordinary citizens”. PiS deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek said on Thursday that his party was “considering all scenarios, including the possibility that the EU will kill itself”. However, he added that the priority remained reforming the bloc and “PiS has no plans to leave the EU”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). When PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it regularly clashed with Brussels over a variety of issues, including judicial reform, trade, climate policy, and migration. Since Tusk, a former president of the European Council, took power in 2023, his government has greatly improved relations with Brussels. Tusk jak zwykle kłamie. Najwyraźniej wychodzi z założenia, że dzień bez kłamstwa jest dniem straconym… Unia Europejska jest potrzebna, ale wymaga gruntownej reformy. Kryzys i zapaść w jej obecnym kształcie to efekt rządów Merkel i jednego z jej pomocników, Tuska. Nie ma co się… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) October 29, 2026 Poland has been the largest net recipient of EU funding since joining the bloc in 2004. A study published earlier this year found that the country’s economy is 42% larger than it would have been had Poland not been part of the EU. Opinion polls consistently show a large majority of Poles in favour of remaining part of the EU. However, recent years have seen an uptick in support for Polexit, as well as for anti-EU far-right parties. PiS has increasingly found itself competing against such parties for votes. Regular polling by state research agency CBOS shows that, while opposition to EU membership fell to a record low of 5% in 2022, it has subsequently risen, standing at 14% in the most recent survey. World.title: Polish bishop convicted for failing to promptly report child sex abuse allegations
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the first ruling of its kind in Poland, a Catholic bishop has been found guilty of failing to promptly inform the law enforcement authorities about allegations of child sex abuse committed by priests under his authority. Andrzej Jeż, the bishop of Tarnów, was handed a non-custodial sentence that will require him to donate 25% of his earnings for two years to a charity that supports victims of child sexual abuse. However, the verdict can still be appealed, and the diocese of Tarnów has already announced that it “disagrees with the court’s ruling” and that an appeal will be filed. Pierwszy taki wyrok w Polsce. Biskup skazany za zwlekanie z powiadomieniem prokuratury o pedofilach w sutannach Ordynariusz tarnowski bp Andrzej Jeż jest pierwszym biskupem oskarżonym o zbyt późne powiadomienie prokuratury o pedofilii w Kościele. I pierwszym, który który został… — Bartosz T. Wieliński 🇵🇱🇪🇺🇺🇦🇬🇱 (@Bart_Wielinski) October 29, 2026 The case relates to alleged abuse by two priests who worked under Jeż’s authority. They can be identified only as Stanisław P. and Tomasz K. under Polish privacy law. In 2022, prosecutors discontinued an investigation into allegations against Stanisław P. because the statute of limitations had expired, despite concluding that he had harmed at least 95 children and committed “sexual acts” against 77 of them over several decades in parishes in Poland and Ukraine. In 2023, prosecutors decided to charge Tomasz K., who allegedly sexually abused children as early as 2018. However, they have been unable to formally present the charges to him because of his poor health, news website OKO.press reported earlier this year. Though Jeż was not accused of complicity in the alleged abuse itself, he was charged under a 2017 law making it a criminal offence not to “immediately notify the authorities” of “credible information” about sexual abuse of minors. The offence is punishable by up to three years in prison. Investigators say that, although an internal church probe into Stanisław P. was initiated in the 2000s and a decision to remove him from the clergy was made in 2013, Jeż only notified the prosecutor’s office in 2020. In the case of Tomasz K., the bishop notified prosecutors only in 2021. In court, prosecutor Marcin Stępień said that Jeż’s failure to report the abuse promptly had allowed the statute of limitations to expire in the case of some of Stanisław P.’s victims. Stępień also noted that the bishop had only come forward with the information when media coverage brought the allegations against Stanisław P. to light, reports broadcaster TVN. A church commission set up to investigate child sex abuse in a Catholic diocese in Poland has identified at least 50 victims and 29 abusers. It also found that bishops repeatedly failed to take action when credible reports of abuse were submitted to them https://t.co/MRNl5vWp4E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 13, 2026 Prosecutors sought a 10-month prison sentence, suspended for three years, and a fine of 20,000 zloty (€4,550). Jeż, however, denied the allegations against him and sought an acquittal. He argued that he had reported the alleged abuse to the authorities as soon as there was credible information. On Thursday, the court found the bishop guilty, giving him a sentence known as “restriction of liberty” (ograniczenie wolnośći), under which a convict is not imprisoned but required to do some kind of social good. In Jeż’s case, the court ordered that 25% of his salary for two years be donated to the Empowering Children Foundation (Dajemy Dzieciom Siłę), which supports victims of child abuse. He was additionally ordered to pay 20,000 zloty to the Fund for Assistance to Victims and Post-Penitentiary Assistance. In a statement after the verdict was issued, the diocese of Tarnów said that it “disagreed with the court’s ruling” and that, after a written justification from the court was reviewed, “an appeal will be filed”. The Catholic church in Poland has in recent years been hit by a series of revelations regarding historical abuse of minors by members of the clergy and allegations that bishops covered cases up. The Vatican has taken action against a number of Polish bishops over the issue. Most recently, in 2024, the Vatican announced the resignation of the bishop of Łowicz, Andrzej Dziuba, due to his “negligence in handling cases of sexual abuse against minors”. In February, a commission created by the diocese of Sosnowiec following a series of scandals announced that it had identified at least 50 children who were harmed and 29 people suspected of abusing minors, most of them members of the clergy. World.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Turkish software engineer has, with the help of AI and vast quantities of Polish public data, created a precise digital replica of Warsaw, the city where he lives. The map, which can be explored for free online, features almost 200,000 buildings, moving trams that match their real-life schedules, changing light and weather conditions, and over 45,000 accurately placed streetlamps that turn on at night. It is even possible to fly a virtual plane through the city. The person behind the project, Bedirhan Yildirim, was inspired by recent efforts to produce similar maps of New York and London. While he initially considered producing one of Istanbul, his hometown, he decided instead to pick the city he lives in, Warsaw. “It is smaller, mostly flat, and I walk its streets every day,” he explained of his choice. Yildirim then used AI coding agents to create the map through a process of trial and error, constantly tweaking and improving the model. The initial version took only two days to produce and was launched on 22 October, but it has been regularly improved since then based on feedback from users. The work was made possible by what Yildirim says is the “incredible amount of data” Poland’s national mapping office, GUGiK, provides for free, including 3D building models, terrain scans, and even details of almost 2 million trees. Further information, including on parks, streetlamps, and traffic lights, was taken from OpenStreetMap, a freely licensed database. Meanwhile, timetables from Warsaw’s public transport authority, ZTM, and Poland’s national rail operator, PKP, allowed the map to feature accurately timed trams and trains. Current weather conditions are input from Open-Meteo, an open-source meteorological service. But users can also choose to manually adjust the time of day or year, with light and weather changing accordingly. An observation deck at the top of the EU's tallest building, Varso Tower in Warsaw, has opened to the public. Located 230m up on the tower's 53rd floor, the attraction offers a 360° panorama of Poland's capital.https://t.co/VeEapOmh4s — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 9, 2025 The result is an incredible level of explorable detail, from major landmarks, such as the communist-era Palace of Culture and Science and Varso Tower, the EU’s tallest building, down to the seating steps and bars along the Vistula River boulevards. The map also features graveyards reflecting Warsaw and Poland’s diverse past, including Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Jewish and Tatar Muslim graves. Around 1 November, when Poles visit cemeteries around All Saints’ Day, candles glow around the graves. A final touch Yildirim has added is a flight simulator, allowing users to travel over the city – and complete missions – in a Cessna aeroplane, an air ambulance, a flying car, or even a UFO that takes off from the Copernicus Science Centre and travels to the National Stadium. I turned Warsaw into a flight sim 🛩️ Take off from Chopin, fly through the ring over the Palace of Culture, then land a UFO inside Stadion Narodowy as the roof opens 🛸 Desktop only for now. Can you land it? 👇 pic.twitter.com/DT2fdk1Vem — Bedirhan (@bedcodes) October 27, 2026 Speaking to Notes from Poland, Yildirim says that he moved to Poland in 2022 to pursue a job in IT before starting his own business. Initially living in Kraków, the country’s second-largest city, he then moved to Warsaw in 2025. Asked what his own personal favourite places in the city are, Yildirim points to Warsaw’s parks, such as Skaryszewski, Pole Mokotowskie and Łazienki. His favourite neighbourhood is Saska Kępa on the right bank of the Vistula. The software engineer adds that his project is an example of how AI can be an “amazing tool to do 90% of the job very quickly”. The remaining 10% of human input “is what keeps it from being ‘AI slop'”. Yildirim says that, without the use of AI, the map of Warsaw he created would have needed an entire team to build over a period of months.
