World.title: Function of Croatian Judiciary Facing Serious Problems Once Again
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – The very function of the Croatian judiciary is facing serious problems yet again due to some judges refusing to participate in proceedings if they’re recorded.

President of the Constitutional Court Frane Staničić stated that the Court will function with great difficulty due to the decision of some judges not to participate in sessions that are audio-recorded. Index reports that in an interview for RTL Danas he revealed that he is extremely sorry that individual judges, as he believes, have stopped providing protection to citizens within the judiciary system. These are judges Andrej Abramović, Sanja Bezbradica Jelavić and Lovorka Kušan, who oppose the way in which the audio recording of sessions was introduced. They claim that no appropriate decision of the Court was adopted and refuse to participate in sessions which, in their opinion, are being recorded unlawfully.

“we really tried hard to come to an agreement”

Staničić said that the judges during the past year invested great effort so that the Constitutional Court would function normally and protect the rights of citizens. As an example he cited decisions on politically sensitive laws, among which are the Act on Building Management and the Act on Local Taxes. He emphasised that the decisions on those laws were adopted by a large majority, with only one or two votes against. He added that the number of separate opinions has significantly decreased, which according to his interpretation shows that the judges sought to reach agreement. “Unfortunately, due to the refusal of certain colleagues to participate in the work of the constitutional court bodies because of the introduced audio recording, the system will function with great difficulty,” Staničić said.

When asked why he introduced recording without a decision of all the judges, Staničić confirmed that there was no formal decision of the Constitutional Court as a collegial body. He claims, however, that there was an informal agreement and that all judges were familiar with the procurement and installation of the equipment. “I warned the judges several times that we would buy the system, that we had procured it, installed it and that we were testing it. At the session on the 6th of October, which was also recorded, I said in front of everyone that from that day, in accordance with the agreement, the sessions are being recorded. No one reacted to that,” he explained. He also commented on the appearance of judge Andrej Abramović, who had been a guest on RTL the day before. Staničić believes that Abramović should have pointed out his disagreement before the conflict among the judges arose because of the recording.

the introduction of audio recording doesn’t require the permission of all judges

“He said in your programme that he practically knew that recording was taking place, or rather that recording would be introduced, but that I am neither his father nor mother, so he would not warn me that something is not good,” Staničić said. “I’d like to openly ask the public to judge – is it in accordance with the role of a Constitutional Court judge that if he considers that something is not good, he collegially warns the President of the Court that he considers that this should not be done, or that he remains silent and then on the basis of his unexpressed disagreement creates this problem that has now occurred?” he added.

Staničić claims that he did not need a special decision of all the judges to introduce audio recording because as President he has the authority to decide on the manner of establishing the minutes. As the main reason for introducing recording he cited earlier disagreements about the content of the minutes of the sessions.

“I introduced audio recording for a simple reason: we had a series of problems with establishing the authenticity of the minutes. It happened that colleagues claim that something stands in the minutes that should not stand and vice versa,” he explained. As a particularly problematic case he cited the events from May of this year, when the judges discussed the composition of the panels of the Constitutional Court. According to his words, it was precisely the judges who now oppose the recording who at that time contested the minutes.

“The judges who today contest the audio recording at that time contested the minutes that were signed by two minute-takers and whose accuracy was confirmed by five judges. In such circumstances there is no other way to ensure an authentic record that no one will be able to contest,” Staničić said.

should some sessions be completely open to the public?

The President of the Constitutional Court believes that audio recording should contribute to transparency and the possibility of verifying what was said at the sessions. He also announced that he wants to open a discussion on the possibility that part of the sessions of the Constitutional Court will in future be accessible to the public.

“I personally believe that the Court should be more open to the public in general. I can announce that I will initiate a serious discussion at the Constitutional Court on the Court becoming more open, that perhaps even part of the sessions will be public,” he stated. He emphasised that the main task of the Constitutional Court is the protection of citizens’ rights, but he believes that due to the current conflict that task has fallen into the background. He also rejected claims that the recordings of the sessions are his private documentation.

“This is official documentation created in official premises, with official equipment, and is stored on the official servers and information system of the Constitutional Court,” he said.

Staničić claims that every judge can access the recordings and listen to them. He rejected the claim of judge Abramović that access was denied to someone, but at the same time emphasised that a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening and obtaining one’s own copy of the recording. “I received a request for a copy of the recording. Here a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening, which is absolutely not disputed, and the question of copies. I replied only to the colleague who requested it that her request will be considered in terms of scope and possibilities. Therefore, such a request has by no means been rejected,” he stated.

no agreement has been reached at all

In order to resolve the dispute, Staničić proposed the establishment of a working group that would prepare rules on audio recording. It would include him, the Secretary General of the Constitutional Court and one of the judges who oppose the recording. “Unfortunately, I did not receive a positive answer because participation in the working group is conditioned on the cessation of audio recording. I have already explained that this is impossible, because it is the only way in which I can ensure authenticity,” he said.

Staničić stated that one of the three judges who opposed the recording nevertheless participated in a session, although she retained her opposition. He believes that the remaining two judges could have done the same so that the work of the Court would not be hindered. “Unfortunately, the other two judges did not want to follow that example. They could have retained their opposition, but we want to protect citizens. However, they chose the opposite – not to protect the rights of citizens, but to deepen the conflict, which is unnecessary,” he said.

a new session has been announced for november the 13th

The President of the Constitutional Court said that he has no mechanisms by which he could force the judges to participate in the work. Nevertheless, he hopes that everyone will accept the responsibility they have towards citizens and enable the continuation of regular work. He announced that he will schedule a new session as soon as the two judges who oppose the recording return from an official trip, which he expects to take place on or around the 13th of November. In the meantime the question remains open whether an agreement will be reached on the manner of recording the sessions.

Staničić also said that the Constitutional Court has received requests from GONG, the media and citizens for access to the audio recordings. He emphasised that this is sensitive documentation that may contain secret data and that he cannot make it public on his own. Due to the great public interest he announced that he will seek the consent of all constitutional judges for the publication of the recordings. If he obtains it, he is ready to publish them, and if someone opposes it, he announced that he will publicly say who was against.

“This is a very sensitive issue and secret data that I cannot just give out. However, given the extreme importance of the issue and the interest of the public, I will propose and seek a consensus of all judges that the recordings be given to the public. If a consensus is reached, I will give the recordings. If it is not reached, if even one judge is against, I will publicly announce which judges were against it,” Staničić concluded.

World.title: Daytime Lights Now Mandatory on Roads in Croatia
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – Daytime lights being on is now mandatory on all roads in Croatia, with a fine of 30 euros being prescribed to those who fail to comply.

As of today (November the 1st), the national obligation to use daytime or dipped headlights while driving during the day comes into force for drivers using roads across Croatia. Index reports that this rule will now remain fully in force until the 31st of March 2027. Drivers who fail to comply face the aforementioned fine of 30 euros.

the law applies to all motor vehicles

This is an obligation prescribed by Article 102 of the Road Traffic Safety Act, which the Police Directorate also reminded of ahead of the holiday weekend. Although many newer cars have automatic daytime running lights, drivers of older models will have to make sure to switch them on. According to the law, daytime or dipped headlights must be switched on on motor vehicles while driving during the day, regardless of weather conditions and visibility. For motorcycle and moped drivers the rule is somewhat different – they are obliged to use dipped headlights throughout the year, and a fine of 30 euros is also prescribed for non-compliance.

cyclists and e-scooter owners

The police also state that there are obligations for cyclists and drivers of personal means of transport, which include electric scooters. From the first dusk until full dawn, as well as during the day in the case of reduced visibility, they must have a white light switched on at the front and a red light at the rear. The fine for non-compliance with this rule amounts to 60 euros.

caution with automatic daytime running lights

Owners and drivers of cars with automatic light switching should check how the system works on their vehicle. On some models daytime running lights illuminate only the front of the car, while the rear ones remain off. This can be dangerous in conditions of reduced visibility, such as fog or heavier rain. Daytime running lights serve for better visibility of the vehicle, but are not a substitute for dipped headlights which are necessary at night and in conditions of poorer visibility.

winter equipment on vehicles will also soon become mandatory

The beginning of November brings another change for drivers, which comes into force a little later. From the 15th of November to the 15th of April, the use of winter equipment will also become mandatory on certain sections of public roads across Croatia, regardless of the weather conditions. In the case of winter conditions, when the road is covered with snow or ice, winter equipment is mandatory on all roads nationwide. It’s important not to equate this obligation with the one on the use of lights, which begins two weeks earlier. The Police Directorate calls on drivers to respect traffic regulations and take care of safety. “Comply with traffic regulations and make sure your lights are always on for better visibility, and especially from the 1st of November to the 31st of March,” the police concluded.

World.title: New Ultra-Fast Chargers Put Into Operation on Croatian Motorways
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – New ultra-fast electric vehicle chargers have been put into operation on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, with some having power as strong as 400 kW.

Petrol has put into operation 18 new ultra-fast charging points for electric vehicles on the Croatian motorways A1 and A3, among which are six charging points with a power of 400 kW intended for heavy electric trucks. Poslovni reports that the new connections have been installed at the Janjče west, Dragalić south, Dragalić north and Desinec north rest areas, the company announced. This therefore expands the network of charging stations on important transport routes towards the Adriatic and on the motorway that connects Slavonia with Zagreb.

there are now 70+ ultra-fast connections across croatia

During the summer, Petrol already opened new ultra-fast charging stations at the Vrata Jadrana north and south and Dragalić north rest areas, and the latest investment also includes infrastructure for electric freight vehicles. The company now has more than 300 charging points for electric vehicles dotted all over Croatia, of which more than 70 are ultra-fast. At the regional level its network covers approximately 1,300 connections. Particularly significant is the installation of 400 kW charging points for electric trucks, which due to the large capacity of their batteries require more powerful infrastructure than passenger cars.

Nevertheless, the actual charging speed depends on the capabilities of the vehicle, the state of charge of the battery and other conditions, so the nominal power of the charger does not mean that every vehicle will be able to charge the battery at a power of 400 kW.

eu cash helped to expand the network

The new charging stations are part of Petrol’s OneCharge network and the European CROSS-E project, which is co-financed with European Union funds through the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF). The project includes the development of infrastructure for ultra-fast charging of passenger cars and electric trucks on important transport routes in Croatia and in neighbouring Slovenia. Within the scope of this particular project, Petrol plans to install a total of 98 charging points at 22 locations in the two countries. Part of the infrastructure will be intended for electric freight vehicles.

These considerable investments are also linked to the European Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), with which the European Union is gradually introducing requirements for the availability of charging stations on the main transport corridors. The overarching goal is to facilitate travel by electric cars on longer routes, reduce the need for detours for charging and enable the development of electric freight traffic.

World.title: Croatian Railway Projects Totalling €1.7 Billion Are Now Underway
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Croatian railway projects totalling €1.7 billion are currently underway as part of a major investment cycle.

The Croatian railway network is currently in the middle of a major investment cycle. Index reports that large projects worth €1.7 billion are underway, and by 2035 additional investments of around six billion euros are planned. The goal of the modernisation is to ensure faster, safer and more reliable transport of passengers and freight and to strengthen the competitiveness of Croatian ports.

State Secretary in the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Žarko Tušek, member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić and professor from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences Mladen Nikšić spoke on HRT about the current projects, traffic safety and the deadlines for the first results. State Secretary Žarko Tušek emphasised that the modernisation of the railway is a continuation of major investments in transport infrastructure, after road, maritime and air transport. “It is the turn of the railway, without which there is no development of the economy, port capacities, logistics, rural areas and regional transport,” Tušek said.

a lowland railway to rijeka

He noted that projects worth more than a billion euros have been completed, and almost 700 million euros have been invested in the maintenance of the sector in the last eight years alone. “The value of active, contracted projects currently amounts to €1.7 billion,” he said. Among the largest projects are the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth 900 million euros, and the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section of 350 million euros. Investments are also being made in the Podravina and Istrian railways and the Zadar – Knin railway, while the Vukovar – Vinkovci section has been completed. Long-term plans envisage investment of another around six billion euros by 2035, and the modernisation of the entire 2,600-kilometre network will continue after that as well. As a key future project Tušek singled out the lowland railway towards Rijeka, estimated at around five billion euros.

the dugo selo-novska railway is becoming double-track

“Just yesterday we selected international consultants who will accompany us in the negotiation procedure so that within a year we can reach the conclusion of an Alliance contract for the construction of that major project,” he announced. Member of the Management Board of HŽ Infrastructure Marijan Ćužić said that the reconstruction of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway, worth almost 900 million euros, will bring a significant step forward in the development of transport. “That section is the only one on the former tenth international corridor that has remained single-track. With the completion of the works we will have a double-track electrified railway from the border with Slovenia to the border with Serbia, with speeds of up to 160 kilometres per hour,” Ćužić explained. He compared the importance of the second track with road traffic, where an additional lane increases throughput. He emphasised that this will enable Croatia to reach the standards of modern European railways and ensure faster and safer travel.

croatia will need to wait a decade before it notices a difference

Professor Mladen Nikšić from the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences believes that the current investments will bring significant improvements, especially after the completion of all projects. “I believe that we will have higher-quality railway traffic, shorter journey times and greater track capacity for the transport of passengers and freight. This will also make our ports more prominent,” Nikšić said. He assessed that the modernisation should significantly shorten journeys. “I believe that when those projects are completed, we will be able to reach Slavonski Brod or Vinkovci in two to two and a half hours, and we will travel faster towards Rijeka and the Adriatic cities as well.

That takes time, but I think the full effects will be visible in about ten years,” he said. Nikšić added that investments in infrastructure must be accompanied by better quality of transport, especially the punctuality and reliability of trains. “Work needs to be done on the quality of transport, punctuality and reliability. We also have new vehicles, and all of that together with a quality timetable must form a complete whole,” he said.

Professor Nikšić also commented on recent railway accidents in Croatia. He pointed out that the causes can be divided into two groups: non-compliance with procedures and problems in communication, and shortcomings in vehicle maintenance. “The number of freight train accidents on the Rijeka railway is particularly worrying.

With the liberalisation of freight traffic the state has lost part of its influence on the maintenance and control of vehicles,” he warned. He believes that the Railway Traffic Safety Agency should intensify extraordinary and unannounced inspections, and that for the prevention of human errors the key are the education of employees and compliance with procedures. “Administratively everything can be in order, but vehicles can be better or worse maintained. Work must certainly be done on that,” he emphasised. Marijan Ćužić from HŽ Infrastructure said that preliminary checks of recent accidents have not shown irregularities on the infrastructure, but that investigations are still ongoing.

the rijeka railway can’t deal with all the freight

“Our first preliminary investigations have shown that there was no error on the infrastructure. The railway systems, including tracks and switches, are correct,” Ćužić said. He added that the education and communication of all participants in railway traffic need to be improved in order to reduce the risk of accidents. Žarko Tušek emphasised that investments in the railway have a key role in strengthening the competitiveness of Croatian ports. As an example he cited Rijeka, whose traffic is growing, but the existing railway cannot accept all the freight, so it ends up on the roads. Marijan Ćužić continued and explained that the construction of the second track will enable significantly greater freight transport. “We calculate that with the new railway we will be able to transport to Europe all the additional quantities of freight that the Port of Rijeka plans in the next ten years or so,” he stated.

could rijeka become a bigger logistics centre than trieste and koper?

Mladen Nikšić believes that along with Rijeka it is also necessary to develop the Dalmatian ports, modernise the Lika railway and better connect Zadar, Šibenik and Split. He also warned that the future lowland railway towards Rijeka will require additional port capacities.

“When the lowland railway is built, its capacity will be 30 million tonnes, which Rijeka alone will not be able to generate. That is why we already need to think about a new port on Krk, a railway connection and a new bridge that would connect the island with the mainland,” Nikšić said. Tušek confirmed that the lowland railway, a new terminal on Krk and a large freight centre in Zagreb are part of the Government’s strategic plans. “Krk is not any fantasy, but a project that needs to start being elaborated urgently. Its potential is such that Rijeka could become a stronger logistics centre than Koper and Trieste together,” Tušek concluded.

When asked when the general public and the economy will feel concrete benefits, Marijan Ćužić replied that the first results will be visible in two to three years, and that the Croatian railway in the next decade should reach the European level. “The first advances will be seen on the section from Zagreb to the Hungarian border, but also on the railways in Istria, in the Knin and Zadar area and on the Podravina main line. Already in a relatively short time our users will be able to use the advantages of a modern railway,” he concluded.

World.title: Meet The Croatian City With a Monument Not to a King, But to a Frog
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – There’s a central Croatian city which was once home to a monument dedicated not to a nobleman or a king, but to a frog.

Rulers and historical warriors are the most common monuments you’ll see dotted all over Croatia. A contemplative artist, statesman, writer or philosopher is also not a rarity. Nor is the one and only Nikola Tesla. Women are also found across the country, including the legendary Mila Gojsalić high in the mountains above Omiš. As Lana Mindoljevic writes for Putni kofer, however, you won’t often notice monuments to animals. That is, of course, unless they’re being ridden by some hero into battle. In Karlovac, one of the best-known monuments was for a long time the one dedicated not to a brave horse or dog, but to a frog. The small bronze resident of the city on four rivers stood for years at the entrance to the city’s so-called Promenade.

croatia’s only frog monument

The frog monument was unveiled in March 2008 and until 2024 stood at the intersection of Stjepan Radić Street and Dr. Franjo Tuđman Promenade, better known as the Promenade. Until 2022 it was the only frog monument in Croatia, but then one was also placed in Zmijavci near Imotski. Unfortunately, you cannot see the Karlovac frog anymore. It was removed during the renovation of Radić Street, when it was taken for safekeeping to the warehouse of the Public Fire Brigade of Karlovac. It never returned to its old location. When relocating it, the city announced that it would find a new location for it, because the old one had proved non-functional; it obstructed, they say, the passage and the organisation of events on that Promenade. But the works have been completed, and the Karlovac frog has still not received a new place.

The monument to the frog was unveiled on the 31st of March 2008, and it was made by the academic sculptor Stjepan Gračan. It was donated to Karlovac by the City of Zagreb on the initiative of Zvonimir Bešker, a Karlovac native who worked in the Zagreb city administration. It arrived in the city two years before it was placed, and in the meantime the best place for it was being sought; even placement on the wall of the city magistrate was considered. In the end a location accessible to passers-by and children was chosen, for whom it was believed they would rejoice most in the new attraction.

a monument to the frog catchers of karlovac

The Karlovac frog was chosen because of the old nickname of the people of Karlovac: the inhabitants of the city on four rivers were once, namely, called frog-catchers (žabari). What was once a pejorative name, some of the inhabitants over time accepted as part of their identity. While the frog was still standing in its place, a story also appeared that it brings luck: one was supposed to, allegedly, rub it behind the left eye and make a wish. Whether the firefighters today whisper their wishes to the frog or have already become so used to it that they don’t even notice it, we don’t know, but we believe that many more people would rejoice in it on some public surface.

World.title: Tourism Minister Welcomes Advent Price Caps Across Croatia
World.content:
October the 31st, 2026 – Tourism Minister Tonči Glavina has stated that he more than welcomes advent price caps announced across Croatia, hoping for higher winter visitor figures.

The tourism minister stated that ” for any Advent to be successful, its most important component in terms of the structure of guests, in terms of revenue, in terms of hospitality and so on, is precisely domestic consumption,”

Index reports that he added that this type of consumption depends most on the citizens who live in the municipalities and cities that organise Advent fairs. He recalled that Poreč, Pula and Split have introduced price limitations for part of the Advent offer. He pointed out that the Split model provides for the determination of part of the prices already in the public call that regulates the relations between the city and the tenants of the Advent stalls. At the same time, prices are limited only for a smaller part of the hospitality offer.

“In this way, they’ve very clearly ensured the conditions that Advent and the hospitality offer at Advent are absolutely accessible to everyone,” Glavina said.

split caps its advent prices for the first time ever

It’s worth noting that this year, Split has introduced limitations on the prices of part of the food and drinks at Advent stalls for the very first time. According to the public call published by the city company Žnjan, a portion of fritule of at least 150 grams may cost a maximum of four euros, while a hot dog and sausage of at least 80 grams may cost a maximum of three euros. Mulled wine and hot chocolate, in a quantity of at least two decilitres, may cost a maximum of three euros. For the same quantity of tea hospitality providers will be able to charge a maximum of €2.50, while half a litre of water must not be more expensive than two euros.

The limitations apply to the seven listed products, and not to the entire offer. A novelty is also that the City of Split will for the first time, when selecting tenants, score the quality of their hospitality offer, and not only the offered rent. This year’s Advent in Split will last from the 27th of November to the 6th of January, and Advent stalls will be set up on the Riva, Prokurative, in Đardin and Stobreč.

pula also caps its advent prices

A similar decision was made by Pula, where fritule, pancakes and Christmas cookies may cost a maximum of three euros per portion. For mulled wine, hot chocolate and cocoa the maximum price will be three euros, and for a hot dog, hamburger and bakalar five euros. Tea and water will be able to cost a maximum of two euros. Nevertheless, the limitations do not mean that all products at Pula’s Advent stalls will have prescribed prices. Hospitality providers will have to offer at least one product at a limited price, depending on the type of offer, while they will be able to determine the prices of other products independently.

Such a model has already been applied for years in Poreč, and things will be no different throughout the upcoming festive period, either.

Glavina emphasised that Advent as a tourist product is very important for the development of year-round tourism and tourist results in the months of December and January. He stressed that this year the Croatian National Tourist Board is for the first time conducting a national campaign with all key domestic Advent destinations, directed towards the main markets from which tourists come to Croatia.

“We’re making that transition towards year-round tourism and it is very important for us to have good content and programmes, and I am sure, because of the good prices, that the number of visitors at Advent will perhaps be higher than ever before,” he concluded.

World.title: US dollar edges down in Baghdad, holds steady in Erbil at 167,900 IQD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down slightly across Baghdad’s main currency exchanges on Saturday, October 31, 2026, while holding steady in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, at the opening of the weekly trading cycle.

According to market data, wholesale rates at Baghdad’s central Al-Kifah and Al-Harithiya exchanges slipped to 167,900 dinars per $100, marking a slight decline from 168,000 dinars recorded at the close of trading on Thursday.

Retail exchange desks across local markets in Baghdad saw retail selling rates stabilize at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, parallel trading counters maintained flat levels, quoting selling prices at 167,750 dinars alongside purchase bids of 167,650 dinars per $100.

World.title: Iraqi government denies 16 trillion dinar foreign loan reports to cover deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi federal government denied reports on Friday, October 30, 2026, alleging that Baghdad intends to borrow 16 trillion Iraqi dinars from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, China, Germany, and France to plug the sovereign budget deficit, confirming that state fiscal strategy relies on deploying domestic revenues to sustain public expenditures.

In statements delivered to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Government Spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi stated that widely circulated claims regarding foreign borrowing arrangements to offset budget shortfalls are entirely unfounded.

Al-Aboudi affirmed that there is no fiscal necessity for external borrowing, citing sustained crude export performance and favorable revenue flow.

Al-Aboudi explained that the executive administration adheres to a disciplined economic policy centered on optimizing state revenues to fund public commitments and sovereign operational requirements.

He noted that elevated crude export ceilings have bolstered treasury inflows, enabling the government to maximize available financial resources and fulfill state obligations without turning to foreign debt.

World.title: Health Minister highlights global partnerships at 6th Iraq International Health Expo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Health, Abdul-Hussein Aziz Al-Mousawi, underscored on Friday, October 30, 2026, the imperative of expanding international healthcare partnerships, transferring advanced medical technologies, and upgrading clinical healthcare delivery across the country.

Speaking during his inspection tour on the third day of the 6th Iraq International Health Exhibition and Conference, Al-Mousawi highlighted the exhibition’s role as a platform for exchanging technical expertise, acquiring advanced healthcare systems, and driving modernization across state and private healthcare infrastructure, according to a ministerial statement reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The minister commended the wide international turnout at this year’s edition, which brought together 375 healthcare corporations representing 24 countries.

Al-Mousawi noted that the significant global participation reflects growing commercial confidence in Iraq’s healthcare sector and opens viable investment pathways with international pharmaceutical and biomedical institutions.

During the walkthrough, Al-Mousawi inspected newly introduced medical diagnostic devices, surgical machinery, and specialized pharmaceutical supplies, engaging with company representatives and technical specialists on modern clinical solutions, hospital management technologies, and localized healthcare supply-chain integration.

World.title: Iraq to sign transit deals in Doha routing European internet traffic
World.content:
The Iraqi Ministry of Communications announced on Friday evening, October 30, 2026, that it will sign official agreements in Doha, Qatar, with three major nations to transit internet capacities through Iraqi territory to Europe.

The formal signing ceremony will take place on November 9, 2026, on the sidelines of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference and elections.

According to a ministerial statement, the strategic initiative is designed to solidify Iraq’s role as an international data transit bridge and a pivotal regional telecommunications hub linking the Middle East and Asia directly to European digital networks.

The ministry highlighted that this expansion will position Iraq as a global leader in the growth of terrestrial transit capacity volumes routed across sovereign territory over the preceding four months, advancing Baghdad’s broader strategy to monetize its geographic advantage as an alternative overland fiber corridor to undersea maritime routes.

World.title: Iraqi pharmacy sets Guinness World Record with 79,069 hydration pledges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has achieved a Guinness World Records title after Haya Pharmacy’s “Ghaith” hydration awareness campaign collected 79,069 pledges in one month, encouraging people across the country to adopt healthier water-drinking habits.

The initiative, which broke the record in Baghdad on October 5, 2026, got the highest pledges for a hydration awareness campaign in a single month.

The campaign, which was created in partnership with the Ebers marketing team, integrated community participation and public health awareness efforts to encourage regular water intake.

The campaign was strategically driven from Dubai, with teams from Ebers and Haya Pharmacy overseeing its execution on the ground in Iraq.

The success marks a significant milestone for Haya Pharmacy’s public health programs, demonstrating the effectiveness of national awareness campaigns in promoting better lives and community engagement.

World.title: Iraq signs agreement with Swiss pharma giant Roche
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Swiss pharmaceutical manufacturer Roche has inked a strategic partnership deal with Iraq’s Ministry of Health to strengthen healthcare services, with a focus on ophthalmology and hemophilia A.

In Baghdad, Swiss Ambassador Peter Nelson and officials from Roche and the Iraqi Health Ministry attended the signing of the agreement.

The partnership’s goal is to enhance patient care by strengthening diagnostic capacities, introducing sophisticated medical technology, and providing specialized training for Iraqi healthcare personnel.

Roche also reiterated its long-standing commitment to Iraq’s healthcare sector, emphasizing the necessity of working with government institutions to provide access to breakthrough therapies and medical knowledge.

The company thanked Iraqi Health Minister Dr. Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi for his support of foreign pharmaceutical companies and recognition of the significance of intellectual property protection in promoting medical innovation.

The arrangement is part of an attempt to modernize Iraq’s healthcare system and provide access to specialized medical services.

World.title: Maserati expands Iraq presence with new automotive partner
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Italian luxury carmaker Maserati has appointed Tiraz Automotive and Service Group as its new official partner in Iraq, aiming to strengthen its presence and expand customer access to the brand.

The deal was inked on September 18 in Modena, Italy, during a meeting between Maserati personnel and a Tiraz team headed by Kambiz Fathibitaraf.

Maserati hopes that the relationship would allow it to grow its operations in Iraq and provide consumers with a more personalized ownership experience, including access to its Fuoriserie customization program.

Customers may personalize their automobiles with various colors, materials, and design features that suit their specific interests.

The appointment is part of Maserati’s strategy to expand its presence in the Iraqi luxury automobile market and increase its local customer base.

World.title: Iraq signs gas capture agreement with US firm Morgan Hughes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US-based Morgan Hughes Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Iraq’s General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE) to develop projects aimed at capturing and utilizing associated gas currently flared at oil production sites across Iraq.

The agreement was signed in Baghdad by Morgan Hughes Energy Managing Director Gregory Bloom and GCCE, under the patronage of Iraq’s Minister of Environment, Sarwa Abdulwahid, and in the presence of US Chargé d’Affaires Steven Fagin.

The proposed partnership will focus on recovering low-pressure associated gas and using it to generate electricity for oil production facilities, reducing gas flaring and reliance on Iraq’s national electricity grid.

The initiative also aims to develop carbon credit projects using internationally recognized monitoring and verification standards, creating potential revenue opportunities through carbon markets while supporting Iraq’s emissions reduction targets.

Morgan Hughes Energy said it plans to bring American expertise and technology to the projects, supporting Iraq’s energy security and hydrocarbon development.

The company operates in the upstream and midstream oil and gas sectors, with interests across the Middle East, including offshore gas production, pipeline infrastructure, and gas storage facilities.

The MoU represents an initial step towards a broader strategic partnership between the two companies, with specific projects still subject to further development.

World.title: 'Politicisation of energy flows harmful': Jaishankar calls for diversified supply chains at G20
World.content:
External affairs minister

on Saturday called for reducing political interference in energy markets and diversifying global supply chains, saying disruptions were placing a disproportionate burden on developing countries.

Speaking about the message he delivered at G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said the discussions covered geopolitical conflicts, energy and food security, and resilient supply chains.

âLook, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications,â ANI quoted him as saying. He added that âthere are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway.â

On energy security, Jaishankar warned against disruptions in fuel distribution and their impact on developing economies. âThis distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful,â he said, adding that âthe Global South was bearing the brunt of the energy shortages and that something needs to be done.â

He also flagged risks to food security, citing disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea regions.





At the meeting's concluding session on supply chains, Jaishankar called for wider diversification of manufacturing and production across countries. âToday we need more diversified supply chains,â he said, advocating âmore globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing.â

In a post on X after the session, he said securing supply chains was central to the global economy's well-being and called on the G20 to promote âthe right to industrialiseâ and resist âpredatory practicesâ.

âDiversification and de-risking, including in connectivity, is the key to supply chain resilience, threatened by pandemics, conflicts, climate events and mishaps,â he said.

World.title: 10 lakh turnout target, 4,000 cops, 200 CCTV: Delhi braces for INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting a turnout of up to 10 lakh people and police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds.

The rally is being organised to protest against alleged electoral irregularities and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The mobilisation comes amid the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chori' and large-scale voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

'Chalo Dilli' march to precede rally

The programme will begin with a march, called 'Chalo Dilli', from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan at noon.

The rally at the venue is scheduled to continue from 10am to 5pm.

INDIA bloc leaders are expected to travel in open buses from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to the march's starting point.

The protest is expected to bring together leaders and supporters of opposition parties, along with student groups and civil society organisations.

The INDIA bloc has appealed to students, youth, women and workers to participate.





The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Abhijeet Dipke, and several student organisations have also extended support to the mobilisation.

4,000 cops, 200 CCTV cameras for security

While INDIA bloc leaders have projected a turnout of up to 10 lakh, Delhi Police expects around 50,000 people. Officials estimate that the ground can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, news agency PTI reported. With chairs, enclosures and passageways in place, its capacity is expected to fall to around 30,000 to 40,000.

Additional space will be kept outside to manage any spillover.

More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, will be deployed along the march route and at the venue. Ramlila Maidan has been divided into 14 security zones, each supervised by an assistant commissioner of police-rank officer.

More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will be used for surveillance.

A control room has also been set up inside the ground to monitor the arrangements.

Traffic curbs across key Delhi roads

Traffic restrictions will remain in force across parts of Delhi between 10am and 5pm. Diversions are planned at major intersections, including ITO, Delhi Gate, Rajghat, Ajmeri Gate and Turkman Gate. Commuters have been advised to avoid Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Minto Road and Desh Bandhu Gupta Road.

Special arrangements will be made to ensure that ambulances and emergency vehicles can reach LNJP and GB Pant hospitals.

Passengers travelling to New Delhi Railway Station have also been advised to plan their journeys in advance.

Delhi Police has said permission has been granted for the rally at Ramlila Maidan, but it has not received an application for the proposed procession from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction.

Rally follows symbolic 'public impeachment' of CEC

The rally follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Kumar organised by the INDIA bloc at Kharge's residence on Saturday.

Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, while Kharge moved a resolution listing the opposition's allegations against the CEC. Rahul Gandhi delivered the concluding remarks before the resolution was adopted.

Leaders of opposition parties, civil society representatives and people affected by the SIR exercise participated in the proceedings, which were modelled on parliamentary debates.

The resolution accused Kumar of facilitating alleged electoral manipulation, large-scale deletion of voters and undermining the Election Commission's independence, and called for his removal.

World.title: CGHS cover for dependent widowed, divorced daughters after parents' death
World.content: Widowed and divorced daughters returning to live with parents can now be added to their parents' Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) cards, even after the death of the govt employee or pensioner in whose name the original card was issued. Health ministry has allowed eligible daughters to be added or reinstated in cards held by family pensioners.The move will help parents supporting daughters with no independent income who need medical care. Earlier, once the original cardholder died and the spouse began receiving family pension, there was no provision to add or reinstate dependent family members.The ministry said it had received representations from pensioners facing difficulties supporting such daughters, particularly those with serious medical conditions requiring continued treatment. The benefit will not be automatic: authorities will verify daughter's marital status, income and dependency.All other CGHS eligibility conditions will continue to apply, the Oct 28 order said. It has been circulated to all central govt ministries and departments and DG of CGHS.

World.title: Opposition into politics of obstruction, must see anti-India pattern: PM Modi
World.content:
EKTA NAGAR, KEVADIA: PM Narendra Modi Saturday attacked opposition for abandoning its constitutional duty and instead resorting to politics of âobstructionâ, driven by âdespair and disappointmentâ.

Addressing the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade â organised annually on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel â Modi recalled how Sardar Patel and BR Ambedkar had, while framing the Constitution, clearly laid down duties and roles of govt and opposition.

âOpposition is exercising politics of âobstructionâ, in complete disregard of constitutional boundaries and propriety,â he added.

Warning against divisive forces that have come out in the open after more than a decade of political frustration to plot conspiracies, pit citizens against one another, and weaponise social media to spread rumours and tarnish Indiaâs image, the PM urged citizens to recognise the patterns of such forces conducting secret foreign meetings, their external backing by anti-India elements, and their rhetoric echoing the nationâs enemies.

âWe have ended Naxalism in remote areas, but the threat from ideological extremists (dimagi Naxals) is not yet over, and the country has to remain ever vigilant against such entities,â he cautioned.

Stressing that the grand mission of national unity and the journey toward a strong and capable India must continue regardless of difficulties, the PM outlined the next major national priorities of fully securing Indiaâs borders, putting an end to infiltration and resulting demographic changes, and advancing toward a secular civil code.





Acknowledging that major resolutions and bold decisions will inevitably face roadblocks and storms, he declared that the nation will not be deterred from the unwavering resolves of âEk Bharat, Shreshtha Bharatâ and a âViksit Bharatâ, working tirelessly with every breath and heartbeat toward the 2047 goal of a strong and capable India.

Modi also referred to the instability and uncertainty facing the world in the current times, with some countries at war and major nations facing global supply chain disruptions and energy crises, while also recalling how India beat apprehensions that it would be among the worst affected by energy crisis.

"Amid these apprehensions, some anti-india forces had also become active. But thanks to India's resilience, we did not let the people feel the hit of global energy crisis.

This is a diplomatic and political victory of Indiaâ¦as well of the unity of its people," he stated.

The prime minister, while attacking the earlier govt of electorally milking the promise of 'garibi hatao' without delivering on it, cited a recent World Bank report that stated that 50 crore Indians had beaten poverty over the past 10-12 year preceding 2024.

Recalling that he had last year, while paying homage at the 'Statue of Unity', resolved not to rest until the country became Naxal-free, the prime minister said the goal has been achieved in the next one year. I"n 2015, 126 districts were Naxal-hit. By March 2026, not a single district was Naxal-hit. For decades, youths there who once faced an uncertain future, now have access to opportunities like education and employment," he said.

"In this parade, families of Naxal-hit areas are invited. I welcome them and hope for their bright future. I also salute the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice to restore peace in the once Naxal-hit states," said the prime minister.

World.title: Sardar Patel had said if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad: Rajnath Singh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Paying rich tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary, defence minister

on Saturday recalled how the âIron Man of Indiaâ firmly dealt with the Nizam and Razakars, who sought to challenge Indiaâs sovereignty and âlaid the foundation of a strong and united Indiaâ.

On the issue of Kashmir, Rajnath said, âSardar Patel himself had said that if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad.â

Addressing a gathering, the defence minister said, âSardar Patel was the architect of Indiaâs political and territorial unity, whose extraordinary leadership, courage and unwavering commitment to national interest laid the foundation of a strong and united Indiaâ.

He further said, âIn democracy, govts are formed by winning the trust of the people and on the basis of public opinion, not through violence and anarchy. The path to change of power is elections, not coups. Those who challenge the unity and integrity of India should not forget the history of Sardar Patel.â âThose who dream of weakening India or creating disorder must remember that the land which gave birth to Sardar Patel has also given birth to Narendra Modi,â the minister said.





He also criticised Congress and its allies for their use of the term 'regime change'. He emphasised that âregime changeâ essentially implies a coup, violence, anarchy and civil war.

Rajnath said that Sardar Patel firmly believed that India should never seek what does not belong to it, but should never give up what rightfully belongs to it, under any circumstances. He said that India continues to move forward guided by this very principle.

âIndia does not seek to occupy anyone else's territory, nor does it initiate conflict. However, it remains resolute in securing what rightfully belongs to it and safeguarding its national interests.

â

He further asserted that whether it is avenging terrorist attacks or reclaiming Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK), India remains firmly committed to defending its rights and sovereignty.

Recalling the events surrounding the Congress presidential election of 1946, the minister said that despite overwhelming support from provincial Congress committees, Sardar Patel withdrew his candidature in deference to Mahatma Gandhi's wishes.

âFor Sardar Patel, the country was always bigger than the chair. Duty was more important than position, and national interest was greater than personal ambition.

â

The defence minister expressed concern over what he described as the historical neglect of Sardar Patelâs contributions and recalled that Patel was conferred the Bharat Ratna only in 1991, nearly four decades after his demise. He also referred to the contrast between the celebrations of Jawaharlal Nehru's birth centenary in 1989 and the relatively subdued observance of Sardar Patel's birth centenary in 1975.

He credited PM Modi with restoring national recognition to Patel's legacy through the Statue of Unity, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, Run for Unity and Ekta March.

âSardar Patel was a great leader in his own right. Honouring him has not made him any greater; rather, it has brought greater honour to India.â

Highlighting Sardar Patel's emphasis on military modernisation and indigenous production of weapons and ammunition, Rajnath said that India's growing defence manufacturing capabilities reflect the spirit of self-reliance that Patel advocated.

He said that Sardar Patel's legacy extends far beyond the integration of princely states. It is reflected in India's strong administrative institutions, national security, social harmony and commitment to national interest.

He said that the vision of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat' and the mission of building a Viksit Bharat are inspired by the ideals that Sardar Patel upheld throughout his life.

âIndia's greatest strength lies in its unity. We must never allow internal differences to weaken our national resolve. Preserving India's unity and integrity is the responsibility of every citizen,â he said.

World.title: Government extends Nilekani-led exam reforms panel tenure till January
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Centre has extended the tenure of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on examination reforms till Jan 2027, with the prime minister's office (PMO) seeking consultations with chief ministers and chief secretaries before the panel finalises its recommendations, TOI has learnt from govt officials.

During consultations, some stakeholders and experts have also suggested a hybrid format for NEET-UG 2027, allowing time to expand infrastructure for a complete shift to computer-based testing (CBT) in 2028.

A govt official said the PMO wants the task force, earlier expected to submit its report by Oct-end, to seek views from state leadership on challenges particular to different regions. The aim, the source said, is to better understand disparities in testing infrastructure, connectivity and administrative preparedness, and reflect these state-specific concerns in a more comprehensive examination reform roadmap.

Another proposal likely to feature in the task force's recommendations is a nationwide network of CBT centres developed by Centre and state govts with private investment, sources said. Such a model could expand govt oversight of testing facilities while mobilising private capital to build infrastructure, particularly in districts that lack secure, adequately equipped centres. The funding, ownership and operating arrangements would need to be worked out.





Such centres could support common security standards, reliable connectivity and better access for candidates outside metros.

TOI had earlier reported that the task force is prioritising "debundling" examination responsibilities. Under the proposed restructuring, question-paper setting, conduct of exams, management of test centres and security would be assigned to separate agencies instead of being concentrated with a single operator.

The objective is to create clearer lines of accountability and limit the risk of a lapse in one part of the examination process affecting the entire exercise. The approach would, however, require coordination between the agencies handling different stages.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The panel is also considering exam centres in every district and a common calendar for National Testing Agency (NTA), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) and Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs).

Coordinated schedules could help students and job applicants avoid exam-date clashes and allow testing infrastructure to be used more efficiently.

The six-member task force was constituted in July following the NEET-UG 2026 controversy, which led to the cancellation of the original exam and a retest. It has held 18 internal meetings and around 40 consultations, in addition to seeking public suggestions.

An Oct parliamentary committee report also recommended secure govt-controlled testing centres across districts and a phased transition to CBT for NEET-UG. The extension gives the task force more time to assess the feasibility of its proposals with states.

World.title: November to be slightly warmer than usual, predicts IMD
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nov is likely to be slightly warmer than usual, recording 'above normal' maximum (day) and minimum (night) temperatures over most parts of the country, IMD said Saturday.

The Met department also predicted that the country may get 'below normal' rainfall in most parts except for some areas in central, northwest and northeast India, where normal to 'above normal' rainfall is expected in Nov. 'Below normal' rainfall may be a concern for peninsular India as that part of the country usually gets good rain during Nov on account of the winter (northeast) monsoon.

The prediction of normal to 'above normal' rainfall in some areas of central and northeast India assumes significance for Madhya Pradesh and adjoining areas of Maharashtra and Gujarat, east Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as it will help wheat crop in these rain-fed regions during the month.

Meanwhile, the existing depression over southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to develop as a cyclonic storm on Sunday and cross south Andhra Pradesh and north Tamil Nadu coasts during the Monday evening-Tuesday morning period, bringing heavy rain to the coastal areas of both the states. Once the existing system develops into a cyclonic storm, it will be called 'Murasu'. 'Murasu' is a Tamil word which means a drum, particularly a traditional percussion instrument.

"Monthly rainfall for Nov over the south Peninsular India, consisting of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikkal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region, Kerala, Mahe and south interior Karnataka, is most likely to be 'below normal' (less than 77% of the long period average)," said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra while releasing the monthly outlook for rainfall and temperature for Nov.

The long period average of rainfall over south Peninsular India during Nov, based on data from 1971 to 2020, is 118.7 mm. In Oct, rainfall over the country (51.7 mm) was the sixth lowest since 2001 and 25th lowest since 1901, with a deficit of 31%. Rainfall over south Peninsular India (122.2 mm) was the sixth lowest since 2001.

World.title: Uttarakhand helicopter crash reiterates concerns raised by Parliamentary panel
World.content:
Another Char Dham chopper crash revives concerns over aviation safety lapses flagged by a parliamentary panel

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Yet another crash of a chopper ferrying pilgrims on the Char Dham route has brought into focus safety flags raised by a parliamentary panel overseeing aviation sector that have gone unheeded despite recurring tragedies.From "responsibility vacuum" which dilutes accountability to "pressure culture" that allows commercial considerations to override no-go weather conditions, the committee has in its recent reports, including one in March, highlighted several worrying factors at play in the helicopter services being offered to Char Dham pilgrims."The situation with helicopter operations in Char Dham sector is a symptom of a larger and dangerous structural flaw in India's aviation governance: a fractured and ambiguous regulatory command structure," the parliamentary panel on transport, tourism and culture headed by JDU MP Sanjay Jha had said.It said DGCA has ceded direct oversight of one of the country's most hazardous aviation zones to a state-level body, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority, whose capacity and expertise are under the scanner. This two-tiered safety system, with differing levels of scrutiny, is inherently unsafe and unsustainable, it added.A series of chopper crashes on the Char Dham route last year had led the committee to consult a number of experts and stakeholders, including aviation ministry, DGCA and private players, to look into the reasons behind the accidents and offer recommendations which, sources said, are yet to be implemented.The committee also pointed out "a glaring regulatory gap of significant concern", which is the absence of any mandatory, terrain-specific mountain flying training and certification for pilots who operate in the treacherous Himalayan region. "DGCA itself had expressed concern that UCADA lacked adequately trained and competent manpower for such high-density operations, yet a specific training mandate for these unique conditions was not in place.Aviation ministry acknowledged the high-risk operational environment, marked by challenging topography, rapidly changing and often severe climatic conditions, and high-density traffic, and said the inherent risks warranted immediate and serious intervention.

World.title: INDIA Bloc to hold mega rally against CEC, SIR today; leaders, supporters begin arriving in Delhi | LIVE
World.content:
The stage is set for the INDIA bloc’s mega rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday (November 1, 2026), with opposition leaders and supporters from different states beginning to reach the national capital for a show of strength against alleged electoral irregularities and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

World.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
World.content:
Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.

Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections:

Ro Khanna

Congressman Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Pramila Jayapal

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.

Also read: Pramila Jayapal has a close Bengaluru connect

Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond.

Ms. Jayapal was the first Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and has represented Washington’s 7th Congressional District since 2017.

On October 14, 2026, Ms. Jayapal voiced concern over reports about the removal of 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls in India. The Democratic lawmaker said she supported non-violent protests against what she described as anti-democratic efforts.

She said the developments appeared similar to attempts in the United States to undermine voting rights. India rejected her remarks on the Election Commission’s revision of electoral rolls, describing them as unwarranted, uninformed and an interference in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.

Ami Bera

Dr. Bera, a physician and politician serving in the U.S. House of Representatives, is seeking re-election as the Democratic candidate from California’s 3rd Congressional District.

The son of Gujarati immigrants from Rajkot, Dr. Bera was born in the United States. He was the third Indian-American elected to Congress. His father, Babulal Bera, later pleaded guilty to illegally funding his son’s election campaigns in 2010 and 2012.

Also read | Congressman Ami Bera’s father guilty of election crime

Dr. Bera has consistently advocated stronger India-U.S. ties. He served as co-chair of the Congressional Caucus on India and Indian Americans during the 114th Congress from January 2015 to January 2017.

Suhas Subramanyam

Congressman Subramanyam, who made history by becoming the first Indian-American elected to Congress from Virginia and the East Coast in 2024, is seeking re-election.

Mr. Subramanyam’s parents moved to the United States through Dulles Airport in the late 1970s. His mother is from Bengaluru and his father from Chennai, though he also spent part of his childhood in Secunderabad because his father served in the military.

Mr. Subramanyam has strongly supported closer India-U.S. ties, describing India as one of the world’s most important democracies and stressing the importance of strong relations between democratic nations.

Vivek Ramaswamy

Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is running for Ohio Governor. Backed by President Donald Trump, Mr. Ramaswamy won the Republican primary in May and became the party’s nominee for the November election.

A former co-chair of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), Mr. Ramaswamy launched a presidential campaign in 2024 before withdrawing and endorsing Mr. Trump.

The son of immigrants from Kerala, Mr. Ramaswamy was born in Cincinnati, Ohio. His father, Vadakanchery Ganapathy Ramaswamy, worked as an engineer at General Electric, while his mother is a psychiatrist.

Mr. Ramaswamy studied at Harvard University and Yale Law School before building a career in biotechnology and finance. He founded Roivant Sciences and served as its chief executive officer from 2014 to 2021. He later founded the asset management firm Strive. According to Forbes, his net worth is estimated at $2.5 billion.

Saritha Komatireddy

Republican Saritha Komatireddy, the party’s nominee for New York Attorney General, is a former federal prosecutor and a graduate of Harvard College and Harvard Law School.

She spent more than a decade prosecuting members of Al Qaeda, ISIS and Mexican drug cartels. As a federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of New York, she handled several high-profile cases involving terrorism, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, fraud and foreign public corruption, according to her official campaign website.

She later served in senior positions including Chief of International Narcotics and Money Laundering, Deputy Chief of Appeals and Deputy Chief of General Crimes in the district’s National Security and Cybercrime Section. She also served as Chief of Staff at the Drug Enforcement Administration and is currently a partner at Holtzman Vogel.

Nithya Raman

Nithya Raman, an urban planner and member of the Los Angeles City Council representing District 4, is contesting the Los Angeles mayoral election, according to the City of Los Angeles official website.

A graduate of Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Ms. Raman has served as co-chair of the Silver Lake Neighborhood Council’s Homelessness Committee and co-founded the SELAH Neighbourhood Homeless Coalition.

She was elected to the City Council in 2020, becoming the first Asian-American woman and the first South Asian elected to the body. In March 2024, she won a second term.

Ms. Raman currently chairs the Civil Rights, Immigration, Social Services and Neighbourhoods Committee and serves on several other council committees.

Pooja Sethi

Pooja Sethi is the Democratic candidate for Texas House District 47. An attorney by profession, Ms. Sethi has served as chief of staff in the Texas Legislature and as chair of the Travis County Democratic Party, according to her Linkedin profile.

Sandeep Srivastava

Sandeep Srivastava is the Democratic candidate for Texas House District 66. A long-time resident of the Plano-Frisco area, businessman and community advocate, Mr. Srivastava is challenging a five-term Republican incumbent in the November election, according to his official campaign website.

Pia Dandiya

Pia Dandiya, a former high school principal, is the Democratic candidate from Florida’s 22nd Congressional District and faces Republican Casey Askar.

A first-generation American, Ms. Dandiya has built her campaign around education and affordability. Born and raised in Palm Beach County, she began her career as a teacher before becoming a high school principal in Harlem.

She later founded a high school aimed at improving opportunities for low-income students. According to her campaign, every graduate of the school secured admission to college despite a large majority coming from low-income households.

Amish Shah

Amish Shah, a physician and former State Representative, is the Democratic candidate from Arizona’s 1st Congressional District. He is contesting against Republican candidate Jay Feely, a former National Football League kicker endorsed by President Donald Trump.

Mr. Shah served three terms in the Arizona House of Representatives. He narrowly lost the 2024 congressional election to Republican David Schweikert.

The Cook Political Report has classified Arizona’s 1st Congressional District as “Lean Democratic”, making the contest one of the closely watched races of the election cycle.

World.title: Stage set for polling in 92 urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh | LIVE
World.content:
After days of hectic political activity and violent incidents during the filing of nominations, the stage is set for elections to 92 urban local bodies (ULBs) in Andhra Pradesh on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The elections will be held in 13 Municipal Corporations and 79 of the 87 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.

Also Read: Arrangements in place for polling in 222 wards across NTR districts

Elections in eight Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats — Allagadda, Dachepalli, Darsi, Gurajala, Kamalapuram, Piduguralla, Proddatur and Rayachoti — were unanimous, with both chairpersons and ward members elected unopposed.

District Collector G. Lakshmisha said that comprehensive arrangements were made to ensure the peaceful and successful conduct of elections within the limits of Vijayawada Municipal Corporation(VMC) and four municipalities in the NTR district.

Mr. Lakshmisha, District Election Expenditure Observer B. Vijay Kumar and VMC Commissioner Dhyanachandra H.M. visited the distribution centre at Loyola College in Vijayawada on Saturday (October 31). They inspected the election materials and various forms being supplied to polling teams.

World.title: Morning Digest: INDIA bloc to hold ‘Chalo Dilli’ march against CEC, SIR today; Britain open to apologising for slavery, says U.K. PM; and more
World.content:
INDIA bloc holds symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on six charges

The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands .They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

Britain open to apologising for slavery, says U.K. PM Andy Burnham

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations. Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past, including in India.

At CEC’s ‘public impeachment’, voters question deletion of names from rolls

The Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance’s symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31, 2026) featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. Among them was Anita Jaiswal, who moved from Kolkata to Delhi. She said she had voted in every election between 2012 and 2025 but was now being asked to establish her citizenship.

Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s arrangements to leave Brazil after his election loss. Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after a court ordered his passports be seized amid multiple investigations against him.

Centre releases additional instalment of tax devolution of ₹1.09 lakh crore to states

The Centre on Saturday (October 31, 2026) released an additional instalment of tax devolution to state governments totalling over ₹1.09 lakh crore. This is in addition to the regular monthly devolution and the second additional instalment this financial year. The Union government released tax devolution of ₹1,09,019 crore to state governments, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

‘Make Rahul Gandhi a mock PM’: BJP slams INDIA bloc over mock Parliament

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) accused the Congress and its allies of ridiculing democratic institutions by staging a mock Parliament session, and said that Opposition parties had repeatedly disrupted proceedings in the real Parliament. At a press conference, BJP MP Sambit Patra referred to the structure resembling the old Parliament building erected for the mock Parliament session and said: “They want to retain everything from the old British-era structure... They should seat Rahul Gandhi ji as the mock Prime Minister in that very old structure. We have absolutely no objection.”

Rahul Gandhi appeals to Delhi rally goers to do festival shopping from local traders

Amid concerns of traders in central Delhi over the impact of the crowd expected at the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally on Sunday (November 1, 2026), Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) urged people to do some festival season shopping after attending the rally. In a video released late in the day, Mr. Gandhi appealed to people to shop for upcoming festivals like Deepavali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj.

Mamdani says Trump has agreed to grant visa to mother of Ghanian teen killed in Bronx shooting

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has claimed in a social media post that President Donald Trump has agreed to grant a visa to the mother of a 15-year-old immigrant from Ghana who was shot dead earlier this week. The teen, Javits Frimpong, was on his way to school in a Bronx neighbourhood shortly before 9.30 a.m. on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when he was shot in the abdomen, New York City police said.

London police arrest 139 people outside U.S. Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group

London police said they arrested 139 people at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in support of the banned group Palestine Action. The majority of those taken into custody had expressed support for a proscribed organisation, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement. It said that more arrests are expected as officers remain at the scene.

Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion

Foreign Ministers from the United States, India, Japan and Australia on Saturday (October 31, 2026) jointly raised serious concerns about “economic coercion” like export curbs and practices leading to overproduction, in veiled criticism of China. “The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions,” said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday (October 31, 2026) said the market regulator is monitoring developments relating to governance at the holding company level in the Tata Group, and pointed out that the group’s listed companies and their promoters are subject to SEBI’s disclosure and compliance norms.

Indian women’s cricket in a healthy state: Muzumdar
